title: SEN / SEND Tutor, Somerset / Bristol
description:
You can make a difference, be rewarded, and join our impact-driven community now - at Targeted Provision we change lives!

In order to make an application, simply read through the following job description and make sure to attach relevant documents.

Multiple positions are available, hiring is ongoing, and interviews are being arranged as applications come in. We will contact you with nearby tutoring work within 45 minutes drive of the advertised location and/or within 45 minutes of the postcode you provide us.

What Makes This Role Right For You

We are working with Schools and Local Authorities in your area and are looking for Core Subject (Maths, English, or Science) SEND Tutors and Teachers like you to transform the lives of Young People with SEND and SEMH needs in your community!

We are looking for SEND Tutors and Teachers with a genuine passion for transforming the lives of disengaged, at-risk, and vulnerable learners – take control of your teaching journey with us and work flexibly, creatively, and in a trauma-informed way to make a difference in your own life and the lives of the young people we support.

The Benefits We Offer Our SEND Tutor And Teachers

- Competitive pay: £28 - £35 per hour
- Flexible working: In person, hybrid, and work from home teaching opportunities
- Flexible hours: Flexible part-time up to full-time hours to suit your schedule
- CPD and employee mentoring: TES CPD suite and professional mentor access
- SEND Support Team: Support to keep a team around you and the child
- Community and Company Events: Knowledge sharing and resources
- Referral Programme: Get rewarded for successful tutor referrals
- A Role with Purpose: Join a child-centred company committed to reimagining the world of support for vulnerable young people for the better

SEND Tutor And Teacher Role Requirements

- Experience: 2+ years teaching experience, ideally working with SEND, SEMH, MLD, SLD, and/or PMLD in a holistic and trauma-informed way
- Subjects: Familiarity teaching English, Maths, and/or Science
- Qualifications: Qualified Teacher Status (QTS / QTLS)
- Compliance: Enhanced DBS (we can facilitate this if needed) and 2+ professional references
- Location: You must be based in the UK with the right to work in the UK, even for remote / online jobs
- Safeguarding: Knowledge of safeguarding and creating a safe learning environment

The SEND Tutor And Teacher Role And Responsibilities

- Provide in person, online / remote, and hybridMaths, English, or Science tuition to children, teenagers, and young people with SEMH and SEND needs, including MLD, SLD, PMLD, and other Additional Educational Needs
- Support pupils and students, ranging from KS1 - KS5 (as appropriate for your skills), referred by local authorities and schools by planning and delivering flexible, trauma-informed tutoring and mentoring
- Plan and report for lessons and provide regular feedback on student progress
- We are on a mission to raise the standard of education provided to young people with SEND (Special Education Needs and Disabilities), as well as other needs such as SEMH needs (Social, Emotional and Mental Health). We are increasingly supporting children and young people with MLD (Moderate Learning Difficulties), SLD (Severe Learning Difficulties), and PMLD (Profound and Multiple Learning Difficulties). We want you as part of our mission!

Applying

- Apply in less than 5 minutes via our mobile and browser optimised application form
- Interviews are being scheduled on a rolling basis - apply now and start making a difference!
- We welcome tutors from all backgrounds - our learners come from diverse communities and our organisation must reflect and represent their experiences
- We take Safer Recruitment seriously. All candidates must pass through our safer recruitment process to ensure their suitability to work with children and young people

SEND Tutor And Teacher Employment Status

- This position involves engaging with us on a self-employed basis, as and when opportunities arise

Relevant Job Titles / Previous Experience

Individuals with highly relevant experience from teaching background often have worked in the following roles:

- SENDCo (Special Education Needs Coordinator)
- SLD / MLD Teacher
- Autism / ADHD Support Teacher
- Intervention Specialist / Teacher / Tutor
- Ex-Teacher

Other highly relevant roles from therapeutic and learning support background include:

- Learning Support Assistant (LSA) / Teaching Assistant (TA)
- Educational Therapist
- Speech and Language Therapist (SALT)
- Educational Psychologist (EP)
- Inclusion Coordinator

If you hold one of these roles, meet our requirements, and are considering a career change please do consider applying with us.

Due to the number of applications we receive, we are unable to respond to every applicant. We aim to respond to all successful applicants.

title: Healthcare Practitioner - Nurse, UK
description:
Description & Requirements

Job Position - WCA Registered Nurse - Hybrid

Location - Newport

Salary - £39500

Permanent Mon to Friday 9am to 5pm - Hybrid

Working Full and Part time available

Be part of something great Maximus is a global organisation that specialises in providing health and employment services to millions of people every year. Here in the UK we employ around 5,000 people across the country to deliver services that have a profound impact on people’s lives. From assessments and health services to employability programmes and specialist support, we do work that matters with people who care. The role is necessary to carry out clinical reviews and provide case managers with advice in relation to complaints and enquiries in connection with PIP referrals. Complaints and enquiries can come from customers, representatives (including welfare rights groups & MPs), as well as DWP. Part of the role is also to provide outcomes and feedback on all complaints about healthcare professionals that is used as part of professional development and improvement in addition to being utilised to make overall business improvements.

Do good. Be great as a nurse.

Are you a Registered Nurse, Nurse Practitioner or Registered Mental Health Nurse seeking professional growth, flexible working and a better work-life balance?

About The Role

As a Nurse Functional Assessor at Maximus, you'll use your clinical expertise to understand how a person's disability or health condition affects their daily life. You’ll work on complex cases involving physical and mental health conditions and chronic pain disorders, while your compassion and experience helps customers move forward with their lives.

The role can be both challenging and rewarding, which is why we provide a tailored training programme* to help you thrive. You'll begin with formal training before assessing customers and have ongoing support and mentorship in your role with us.

Duties And Responsibilities

Conduct telephone, video or face-to-face assessments to understand how a person's disability or health condition affects their daily life

Produce Work Capability Assessment (WCA) reports to help the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) determine a person’s eligibility for benefits

Develop your clinical knowledge and assessment skills with the support of regular feedback and supervision

Requirements

Valid NMC registration number

At least 1 year of broad post-registration adult or mental health experience gained within or outside of the NHS

You MUST have the right to work in the UK – we cannot offer sponsorships

Excellent oral and written communication skills

Comfortable using computer software to type and produce detailed reports

What We Offer

£39,500 salary

Flexible working – full-time, part-time and hybrid

No bank holidays, evenings or weekends

Leading maternity and paternity paid leave

Bank holidays plus 25 days’ holiday with the option to buy or sell 5 days

Ongoing CPD, clinical development and reimbursed validation fees

£2,000 for referring a friend

Life insurance and Medicash Healthcare Cash Plan

Join us and become part of a team that's making a real difference to people’s lives.

We know that feeling included has a dramatic impact on personal wellbeing and are working to ensure that no job applicant receives less favourable treatment due to any personal characteristic. Advertisements for posts will include sufficiently clear and accurate information to enable potential applicants to assess their own suitability for the post.
- We are a Disability Confident Leader, thanks to our commitment to the recruitment, retention and career development of people with disabilities and long-term conditions. The Disability Confident scheme includes a guaranteed interview for any applicant with a disability who meets the minimum requirements for a job. When you complete your job application you will find a question asking you if you would like to apply under the Disability Confident Guaranteed Interview Scheme. If you feel that you have a disability and apply under this scheme, providing that you meet the essential criteria for the job, you will then be invited for interview. Your Guaranteed Interview application will only be shared with the hiring manager and the local resourcing team.
- Where reasonable, MAXIMUS will review and consider adjustments for those applicants who express a requirement for them during the recruitment process.

title: Warehouse Supervisor
description:
Company Description

Do you enjoy leading a team to hit delivery targets? Are you skilled at turning warehouse challenges into simple, safe processes? Would you like to develop your career in a busy, people-first distribution team?

We are looking for a Warehouse Supervisor to join our Glasgow Hub, Working a Monday to Friday, 10:30 - 19:00.

Rexel UK is a global leader in the distribution of electrical and energy-efficient products and services. Our mission is to deliver smart electrical solutions that enhance the comfort, safety, and security of homes, businesses, and industries.

The Benefits Of a Career With Rexel

- Support & Development: Extensive learning opportunities from day one
- Health & Wellbeing: Free virtual GP service, Healthy Mind Champions, and more!
- Perks: Contributory pension scheme and life assurance, Staff discounts, exclusive holiday offers and free financial support and education

Job Description

As a Warehouse Supervisor, You will be supporting the Hub Manager, by taking ownership of the team, ensuring that operational targets and SLA's are met, site Health & Safety is upheld and any team escalations are dealt with.

You will supervise about 5-6 operatives across Warehouse operation, so ideally, you will have team lead or supervision experience from a Logistics/Distribution background, Have great stock management knowledge and able to effectively communicate across different stakeholders.

Role Responsibilities

- Supervising and supporting a team of operatives to deliver daily KPI’s,
- Allocating workload, managing priorities and coordinating cover to meet dispatch deadlines,
- Monitoring accuracy and quality, reducing picking errors and ensuring orders are packed correctly,
- Coaching team members on processes, safe working and best practice to improve performance,
- Ensuring goods are handled, stored and packed to prevent damage and maintain stock integrity,
- Maintaining warehouse Heath & Safety standards/Requirements & housekeeping,
- Using warehouse systems/scanners to track work and maintain traceability (where applicable),
- Communicating with internal stakeholders (e.g., customer service/transport/branch teams) to resolve issues quickly,
- Communicating with external stakeholders such as Customers, Suppliers and External agency support.

Qualifications

At Rexel, we prioritise hiring individuals based on behaviours and potential, rather than requiring specific formal qualifications for roles, the behaviours that will set you up for success as an Warehouse Supervisor colleague include:

COLLABORATION: Building partnerships and working collaboratively with others to achieve shared objectives

TAKES ACCOUNTABILITY: Taking action, overcoming obstacles, and meeting commitments

CUSTOMER FOCUS: building strong customer relationships and delivering customer-centric solutions

What We Are Looking For

- Proven background and knowledge of warehouse operations ideally in a supervisory position
- Great communication skills across all different levels
- Good Warehouse & Logistics Health & Safety knowledge
- Proficiency with IT systems

Additional Information

At Rexel UK, we’re all about welcoming people from different backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives because we know that diversity drives fresh ideas and great results.

By coming together as one team, we’re building a high-performance culture that not only drives success but also creates real value for our customers and communities.

Creating an environment where individuality is celebrated and creativity flourishes, we're making sure everyone feels supported and confident to be their best.

title: Customer Service Advisor
description:
Full-time | Remote Working | Site travel | Permanent employment

- Coventry
- Full-time
- Permanent

About Elis

About a career with Elis

Elis is an international leader in textile, hygiene and facility services, helping businesses across a wide range of industries to operate safely, sustainably and efficiently. With a presence in 29 countries and a team of around 52,000 people, we combine the scale and stability of an international organisation with the opportunity to build a rewarding and long-term career.

Our people are at the heart of everything we do. We believe in investing in our people, recognising their contribution and giving them the opportunity to develop, progress and build careers they can be proud of.

At Elis, you'll be part of a culture built on trust, respect and collaboration, where your ideas and contribution are valued. We want our people to have a voice, and our commitment to listening and acting on employee feedback was recognised when Elis UK won Best Employee Engagement Experience Initiative at the 2024 CIPD People Management Awards for our Employee Voice programme.

With opportunities across operations, engineering, logistics, sales and our head office support functions, there are many ways to develop your career with Elis.

The Opportunity

We are looking for a Customer Service Advisor to join our team at our Coventry site.

This is a varied, customer-focused role where you'll play an important part in delivering an excellent experience for our customers, building strong relationships and ensuring queries or issues are resolved effectively.

This isn't purely a desk-based customer service position. You'll work across both the office and out in the field, meeting customers face-to-face and working closely with colleagues across our service teams. You'll support with everything from resolving customer queries and complaints through to site visits, product fittings, stock checks and helping customers get the best from the services we provide.

What You'll Be Doing

Responsibilities

You'll take ownership of the customer experience and act as an important link between our customers and our operational teams. Your responsibilities will include:

- Managing and following up customer queries promptly and professionally, working with both internal teams and customers.
- Taking ownership of customer complaints, including attending customer locations where required to help achieve a positive resolution.
- Coordinating solutions and following up with customers to ensure issues have been resolved effectively.
- Building strong relationships with customers and understanding their individual service requirements.
- Providing customers with guidance and education on the services and products available to them.
- Supporting customer renegotiations where required.
- Carrying out employee garment sizing and fittings at customer locations.
- Completing rental stock checks and supporting locker installations and clear-outs.
- Capturing and sharing Voice of the Customer (VOC) feedback to help us continuously improve our service.
- Identifying opportunities to grow existing customer relationships in line with agreed targets.
- Working collaboratively with our service teams to deliver excellent customer outcomes and achieve shared performance targets.

What We're Looking For

We're looking for someone who genuinely enjoys working with customers and is comfortable taking ownership when something needs resolving.

You'll Ideally Bring

- Previous experience within a customer service, account management or sales-focused environment.
- A genuinely customer-centric approach.
- Strong communication and listening skills.
- Confidence dealing with customer queries and challenging situations in a calm and professional manner.
- A proactive, solution-focused approach to problem solving.
- Strong organisation and planning skills.
- The ability to manage multiple priorities effectively.
- A self-motivated approach and willingness to take ownership.
- A willingness to learn and develop your skills.
- A full driving licence, as the role involves visiting customer locations.

What We Offer

As part of Elis, you'll join a supportive and established international business where your contribution is valued.

We Offer

- A competitive salary
- Training and ongoing development
- Opportunities to progress your career within Elis
- The stability and opportunities that come with being part of an international organisation
- A supportive working environment where your ideas and contribution matter
- 29 Days Holiday
- Car Allowance
- Company Pension

Interested?

Then apply online!

title: Jumper / Materials Handler
description:
Job Description

About the Business

ITW Construction – Offsite Europe is a business unit of ITW within in the Construction Products segment, a segment which generates $1.9 billion in global revenue. The Offsite Europe business’ annual revenue is $40 million, with 80+ colleagues across the UK & Ireland. We are suppliers of innovative engineered connectors and design software, and our products are uniquely capable of driving value for our customers, supported by strong customer service capabilities and a continuous improvement mindset.

ITW Construction – Offsite Europe are consistently innovating, designing and manufacturing advanced industrial technology. We are industry influencers with 2 high-quality brands that are known throughout the industry, and we aspire to grow our business in our current markets as well as explore new market opportunities. At all levels in our organisation, we are encouraged to embrace our inner entrepreneur to drive actions, focus on what matters and share ideas so that every individual can have an impact on the business. In return we are rewarded, supported in our development and given the opportunities to grow within a large multinational organisation.

Role

Working as part of the production and wider operations team within the Glenrothes site, the Jumper role is responsible ensuring all production machinery is ready for use by the operations team. The role must ensure all daily targets are met, whilst following all internal safety and quality procedures. The role is responsible for the general upkeep of all raw materials (steel coils) involved in production and the management of the waste circuits (including scrap). The Jumper also provides key shift support in the absence of the Shift Supervisor

Responsibilities

- Operate forklift trucks for the removal of finished product into the warehouse where required.
- Ensure the power presses are replenished as required during production with all consumables.
- Material handling - loading and unloading of steel coils up to 6.5 tonnes.
- Unloading the raw materials (steel coils) into the Kanban locations using 10-tonne overhead crane and ensuring all paperwork is filled in.
- Inspection and quality control of manufactured components and incoming goods.
- Assembling/packing parts ready for dispatch.
- Organising the pick-up and delivery of any waste removal and/or raw material deliveries.
- Operate power press if required during breaks, holiday periods and/or lunch times.
- Shift Supervisor and Production Manager with the achievement of production plans.
- Shift Supervisor and Production Manager with the Kanban approach (MRD), with a focus on raw materials.
- Responsible for opening and closing the site facility where required.
- Working with the production team, to schedule in and manage steel deliveries.
- Physical stock counting of steel and raw materials at the end of each shift.
- Involvement in progress activities and driving improvements and efficiencies where possible.
- Any other reasonable and relevant duties as and when required.

Health & Safety

- Ensure a high standard of housekeeping is maintained in your working area (6S)
- Completing safety checks on all equipment as required
- Actively participate in Focus Groups and other safety initiatives
- Ensure all guarding and safety equipment is in place and used when needed
- Report all health and safety or maintenance issues
- Ensure health and safety requirements are met and understand all relevant safety regulations

Experience/Skills/Attributes

Job Requirements:

- Forklift driving – up to 7-tonne truck.
- Overhead crane experience.
- The ability to work well under pressure.
- Effective communication skills.
- Motivated individual who is flexible and willing to learn continuous best practice.
- Ability to demonstrate initiative and positive attitude.
- Excellent organizational, time management and attention to detail skills
- Comfortable in being able work alone and/or within a team environment, contributing and sharing best practices, resources and ideas in order to continually improve.
- The ability to work to set standards and procedures.

title: Customer Service Representative UK & IE
description:
Who We Are

At Brooks, we believe movement is the key to feeling more alive. That’s why we’re driven to create gear and experiences that take people to the place that makes them feel more alive — whether it’s a headspace, a feeling, or a finish line.

Everyone who works at Brooks is propelled by a company culture that sparks excitement, fuels collaboration, inspires creativity, and ignites innovation.

Our brand values help bond us together and drive our success:

- Runner First

We act in the best interest of the runner

- Word is Bond

We do what we say we’ll do

- Champion Heart

We give our all in everything we do

- There is no “I” in Run

We stay generous with our humanity

- Keep Moving

We find ways to move every day, because joy is kinetic!

We welcome everyone from every walk of life looking to inspire others through the power of movement — because we’re all moving towards something. Let’s run there

Your Job

The Customer Service Representative will be the frontline contact for Brooks retailers in UK & Ireland. You will be responsible for upholding the established standards of customer service excellence set by the Brooks Customer Service team whilst always looking for opportunities to excel. The Customer Service team meets the needs of our retailers by building strong relationships and supporting them through order processing, tracking, and reviewing performance against set KPI’s as well as providing product explanations. Customer Service also communicates daily with Finance, Sales, Operations and Marketing, being an important line of communication for colleagues on the road.

Your Responsibilities

- Customer Order Tracking and Sales Co - ordination
- Respond to Sales Reps/accounts within 24 hours of initial inquiry and interact with customers in a professional, friendly, helpful manner via various contact channels (including social media, chat, text).
- Enter and maintain Future Orders through different systems and ensure timely and accurately shipment in accordance with our operations & logistics protocols (Booking-in).
- Track orders to provide estimated delivery times, and work with Operations team or DC to re-arrange deliveries as needed.
- Communicate an account’s shipping and packing requirements to the warehouse.
- Place fill in orders as well as provide information on inventory availability to accounts and sales reps.
- Proactively communicate with Sales Reps or Sales Management regarding order amendments and cancellations.
- Issue RA numbers and defective credits as needed within 5 working days.

Create and maintain customer database, answer inquiries/troubleshoot

- Create new customer accounts.
- Communicate changes for an account to the appropriate party(s); i.e., billing or shipping address as changed, new phone number or email address or create complete new customer accounts if required.
- Provide accounts with information on our apparel and footwear lines to help customers determine which product is best for them.
- Deal with enquiries for B2B & B2C orders.
- Maintain an organize and up-to-date filing system for accounts orders and correspondence that can be easily accessed by others when needed.
- Provide copy invoices/order confirmations/dispatch notes as needed.
- Process returns and issue credits when necessary.
- Work with finance to resolve invoicing issues. Fill out credit memos/debit as needed.
- Process returns and issue credits when necessary.

Other

- Complete reports as provided by sales and management.
- Provide Sales and Marketing Support as needed.
- Other duties as assigned.
- Maintain an activity log of all customer touch points.

Your Qualifications

-
- Successfully completed sixth form college level (or equivalent).
- Customer service experience preferred but not essential as full training will be given.
- Computer proficiency: Excel, Word, Outlook.
- Native in English, demonstrating effective listening through concise, clear verbal and written communication.
- Keen attention to detail in planning, organization and execution of tasks, ability to manage conflicting priorities on a daily basis.
- Demonstration of innovation and initiative – always looking at improving our products and processes while also displaying a willingness to dive into the details and help out wherever necessary.
- Proven ability to work effectively with retailers and consumers.
- Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to deal with adverse situations positively.
- Ability to interact effectively and professionally with all levels of the organization.
- Excellent interpersonal skills that inspire and build trust resulting in effective working relationships across the company, and with retailers and consumers.
- Passionate participation in Brooks’ sports activities a plus, overridden by the ability to understand and empathize with the runner in order to develop loyal, engaging relationships with our customers and the Brooks community.
- Unwavering demonstration of Brooks’ corporate values: Runner First, Word is Bond, Champion Heart, There is no “I” in Run, and Keep Moving!

title: Principal Electrical Engineer
description:
Join Our Team as a Principal Electrical Engineer working with Wastewater Treatment Works (STW) & Bioresources!

At Severn Trent, our people are at the heart of everything we do. We’re in the top 5% of utility companies worldwide for employee engagement, and we’re equally proud of our strong Glassdoor score — reflecting how much our people love working here.

Join us to make a positive impact on the environment and our communities, while being valued and supported in a truly inclusive workplace.

If you want to do more, because you care, we want you on our team.

EVERYTHING YOU NEED TO KNOW

Severn Trent Water is seeking an experienced and motivated Principal Electrical Engineer to join our Engineering and Design team.

This is a permanent position based at our Raynesway office in Derby.

You will be responsible for leading the electrical design and technical delivery of major wastewater treatment projects. The successful candidate will provide technical leadership across the project lifecycle, from feasibility and outline design through to detailed design, construction support, commissioning and handover.

Working within multidisciplinary teams, you will ensure designs are safe, efficient, sustainable, and aligned with Severn Trent's operational requirements and engineering standards.

LET’S TELL YOU MORE

Electrical Engineering Leadership

- Lead the development and delivery of electrical engineering solutions for wastewater treatment and bioresources projects.
- Act as the electrical engineering technical authority on assigned projects.
- Provide technical leadership, mentoring, and support to engineers and designers.
- Promote engineering excellence, innovation, and best practice throughout project delivery.
- Provide electrical expertise to develop standards

Outline & Detailed Design

- Develop electrical solutions for:
- Wastewater Treatment Works (STW)
- Bioresources

- Progress designs through concept, outline, and detailed design stages.
- Ensure designs meet project objectives, regulatory requirements, budget constraints, and operational needs.

Design Coordination

- Collaborate with Process, Civil, Structural, Mechanical, ICA, and Operations teams.
- Ensure electrical designs integrate effectively with treatment processes and operational requirements.
- Support multidisciplinary design reviews, ALM, HAZOP studies, constructability reviews, and value engineering workshops.
- Resolve technical interfaces and design challenges throughout project development.

Technical Assurance & Governance

- Undertake and coordinate electrical design reviews and approvals.
- Ensure compliance with:
- Relevant British Standards and Eurocodes
- Health and Safety legislation
- Water industry standards and guidance
- Severn Trent engineering standards

- Support engineering assurance and risk management activities.

Construction & Commissioning Support

- Provide technical support during construction, installation, testing, and commissioning phases.
- Assist contractors and suppliers in resolving technical queries.
- Support project handover and operational integration.

What You’ll Bring To The Role

- Degree in Electrical Engineering or a related discipline.
- Chartered Engineer (CEng) status, or demonstrable progress towards chartership.
- Ample experience within utilities projects.
- Strong knowledge of UK water and wastewater treatment processes, assets and standards.
- Proven experience delivering outline and detailed electrical design for complex infrastructure projects.
- Experience leading multidisciplinary engineering teams.
- Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.

Of course, it’s important that we attract the right skill sets and those with the right experience but we value character, positivity and a caring attitude in equal weight.

We do more, because we care.

We want people who show up and get involved. Those who are ready to be part of something bigger and who want to make a difference because they care. Is that you?

What’s In It For You

Working here isn’t just a job. You can build a career at Severn Trent. We’ll reward you for it, too. We have a range of benefits that recognise great work and award-winning training to help you reach your potential.

Here are just some of our favourite's perks that you’ll get being part of the Seven Trent family:

- 28 days holiday + bank holidays (and the ability to buy/ sell up to 5 days per year)
- Annual bonus scheme (of up to £2,250, which is subject to eligibility)
- Leading pension scheme – we will double your contribution (up to 15% when you contribute 7.5%)
- Sharesave – the chance to buy Severn Trent Plc shares at a discounted rate
- Dedicated training and development with our Academy
- Electric vehicle scheme and retail offers
- Family friendly policies
- Two paid volunteering days per year

WHATS NEXT?

We can’t wait to hear from you.

Before you apply, you’ll need an updated copy of your CV and about five minutes to spare. We’ll always let you know the outcome of your application after the closing date - so keep an eye on your phone and emails!

And if your curiosity has peaked and you're wanting to find out even more, search on social media.

title: Nursery Early Years Practitioner
description:
A place where children thrive. A career where you can too.

There aren't many careers where the moments you create today can shape a child's future.

You could be there for a child's first friendship, their growing confidence, or the discovery that sparks a lifelong love of learning. You might help a child solve a problem, ask their hundredth question, or achieve something they've spent weeks trying to master.

That's the impact of Early Years education.

At our YMCA Newport Nursery, we're looking for warm, patient, curious and caring people who want to help children learn, grow and thrive through play-based learning.

Whether you're an experienced Early Years Practitioner, hold a Level 2 or Level 3 Childcare qualification, are working towards one, or are considering a career change, we'd love to hear from you.

Because while qualifications matter, the person behind them matters even more.

A working week with more room for life

Our full-time Early Years Practitioners work 40 hours across four days, giving you:

4 working days, 3 days off every week.

More time for family, friends, hobbies and life outside work. Part-time and job-share opportunities may also be available.

Welcome to YMCA Fairthorne Group Newport Nursery

Newport Nursery is a welcoming setting where children are supported to explore, grow in confidence, and enjoy a strong start to early learning.

Based at St Mary's Hospital, the nursery offers a calm and convenient location for families across the island and is especially well placed for hospital staff.

Children benefit from fresh meals, outdoor play, and a strong school readiness focus, while breakout spaces and quieter areas help us support individual needs in a nurturing way.

Newport feels warm, supportive, and well connected, giving families a setting where children can feel settled, secure, and ready for the next stage.

We want children to feel secure enough to explore, confident enough to try and supported enough to develop at their own pace.

A place to play, learn, make friends and feel that they belong.

Children learn best when they're actively engaged, curious and having fun. Learning might look like:

- exploring nature outdoors
- building, creating and problem-solving
- investigating how things work
- storytelling, role play and imaginative play
- developing independence, resilience and social skills

Sometimes the best learning starts with a carefully planned activity. Sometimes it starts with a cardboard box. Both can be equally valuable.

As an Early Years Practitioner, you'll:

- build warm and secure relationships with children
- help every child feel that they belong
- support children's confidence, independence and emotional development
- create engaging opportunities to learn through play
- follow children's interests and turn everyday experiences into opportunities for discovery
- support communication, language and social development
- encourage creativity, curiosity and problem-solving
- provide exciting indoor and outdoor experiences
- observe children's development and use what you learn to support what comes next
- build positive relationships with parents and carers
- support children with different needs, experiences and starting points
- work closely with colleagues and share ideas and good practice
- maintain a safe, welcoming and inclusive nursery environment
- keep children safe through excellent safeguarding and Early Years practice

While you'll work within the EYFS framework and complete observations and records, your focus will always be the children.

We welcome applications from:

- qualified Level 2 or Level 3 Early Years Practitioners
- those studying towards an Early Years qualification
- people with experience in education, SEND, youth work, healthcare, coaching, community services or care

Most importantly, we're looking for people who are caring, dependable, curious and committed to helping children grow in confidence, independence and curiosity.

If you have the right values, we can support your development through training and apprenticeship pathways.

More than your next childcare job

Joining a YMCA Fairthorne Group Nursery is more than finding your next childcare job.

It's an opportunity to shape children's earliest experiences, develop your career in Early Years education, and be part of an organisation dedicated to helping children, young people and families belong, contribute and thrive.

If you're looking for an Early Years Practitioner or Nursery Practitioner role in Newport, Isle of Wight, or you're considering your first step into childcare and Early Years education, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply today and discover where a career at YMCA Fairthorne Group could take you.

Safeguarding

YMCA Fairthorne Group is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people. Successful applicants will be required to complete appropriate safer recruitment and pre-employment checks, including an Enhanced Disclosure through the Disclosure and Barring Service.

Equality, diversity and inclusion

YMCA Fairthorne Group is committed to creating an inclusive organisation where everyone is treated fairly, with dignity and respect.

We welcome applications from people with different backgrounds, experiences and perspectives.

Requirements

We welcome applications from candidates who:

Hold a Level 2 or Level 3 Early Years qualification, are working towards one, or have relevant transferable experience

- Are caring, patient, dependable and enthusiastic about helping children thrive
- Can build positive relationships with children, parents, carers and colleagues
- Are committed to inclusive, play-based learning and outdoor experiences
- Understand the importance of safeguarding and safe Early Years practice
- Are willing to follow the EYFS framework and complete observations and records
- Can support children with different needs, experiences and starting points
- Are willing to undertake all required safer-recruitment checks, including an Enhanced DBS check

Applications are also encouraged from career changers with experience in education, SEND, youth work, healthcare, coaching, community services or care. Training and apprenticeship pathways may be available for candidates with the right values and attitude.

Up to £30,047 per annum (Dependent on experience)

Benefits

We want you to thrive at work and beyond. That's why you'll enjoy:

- Enjoy free childcare for the hours you work, with 50% discount on any additional days required
- Up to 30 days' holiday, plus bank holidays and the option to buy 10 additional days
- A celebration leave day — an extra day off to celebrate whatever matters to you
- Health Cash Plan and access to a wellbeing assistance programme
- Retail discounts, discounted gym membership and Blue Light Card eligibility
- Career development opportunities to help you learn, progress and achieve your goals
- Fantastic day-camp savings — one free week and one week at 50% off per child, every year
- Discounts at the YMCA Fairthorne Group, including camping, activities, river hire and day camps
- Cycle to Work scheme
- High-quality resources and a modern working environment
- Most importantly, a warm, caring and supportive culture where you'll feel welcomed and valued

title: Naimuri - Software Engineer
description:
Job Title: Naimuri - Software Engineer

Job Location: Salford Quays, Manchester

Job Type: Permanent, Fulltime, minimum 3 days per week on site

Job ID: 20615

We can offer you the chance to help make the UK a safer place through innovation, working in partnership with government, defence, and law enforcement organisations on some of the most challenging data and technology problems out there.

We strongly encourage candidates of all different backgrounds and identities to apply. We are committed to building an inclusive, safe and supportive environment that allows everyone to do their best work. We are happy to support any accessibility or neurodiversity requirements that you may need during the recruitment process.

About us:

We’ve been around for about ten years and grown from being a little-known tech start-up to creating our own community at the heart of the thriving and diverse tech and digital ecosystem of Greater Manchester.

Our name Naimuri is Japanese and simply means…

‘nai’ meaning ‘not’

‘muri’ meaning ‘overburden’

These principles apply to every aspect of an organisation from technology, process and infrastructure, through to people, culture and leadership. This means that we empower our teams to do what they think is the right thing, giving them the skills and confidence to explore new ways of working, and to create a bias-free environment, where all our people feel comfortable collaborating to deliver the finest ideas and solutions in an agile environment.

Our business is focused on 4 cornerstones, which shape and underpin the way in which we go about work and treat each other. These are: Wellbeing, Empowerment, Perpetual Edge and Delivery.

People and culture are at the heart of Naimuri, so that collectively, we can realise our mission of ‘making the UK a safer place to be’.

About the role:

We are seeking a talented and passionate Full Stack Software Engineer to join either a software delivery team which is already supporting, or about to start supporting projects initially within the Defence sector, but with opportunities to work in other sectors in the future.

What You'll Do:

- Support the development of application functionality and features.
- Write clean, well-documented, and testable code, adhering to best practices and coding standards.
- Implement and maintain unit, integration, and end-to-end tests to ensure application quality and reliability.
- Participate in code reviews, providing constructive feedback and ensuring code quality.
- Stay up-to-date with the latest technologies, frameworks, and best practices.
- Contribute to the continuous improvement of our development processes and tools.

We’re looking for someone with :

- Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
- Proven professional experience as a Software Engineer or similar role (2+ years.)
- Previous demonstrable experience in delivery through Agile methodologies.
- Experience with JavaScript (ES6+), TypeScript.
- Experience of full stack development.
- Proficiency with version control systems (e.g., Git).
- Awareness of software development best practices, including testing, debugging, and performance optimization.
- Excellent problem-solving skills and attention to detail.
- Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively in a team environment.

It would be advantageous if you also had :

- Prior experience working in the Defence domain.
- Awareness of Secure by Design (SbD) principles (ie/ JSP 440/604).
- Familiarity with AWS.
- Knowledge of accessibility standards (WCAG).
- Experience with React.
- Experience with Express.
- Experience with the Elastic stack.
- Experience with graph databases.
- Experience of e2e testing using Cypress or Playwright.
- Experience with CI/CD pipelines.
- Experience with Kubernetes and Docker.

Location:

Our Head Office is based in Salford Quays, Manchester, with satellite offices in London and Cheltenham. We offer hybrid working where you can work from home for part of your working week with time on site being based on the needs of your assigned delivery and agreed Ways of Working for your team. We would expect that the successful candidate would be working an average of 3 days a week in the office or customer site.

Pay and benefits:

Naimuri pays competitively within the industry based on your role's base location rates. The salary for this position is dependent upon your experience. We assess seniority relative to the team at Naimuri during the interviewing process.

A full time working week is 37.5 hours and you have flexibility over when you give that time.

Benefits include:

- Flexible/Hybrid working options
- A company performance related bonus
- Pension matched 1.5x up to 10.5%
- AXA group 1 medical cover
- Personal training budget
- Holiday buy-back scheme
- A flexible benefits scheme

Recruitment Process:

We want to ensure that you feel comfortable and confident when interviewing with us. To help you prepare, our recruitment team will discuss the process in more detail with you when you apply.

We are happy to support any accessibility or neurodiversity requirements.

title: Noise Aerothermal Engineer
description:
Job Description

Noise Aerothermal Engineer

Full Time

Derby

Why join Rolls-Royce?

At Rolls-Royce we are proud to be a business that has truly helped to shape the modern world and are committed to always being a force for progress; powering, protecting and connecting people everywhere.

By joining Rolls-Royce, you'll have the opportunity to work on world-class solutions, supported by a culture that believes individuality is our greatest strength, and all perspectives, experiences and backgrounds help us innovate and enable our high-performance culture.

A Noise Engineer is responsible for all aspects of engine noise to support Rolls-Royce's Civil Aerospace businesses. Activities encompass the acoustic prediction of components for future engines and in-service products within the engine and nacelle. It includes verification and validation of engine and component designs via analysis and rig or engine testing, and support of Aircraft Certification of future and in-service products via static and flight noise testing.

The role also includes the definition and execution of technology acquisition programmes to deliver novel technology and concepts for noise reduction. In pursuing this work, you will work closely with various engineering functions, suppliers, marketing and airframe companies in order to meet technically challenging requirements, within demanding timescales.

This is an exciting and challenging role ideal for an individual seeking to further their Acoustics career by gaining real product development experience and influencing the future of aerospace.

Responsibilities

- The provision of component design advice to meet noise requirements
- The estimation of the noise performance of new or in-service engines, often to short timescales and to commercial guarantee or certification standards
- Liaison with programme leadership, internal supply chain units, external customers, partners and suppliers, representing Noise Engineering
- The management of experimental activities, including the acquisition and appraisal of relevant rig & engine acoustic data
- The execution and leadership of research and technology programmes aimed at generating low noise technology
- Working with partners and academia to contribute to the Noise Capability strategy and create and develop new method

Qualifications And Skills Required

- MEng in Mechanical, Aeronautical Engineering or relevant Science or Maths degree
- To be able to contribute from day one previous aeroacoustics, gas turbine cycle design experience, aero-thermal or aerodynamics technical experience is required
- Previous experience in Gas Turbine full Engine or rig testing and analysis is highly desirable.
- An ability to apply logical and analytical thinking on a range of technical problems and be able to communicate ideas effectively
- Proactive, persistent and customer focused with a high level of self-motivation and initiative.
- Strong Project management and planning skills - capable of responding quickly to urgent requests from customers in addition to longer term planning and technical activities
- Effective interpersonal & communication skills essential for liaising with and influencing Airframe customers, Project leadership and the large number of interfaces that exist with this role

Regional Benefits

- Generous Annual Leave
- Retirement Savings through the Rolls Royce Retirement Savings Trust

title: SEN / SEND Tutor, Gloucestershire
description:
You can make a difference, be rewarded, and join our impact-driven community now - at Targeted Provision we change lives!

What Makes This Role Right For You

We are working with Schools and Local Authorities in your area and are looking for Core Subject (Maths, English, or Science) SEND Tutors and Teachers like you to transform the lives of Young People with SEND and SEMH needs in your community!

We are looking for SEND Tutors and Teachers with a genuine passion for transforming the lives of disengaged, at-risk, and vulnerable learners – take control of your teaching journey with us and work flexibly, creatively, and in a trauma-informed way to make a difference in your own life and the lives of the young people we support.

SEND Tutor And Teacher Role Requirements

title: Operational Accountant
description:
Company Description

Stobart (Part of the Culina Group) is a leading ambient transport and logistics business, providing services to many of the UK’s best known brands across core consumer and retail sectors.

At Culina we have a winning culture, we believe that our culture is one of the reasons our company continues to thrive… A place where you're valued, challenged, and inspired!

Job Description

We are seeking an Operational Accountant to join our finance team, supporting key operational and fleet functions across the business. This is a highly visible role where you'll work closely with operational leaders, providing financial insight, performance analysis, and commercial support to drive informed decision-making and continuous improvement.

This opportunity would suit a qualified, part-qualified, or qualified-by-experience accountant who enjoys partnering with stakeholders, analysing performance, and influencing business outcomes in a fast-paced environment.

Key Responsibilities

- Prepare weekly and monthly fleet profit and loss accounts, including detailed commentary and variance analysis.
- Produce regular fleet performance reports to support operational decision-making and financial control.
- Develop and enhance fleet, asset, and Repair & Maintenance (R&M) reporting, providing meaningful insights to the wider business.
- Reconcile fleet assets across multiple systems and support asset lifecycle management, including renewals and disposals.
- Deliver financial analysis and business cases to support strategic decisions relating to fleet operations and investment.
- Manage nominal ledger activities, including journals, accruals, cross-charges, and period-end reconciliations.
- Provide detailed performance analysis and trend reporting, identifying opportunities to improve profitability and operational efficiency.
- Present financial and KPI performance results to operational and senior management teams.
- Prepare balance sheet reconciliations and summaries, highlighting risks, opportunities, and key areas of focus.
- Ensure strong financial governance and controls are maintained across fleet operations.
- Lead the annual budgeting and quarterly forecasting processes in collaboration with operational stakeholders and senior leadership.
- Support audit activities and act as a key contact during internal and external audit reviews.
- Work closely with finance and operational teams to ensure accurate and timely reporting.
- Drive continuous improvement initiatives across financial reporting processes and management information.

Qualifications

- Previous experience in a Management Accountant, Operational Accountant, or Finance Business Partner role.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with a commercial mindset.
- Experience preparing management accounts, forecasts, and budgets.
- Advanced Excel skills and confidence working with large data sets.
- Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills.
- The ability to translate financial information into clear business insights.
- Strong attention to detail and a proactive approach to continuous improvement.
- Part-qualified, fully qualified, or qualified by experience (ACCA, CIMA, ACA desirable).

Additional Information

As part of our drive to make Stobart a great place to work. We are proud to be an inclusive and diverse organisation where we are committed to employee development and recognising success for hard working performers.

Our dedicated learning and development programmes are open to every employee to give you the opportunity to shape your own future within logistics and continue to work in an environment where team culture thrives.

Our People are the driving force behind our success, which is why we offer a wide range of benefits which include:

- Annual Leave – Competitive holiday entitlement of (20 days inclusive of bank holidays)
- Pension scheme – we want colleagues to enjoy a comfortable retirement so we offer a great contribution of (5)% employee and (3)% employer
- Life Assurance - x 2 your annual salary
- Wellness – Via our Employee Assistance Programme we offer immediate access to a confidential telephone counselling and legal information service that operates 24 hours a days, 365 days a year
- Eye Care Vouchers – We can provide you with substantial savings with free eye tests and discounts on prescription glasses
- Reward & Recognition – We recognise that employees have gone the extra mile via Employee of the month and year, special recognition and long service awards.
- Everyday discounts - via our benefit platform you will have access to over 50 retailer discounts for everyday savings!

If you meet the requirements for the above role and are looking for your next career opportunity please apply now and become a part of our #WinningTeam!

title: Customer Support Advisor - Split Shift
description:
About Us

Bally’s Intralot is a newly formed company established through the combination of Intralot and Bally’s International Interactive, positioning the group as a top iGaming operator and a leading global provider of lottery solutions.

Bally’s Intralot is uniquely positioned across digital online gaming markets, lottery, iLottery, and sports betting. Operating at the intersection of technology, regulation, and entertainment. We are optimally positioned to capitalise on strong global growth trends driven by digital adoption and regulatory expansion across lottery and iGaming markets.

Well, what about the team?

Our Customer Support Advisors play a pivotal role in ensuring our players receive a world-class experience at every turn. Our fun and fast-paced contact centre supports players across the UK, Ireland, Europe and a growing number of international markets, so the enquiries reaching you are as varied as the people behind them: payments and verification, betting questions, general account queries. No two conversations will ever be the same!

In the role of Customer Support Advisor, you will leverage exceptional communication skills and a high-energy approach to engage with players via email and live chat, across multiple territories and brands. You will move between markets throughout your shift, using real-time translation tools to support players in their own language. You do not need to speak a second language yourself, strong written English and the judgement to adapt your tone to different audiences matter far more. Occasional outbound calls may be required to resolve complex inquiries.

A core responsibility involves managing the LIVE KYC (Know Your Customer) process, where you will facilitate efficient player verification to ensure a seamless onboarding experience and prioritise first-contact resolution. Because verification requirements differ from one territory to the next, you will build a working knowledge of what each market expects and apply the right process first time. We are seeking a proactive problem-solver dedicated to service excellence who brings an authentic personality to every interaction, embodying our commitment to a fun and engaging workplace.

Working hours follow a rotating 5-week rota with split shifts, two working periods per day with a break off duty in between. We are looking for candidates that are available to work between 07:00 and 02:00 Monday-Sunday. The full rota is shared with candidates before phone interview stage.

Please note that the initial training period will run Monday-Friday, and will follow the schedule below:

- Weeks 1–2: 09:30–18:00
- Week 3: 12:00–20:30
- Week 4: 14:00–22:30

So, what will you be doing?

- Serving as the primary point of contact for players across our digital platforms and territories, leveraging real-time translation tools to effectively manage concurrent multilingual interactions.
- Communicating effectively and efficiently with our players via live chat and email, with occasional outbound calls to players when required.
- Switching between markets and brands as demand shifts through the day, holding the same standard of service in each one.
- Completing LIVE KYC verifications in line with the regulatory requirements of the territory the player is in.
- Keeping on top of products, promotional offerings and tools, including how these differ from market to market.
- Taking ownership and following escalations through to resolution.
- Managing tasks efficiently and on time while working to meet and exceed agreed KPIs.
- Collaborating with colleagues across all departments and locations on projects and attending relevant meetings as required.
- Striving to resolve everything, first time, every time.
- Contributing to, and promoting, a positive working environment. Becoming a role model and inspiring others.

And what will you need?

- To meet legal obligations, you must be 18 years of age or over.
- Be passionate about providing excellent customer service.
- Experience of handling Live Chat, email, and telephone queries.
- Possess exceptional verbal and written communication.
- Be comfortable supporting players from different countries and cultures and adapting your approach accordingly.
- Be able to investigate issues, solve problems, and deliver first-contact resolution.
- Able to think fast under pressure and move between markets without losing your thread.

What benefits will you get?

- 25 days annual leave, plus the bank holiday allowance.
- 35% hourly uplift for hours worked between 11.30pm-2am
- Health insurance.
- Volunteering days.
- Home office allowance.
- Wellness or Gym allowance.
- Flexi-block policy allowing you to work abroad for up to four weeks a year.
- Annual Summer and Christmas parties.

DNA / Values

At Bally’s Intralot we are driven by a set of core values that we like to call our DNA. We strive to embody our DNA and keep them at the heart of everything we do!

We Win as One, we succeed together - across every location and every function. We collaborate openly, raise each other up, and share the wins. We're Powered by Curiosity, we ask questions, challenge assumptions and make space to learn and innovate. We have Fun with Purpose, we bring creativity, energy and joy to how we work and what we deliver, because when people enjoy what they do, the work is better for everyone. Our teams Embrace the Possibility, when opportunity appears, we act. When the unexpected hits, we adapt. We don’t wait for change - we move towards it. At Bally's Intralot, we Guard the Game, we protect what matters most, fair play for our players, integrity for our partners, and accountability in everything we do.

Equal Opportunities

At Bally’s Intralot, we are committed to promoting equal opportunities in employment and working conditions. Diversity, Equity and Inclusion are important to us, and we encourage a culture where everyone can be themselves at work. We believe passionately that employing a diverse workforce is central to our success, this is our superpower.

We do not discriminate against employees or job applicants on the basis of race, colour, nationality, ethnic or national origin, age, sex or sexual orientation, gender reassignment, religion or belief, marital or civil partner status, pregnancy or maternity, political opinion or disability.

title: Software Engineer
description:
We don't just build software; we build the engine that holiday parks and resorts across Europe rely on every single day. Our platform is growing in terms of users, data, and functionality.

- Optimise existing code for performance, scalability, and maintainability

- Thoroughly test, debug, and document your technical solutions
- Actively shape architectural decisions and contribute to technical discussions
- Collaborate closely with Product, Design, and cross-functional teams in an agile environment

About You

You are an experienced Engineer who enjoys solving complex problems and understands what it takes to keep a live system running smoothly.

- A Degree (BSc or higher) in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related technical field
- 3+ years’ hands-on experience building, scaling, and maintaining live production SaaS systems
- Strong proficiency with modern web frameworks, with a solid focus on Ruby on Rails (or a similar MVC framework)
- A strong commitment to code quality, maintainability, and performance
- Excellent communication skills, with the ability to articulate and justify technical decisions within an international team
- Based in the UK and within reasonable commuting distance of our Chester office for our hybrid working model

What We Offer

- A competitive salary based on your experience.
- Annual salary reviews.
- Hybrid working opportunities

- A structured onboarding programme with a dedicated buddy.
- Access to our LMS, internal training and ongoing development opportunities.
- The opportunity to make a real impact in a growing international SaaS company.

The Hiring Process

Apply

Submit your application and tell us a bit about yourself.

Initial Review

Cem from Recruitment will get in touch within 5 working days for a quick initial chat.

First Interview

An online meeting with Thijs (Head of Engineering) to learn more about BEX, the role, and your experience.

Second Interview

A technical deep dive to explore your coding approach, problem-solving skills, and technical mindset.

Offer

If it's a great match on both sides, we'll be delighted to welcome you to BEX!

title: Client Care Advisor
description:

title: Mechanical Responsible Engineer
description:
At Amentum, we're not just solving problems; we're engineering the future. Our team is driven by an unyielding commitment to develop your career within a supportive team who always strive to do the right thing for our people, clients and communities.

People are our greatest asset, and we offer a competitive package to retain and attract the best talent.

Work-life balance and flexibility is a key focus area for us. We’re happy to discuss hybrid, part-time and flexible working hours, patterns and locations to suit you and our business. If you're passionate about making a real impact and want to be part of a community that values ethical excellence, this is the place where your ambition can thrive.

Here, we believe that success comes from continuously pushing boundaries and working together to deliver on our promises. We embrace challenges with confidence and are dedicated to creating a secure and vibrant future for all.

We’ll inspire and empower you to deliver your best work so you can evolve, grow and succeed – today and into tomorrow.

We are currently looking for a Mechanical Responsible Engineer (RE). This position may be based in Warrington, Westlakes Ind. Estate or Stockton-on-Tees.

Your role

- The Mechanical Responsible Engineer (RE) holds overall technical accountability for the mechanical and vent engineering scope within their assigned area of responsibility.
- Operating in accordance with the Sellafield Ltd Roles, Responsibilities, Accountabilities and Authorities (R2A2) for Responsible Engineer (ED21), the RE is accountable for ensuring that engineering activities, decisions, and outputs are technically correct, safe, compliant, and fit for purpose throughout the lifecycle.
- The Responsible Engineer provides technical direction and governance to the engineering team, ensures appropriate standards and assurance arrangements are applied, and retains accountability for engineering decisions, including those delegated to Lead, Principal, Senior, or Design Engineers.
- Delegation of tasks does not remove accountability from the Responsible Engineer.
- The Responsible Engineer will work closely with Project Managers, safety case owners, operations, and assurance functions to ensure engineering outcomes are safe, compliant, and fit for purpose.
- The Responsible Engineer may support multiple tasks or projects concurrently and will contribute across different stages of the engineering lifecycle, depending on project needs.

Requirements

- Significant experience delivering and governing Mechanical engineering within a regulated, safety-critical environment.
- Demonstrable experience holding technical accountability for engineering scope, including decision-making and assurance.
- Experience ensuring compliance with applicable legislation, standards, safety requirements, and organisational procedures.
- Experience establishing and maintaining appropriate engineering governance, assurance, and verification arrangements.
- Experience leading and directing multi-disciplinary engineering teams through delegated authority.
- Experience managing and resolving complex technical issues and risks.
- Experience interfacing with project management, safety case, operations, regulators, and independent assurance functions.
- Demonstrated leadership in promoting a strong safety, quality, and compliance culture.
- Degree or equivalent qualification in Mechanical engineering, or a closely related engineering discipline.
- Extensive Mechanical engineering experience commensurate with a Responsible Engineer role.
- Chartered Engineer status with a relevant professional institution (or demonstrable equivalent).
- Ability to meet role-specific security clearance and site access requirements.

Our children require very special teachers who are able to manage some complex and challenging behaviours. They will know that our children require lots of attention, the right sort of communication, consistency and flexibility in equal measure, and a non-judgemental approach.

We want our teachers to be part of the decision making that drives our school, provides outcomes for children and advocates for every child. The Opportunity

Our mechanical infrastructure team designs and delivers mechanical elements of water and wastewater treatment and pumping projects, supports frameworks and projects for clients such as Welsh Water, Wessex Water, United Utilities and Severn Trent. We work alongside Electrical and ICA engineers to deliver integrated MEICA solutions and provide design leadership, technical assurance, equipment specification, multidisciplinary coordination and support to design Managers and Project Manager.

Our graduates use mechanical engineering principles to solve problems that affect all our lives, such as providing energy, managing waste or treating water. You will work on real projects, designing and learning from experts alongside formal training to support you as you grow into your career. Typical day to day tasks may include designs and calculations, technical reports, building 3D models, mechanical equipment specification, site visits, and a variety of project meetings and workshops.

As you discover more of your own abilities and interests, we work with you to increase your role and expand your capabilities. We encourage our staff to work towards a professional qualification with the IMechE, but throughout your time at Arup, you will always be learning, with support and encouragement from our diverse multidisciplinary teams.

The team is looking to expand beyond its traditional water focus into energy-related work. Areas highlighted in team strategy documents include renewables, hydrogen, hydropower, heat networks, energy storage and decarbonisation projects

https://www.arup.com/projects/pont-y-felin-lane/

https://www.arup.com/markets/water/wastewater-management/

Is this role right for you?

For this opportunity, we are seeking the following qualifications, skills and attributes:

- Masters level degree (or equivalent) in Mechanical Engineering or related subject such as Energy or Nuclear but would also consider those with a Bachelors degree. Minimum 2:1.
- A genuine interest in solving problems that affect the way we live
- Keen to deliver mechanical designs for infrastructure and industrial installations as part of multidisciplinary teams
- Degree accreditation by the IMechE is preferred, other institutions would be considered.

- Full working rights in the country of application
- No more than 12 months of full-time experience in a comparable role

- Changemakers: A passion for sustainable development and creating a better world is key.

- Growth seekers: You have a growth mindset, always eager to learn and explore new ways of working.
- Adaptable adventurers: You’re ready to take on any challenge that comes your way.

You should be able to start this opportunity on 1 September 2027.

Eligibility

What we offer you

At Arup, we care about each member’s success, so we can grow together.

Guided by our values, we provide an attractive total reward package that recognises the contribution of each of our members to our shared success. As well as competitive, fair and equitable pay, we offer a career in which all of our members can belong, grow and thrive – through benefits that support health and wellbeing, a wide range of learning opportunities and many possibilities to have an impact through the work they do.

We are owned in trust on behalf of our members, giving us the freedom, with personal responsibility, to set our own direction and choose work that aligns with our purpose and adds to Arup’s legacy. Our members collaborate on ambitious projects to deliver remarkable outcomes for our clients and communities. Profit Share is a key part of our reward, enabling permanent members to share in the results of our collective efforts.

We take an approach to flexible working that supports the diversity and wellbeing of our graduates.

We also provide for our permanent members Private medical insurance, Life assurance, Accident insurance and Income protection cover. In addition, you’ll have access to flexible benefits to help you look after all aspects of your wellbeing and give you the freedom and flexibility to find the best solutions for you, your family, and your individual needs.

Next Steps

We've designed our application process to be straightforward and supportive, giving you the opportunity to showcase your skills and potential. Applications are reviewed as they're received, so we encourage you to apply as early as possible.

The process includes an online application, psychometric testing, application review, case study, interview and offer stage. Our friendly Early Careers team is available throughout the process to answer questions and help you feel confident every step of the way.

Different people, shared values

Our internal employee networks support our inclusive culture: from race, ethnicity and cross-cultural working to gender equity and LGBTQ+ and disability inclusion – we aim to create a space for you to express yourself and make a positive difference.
