title: School Staff and Outdoor Instructor (SSI)
description:
Clifton College is seeking a dedicated and experienced School Staff and Outdoor Instructor (SSI) to play a key role in delivering our thriving Combined Cadet Force (CCF) and Outdoor Education programmes. This is an exciting opportunity for an enthusiastic professional to support the development of young people through adventure, leadership, and service.

This is a full-time, term-time only position, including attendance at field weekends, camps, expeditions, and other co-curricular events as required.

Working closely with the Contingent Commander and the Head of Outdoor Education, the successful candidate will undertake a varied dual role, combining responsibility for the day-to-day operation of the College's CCF with the delivery of a broad and engaging Outdoor Education programme, including the Duke of Edinburgh's Award.

This role offers the opportunity to shape meaningful experiences for pupils through training exercises, expeditions, adventurous activities, camps, and leadership development opportunities. Approximately half of the role will be dedicated to the CCF, including training, administration, logistics, safety management, and supporting cadets and staff. The remaining time will focus on Outdoor Education, supporting the Duke of Edinburgh's Award programme, expeditions, Ten Tors training, and a range of adventurous activities.

Outdoor Education and the CCF are integral parts of life at Clifton College, helping pupils to develop confidence, resilience, teamwork, leadership skills, and a spirit of adventure. Through a wide range of activities including expeditions, field exercises, climbing, kayaking, mountain biking, and rifle shooting, pupils are encouraged to challenge themselves and build lasting skills beyond the classroom.

We are looking for an organised, proactive, and highly motivated individual with strong instructional skills and a passion for working with young people. The successful candidate will bring experience in delivering adventurous activities and training programmes, alongside the ability to manage equipment, logistics, administration, and safety responsibilities to the highest standards. Mountain Leader (Summer) qualification and Skill at Arms Instructor accreditation are essential.

For further details regarding this role, please see the attached job description.

Please note that we can only accept applications via our vacancy website application form (which will also allow you to attach your CV or any other supporting information).

Clifton College is part of Clifton College Education Group, and is a leading independent day and boarding school educating over 1,200 pupils aged 3 to 18 years. The College offers day education, flexi and full boarding and is a proudly inclusive and supportive community, with over 40 nationalities represented.

Founded in 1862, the College provides an exceptional all-round education that successfully combines a rich heritage with modern state-of-the-art facilities. Located in one of the most beautiful suburbs of the vibrant city of Bristol, we are proud to offer the finest all-round education based on the highest academic and pastoral standards, and a diverse range of first-class co-curricular activities.

For further details regarding this role, please see the attached job description.

Please note that we can only accept applications via our vacancy website application form (which will also allow you to attach your CV or any other supporting information).

Closing date: 2nd November 2026

Early applications are encouraged, as the College reserves the right to interview and possibly appoint candidates before the closing date.

Clifton College is committed to creating and promoting a diverse and inclusive workforce that better reflects our community. Applications are welcome from all suitably qualified candidates regardless of age, disability, sex, gender reassignment, sexual orientation, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief and marriage / civil partnerships. We particularly encourage applications from under-represented groups. Please note, we require candidates to be at least 18 years of age for all roles apart from our lifeguard positions where candidates are required to be 16+ with the relevant qualifications.

We are committed to the safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people. All staff and volunteers are required to share this commitment. Safeguarding is underpinned by a range of policies and procedures which encourage and promote safe working practice across the College. We make sure that all our staff are trained and supervised to a high standard so they can provide safe, effective practice.

All posts are subject to a safer recruitment process which includes the disclosure of criminal records and barring checks, scrutiny of employment history, robust referencing and other vetting checks. Due to the nature of the role, you will need to complete an enhanced criminal record disclosure (DBS check) and undergo our pre-employment screening. As a regulated sector we are required to ask for references prior to interview, by applying for this role you are consenting for us to contact your referees.Please note that this role is exempt from the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974 therefore you will be asked to disclose all previous convictions not exempt under amendments to the Exceptions Order 1975, 2013 and 2020.

About Us

St Athan Primary is a one form entry primary school with a nursery. Our school building is a single-story structure built in 1967 and has been well maintained over the years.

Originally being a much larger school, we are fortunate to have adequate space for community rooms and breakout areas for children who have difficulty regulating their behaviour. The school grounds are extensive with a large playing field and playgrounds, and a well-established outdoor learning area.

The school was originally built to accommodate the children from St Athan and the surrounding villages and the children from RAF St Athan which at the time was one of the biggest training camps in the country. The numbers of military children have fallen in recent years but we still have a large contingent of Army children and a transient population of children from the ex-MOD houses, of which many are social housing or buy to lets. This does bring its challenges, we currently have 28% of pupils eligible for free school meals.

Our vision is to nurture confident, curious and resilient learners within a happy, caring and ambitious community, where children and adults are valued, supported and inspired to succeed together.

We are proud to offer:

title: Senior iOS Developer - Manchester
description:
About RA

Resident Advisor has been a home for electronic music culture since 2001. Event discovery, ticketing, news and long-form editorial, artist profiles, original films, and a weekly mix series two decades deep. Around 7 million people use the web platform every month, with a wider audience across our apps and other channels. Underneath the platform sits a network of contributors and city managers across dozens of cities, which is how we stay connected to the scenes we cover rather than reporting on them from a distance. RA is 25 years old, independent, B.Corp certified and intent on being indispensable to the artists, promoters and audiences who make this culture.

The role

You'll be a senior engineer on the RA Guide iOS app: shaping how it's built, leading the technical design of larger features, and raising the bar on quality with the Apps lead.

RA Guide is RA's app for browsing events and buying tickets, native on iOS and Android and used by thousands of people every day. We also make RA Scan, a cross-platform app promoters use to scan tickets at the door. You'll join the Apps team: the Apps lead (who also builds on iOS), an Android developer and a product manager, working closely with design and the web teams who build the APIs the app uses.

We release weekly. Native releases can't be rolled back once they're out, so we care about getting each one right: tests, careful review, and watching what happens after release.

Responsibilities

- Lead the technical design of larger features, including the specs that line up iOS and Android on the same APIs
- Own areas of the codebase, and modernise older parts of it safely
- Raise release quality: automated UI tests on native frameworks, crash analysis and monitoring
- Review code and mentor other developers
- Work with the web and platform teams on the APIs the app depends on
- Help shape how the team uses AI in development, and where it shouldn't

Who We Are Looking For

- Several years building and releasing iOS apps used at scale
- Deep experience with Swift, app architecture and refactoring code that's already live
- Testing and coding habits for stable app releases
- You make the developers around you better, through review, pairing and clear explanation
- You can explain a technical trade-off to product and design in plain terms

If you meet most of these but not all, we'd still like to hear from you. We'll help you grow into the rest.

Nice to have

- SwiftUI, reactive programming and GraphQL
- A/B testing, phased rollouts and data tracking
- Monitoring tools such as Datadog
- Android or cross-platform experience
- An interest in electronic music and the scenes RA serves

What We Offer You

- Generous annual leave policies aimed at promoting work-life balance
- Matched pension, or 401k for US staff
- Comprehensive staff wellbeing initiatives, featuring regular activities and workplace programmes to support mental and physical health. This includes discounted ClassPass memberships and custom-fitted earplugs
- Company-led social events, team lunches, and discounts on merch
- Paid annual volunteering allowance, encouraging contributions to community projects and charities you care about
- A transparent internal company culture committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion (see: https://ra.co/about/diversity)
- Active involvement in community projects within the electronic music community (see: https://ra.co/about/community)

More About RA

We are independent and we intend to stay that way. 25 years in, RA answers to the culture it came from rather than to outside stakeholders. That is what enables us to make decisions on a long-term basis.

Our staff, contributors and international teams are not observers. They are part of the scenes we cover, and that is what we hire for. Craft first, and then a genuine stake in this music rather than just a job in it.

RA has been B Corp certified since 2024, which holds us to standards on social and environmental impact we would want to meet regardless of the badge.

We especially welcome applicants from diverse backgrounds, abilities, ethnicities, experiences, gender identities, and sexual orientations.

Our values

- Electronic music is art
- We celebrate the progressive values that underpin electronic music
- We advocate for a more inclusive and equitable electronic music community
- We honour the past, present and future of electronic music
- We use innovation to empower the community
- We choose honesty over gain and purpose over profit
- We're always front left

This role is a full-time based in our Manchester office. Please note: this position requires applicants to be based in Manchester and to work from the office three days per week. The annual salary range for this role is £60,000- £80,000. If you have questions about the role, please contact work@ra.co.

This listing will be open for a minimum of two weeks from 25th September. Please be sure to add work@ra.co to your contacts and check your junk/spam folder for emails from us.

title: Lead Electrical Engineer Earthing
description:
Lead Electrical Engineer - Earthing

Hybrid working with one of the following as your primary site:
Derby, Manchester or Warrington

We are recruiting a Lead Electrical Engineer - Earthing

The Electrical Systems team is responsible for delivering safe, resilient and technically robust electrical infrastructure across the power station. Earthing and lightning protection systems are fundamental to ensuring plant safety, regulatory compliance and system integrity. This includes the design, verification and substantiation of systems that protect both people and equipment, ensuring a consistent and compliant approach across the station.

About the Role:

As a Lead Electrical Engineer - Earthing, you will provide technical expertise across the design and development lifecycle of earthing and lightning protection systems. You will lead system architecture, sub system design, equipment specification and the selection of components necessary to realise the final verified design of the SMR power station.

You will work across engineering teams electrical, civil, systems, safety and project functions to ensure earthing systems are integrated effectively, compliant with UK and international standards and aligned with overall plant architecture.

You will act as a responsible designer and intelligent customer, ensuring quality, consistency and technical rigour throughout the project lifecycle.

You will support design reviews, risk assessments, strategic planning, and technical governance activities. You may also mentor less experienced engineers and support engagement with suppliers, customers, regulators and external stakeholders.

We'll Need You To:

Provide technical leadership for earthing and lightning protection systems

Assess and substantiate designs to ensure compliance with UK and international standards

Develop system architecture, specifications, design documentation and component selections

Support designers by offering technical guidance and design review input

Lead or contribute to technical reviews, ensuring quality is maintained through project gates

Identify risks and develop mitigations during system design and integration

Support capacity planning, long term strategy and team development

Work across power station engineering teams to deliver standardised, commoditised approaches to system design

Represent electrical engineering in working groups, supplier engagements, customer discussions and regulatory dialogue

Manage or oversee supply chain partners delivering work packages

Coach and mentor less experienced engineers across the electrical discipline

Key Skills Required:

We know there's no such thing as the 'perfect' candidate. If you meet around 75% of the criteria below, we'd love to hear from you:

Experience across the electrical system lifecycle in a regulated industry (nuclear preferred but not essential)

Strong knowledge and experience in earthing and lightning protection system design, assessment, verification, installation, commissioning and maintenance

Knowledge of relevant earthing and lightning protection codes and standards for the UK and Europe

Experience developing earthing and lightning protection systems in nuclear or high integrity environments

Knowledge of systems engineering methodologies, including MBSE tools such as Capella, DOORS or Polarion

Proven ability to manage contract partners delivering technical work packages

Understanding of commercial availability and cost considerations for materials

Practical field experience in earthing or lightning protection design or installation

Strong communication and presentation skills, including the ability to present complex
information to technical and non technical audiences

Degree in electrical engineering or related discipline (or equivalent relevant experience)

We welcome applicants from a wide range of regulated sectors including nuclear, defence, aerospace, rail and energy.

Salary and Package:

The salary band for this will be between £60,000-£78,750 dependent on the skills, values and knowledge you bring. There may be some flexibility with the starting salary in exceptional cases, and, in due course, the role may be developed further.

Benefits include:

Bonus - Performance related target opportunity 12.5%
Benefits Cash Allowance £2,200 per annum for a bespoke package
Pension - 12% employer and 6% employee contributions
Holidays - 28 days (+ public holidays) with the ability to buy or sell up to 4 days
Private Medical Insurance - BUPA single cover
Life Assurance - 6x pensionable pay
Home Office Support - £250 one off payment for new starters

Obtaining Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) clearance

Satisfactory completion of a basic financial probity check

description:

description:
Company Description

Company Description

Within The OWO destination there are a total of nine restaurants and three bars, including one by our signature chef Mauro Colagreco. The Guerlain spa and Pillar Wellness offer the latest in wellbeing, and a 600 seated-capacity grand ballroom, The Whitehall, is perfect for all kinds of special occasions and events.

Job Description

Responsibilities:

- Projects for benefit of kitchen advancement.
- Always able to explain services to guests, visitors, and employees.

Qualifications, Skills & Experience

Essential

- To work as required on a rota basis.
- A proven track record and ability to provide high levels of service under pressure.
- Exceptional communication and customer service skills, both written and spoken.
- Strong time management skills with the ability to multi-task while maintaining an immaculate and professional appearance.

title: BIM Manager
description:
Arcadis is the world's leading company delivering sustainable design, engineering, and consultancy solutions for natural and built assets.

We are more than 34,000 people, in over 30 countries, dedicated to improving quality of life. Everyone has an important role to play. With the power of many curious minds, together we can solve the world’s most complex challenges and deliver more impact together.

Role description:

The BIM Manager will provide leadership for Building Information Modelling and information management across multidisciplinary projects. The role will establish and maintain effective BIM delivery arrangements, lead project teams in the production and assurance of coordinated digital deliverables, and ensure that client, Arcadis and project requirements are understood and achieved.

Working with project managers, technical leads, BIM coordinators, global delivery teams, clients and delivery partners, the BIM Manager will manage BIM strategy, standards, resources, quality and performance. The role will also support bids, client relationships, capability development and the adoption of improved digital methods across the business.

Role accountabilities:

- Lead BIM and information management delivery across single-discipline and multidisciplinary projects, ensuring outputs meet agreed scope, programme, budget, quality and client expectations.
- Develop, implement and maintain project BIM strategies, BIM Execution Plans, procedures, model production and delivery arrangements, information requirements and associated project controls.
- Coordinate project setup, model federation, clash detection, design reviews, data exchanges, drawing production, document control and the issue of coordinated project information.
- Interpret client requirements and translate them into clear responsibilities, workflows, deliverables, acceptance criteria and production schedules for project teams.
- Work closely with project managers and technical leads to select, plan and manage appropriately skilled BIM resources, including Arcadis global delivery teams, suppliers and subconsultants.
- Provide direction to BIM coordinators, modellers, designers and engineers, ensuring team members understand the project brief, standards, interfaces and delivery priorities.
- Undertake or coordinate checking, verification and assurance of models, drawings and related information in accordance with Arcadis management systems, project procedures and applicable standards.
- Lead interdisciplinary coordination and resolve model, information and workflow issues, including differences between designers, coordinators and checkers.
- Monitor BIM delivery performance, risks, assumptions, decisions, changes and dependencies, escalating material issues and implementing corrective actions where required.
- Promote health, safety and wellbeing, Safe by Design principles, CDM compliance and effective hazard identification and risk management throughout digital design delivery.
- Build effective relationships with clients and key stakeholders, communicate delivery status, manage expectations and support the timely resolution of technical and project issues.
- Support project commercial management through accurate scope definition, resource forecasting, progress monitoring, change control and input to invoicing and financial reporting.
- Contribute BIM and digital delivery content to bids, proposals, presentations and client engagement, helping Arcadis produce high-quality, competitive submissions.
- Champion consistent BIM standards, templates, common data environment practices, automation and improved methods of working, including appropriate use of scripting and emerging technology.
- Coach and mentor BIM and engineering professionals, support structured development and CPD, and promote knowledge sharing across teams, disciplines and locations.
- Maintain awareness of industry, technical and legislative developments and contribute to the continued development of Arcadis BIM capability and professional reputation.

Qualifications & Experience:

- A degree, HNC/HND or equivalent qualification in engineering, architecture, construction, BIM, digital design or a related discipline, supported by relevant industry experience.
- Demonstrable experience managing BIM and information delivery on multidisciplinary design or engineering projects, preferably within infrastructure, energy, utilities or the wider built environment.
- Strong working knowledge of BIM processes, coordinated model delivery, clash detection, model assurance, drawing production, document control and common data environments.
- Experience preparing and implementing BIM Execution Plans, project standards, information delivery plans, procedures and digital delivery workflows.
- Proficiency in relevant BIM authoring, coordination and review applications, with the ability to develop capability across more than one software platform.
- Knowledge of applicable UK BIM and information management standards, client requirements, Arcadis management systems and relevant health and safety and CDM obligations.
- Experience leading and developing project teams, coordinating global delivery resources and working effectively across technical disciplines and organisational boundaries.
- Proven project management capability, including planning, resource management, risk and change control, quality assurance, programme and commercial awareness.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the confidence to engage clients, senior stakeholders, technical specialists, suppliers and delivery teams.
- Strong analytical, coordination and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities, resolve complex interfaces and deliver practical solutions.
- A collaborative and inclusive leadership style, a growth mindset and a commitment to continuous improvement, innovation and knowledge sharing.
- Professional membership or progress towards an appropriate chartered or incorporated status is desirable.

Why Arcadis?

We can only achieve our goals when everyone is empowered to be their best. We believe everyone's contribution matters. It’s why we are pioneering a skills-based approach, where you can harness your unique experience and expertise to carve your career path and maximize the impact we can make together.

You’ll do meaningful work, and no matter what role, you’ll be helping to deliver sustainable solutions for a more prosperous planet. Make your mark, on your career, your colleagues, your clients, your life and the world around you.

Together, we can create a lasting legacy.

Join Arcadis. Create a Legacy.

Our Commitment to Equality, Diversity, Inclusion & Belonging

We want you to be able to bring your best self to work every day which is why we take equality and inclusion seriously and hold ourselves to account for our actions. Our ambition is to be an employer of choice and provide a great place to work for all our people. We believe that by working together diverse people with different experiences develop the most innovative ideas. Equality, diversity and inclusion is at the heart of how we improve quality of life and we work closely with our people across six ED&I Workstreams: Age, Disability, Faith, Gender, LGBT+ and Race. A diverse and skilled workforce is essential to our success.

title: German Customer Service Advisor
description:
Job Description

Rate of pay: £14.66 per hour

Upon successful completion of your probationary period, there is a possibility to receive a performance-related bonus of up to 20%, paid quarterly.

Shifts available (36 hours per week):

- Monday to Thursday 11am-7pm & Friday 10am-5.45pm
- Sunday 10am-5.45pm, Monday to Thursday 11am-7pm

During our peak trading periods (up to 20 weeks throughout the year), you’ll also be required to work one additional 4 hour shift, per week in order to better service our customers' needs. This is paid additionally and is booked in advance to maintain a smooth and organised schedule for our employees.

Start date : Monday 2nd November 2026

Location: Radar Road, Leicester

Training : At NEXT, we don’t just hire people; we help them evolve. We want every new colleague in our International Team to feel confident and knowledgeable from the moment they start.

That is why your first five weeks are dedicated to your growth:

- Mandatory paid training (2 weeks): Get to grips with our systems and how we help our global customers
- Coaching (3 weeks): Get dedicated support to help you settle into the role

The role:

Join our dynamic International department and take on the challenge of supporting our global reach. You will engage with customers, handle enquiries with care, and resolve issues efficiently to create a positive experience every time. Working closely with internal teams, you’ll ensure every interaction is smooth and supportive.

This is an incredible opportunity for a fluent German speaker who enjoys problem-solving and thrives in a fast-paced, collaborative environment where we never stand still.

What you’ll take on:

- Always think customer: Deliver professional support in German and English across phone, email, WhatsApp and live chat, ensuring every interaction is clear and helpful.
- Make it happen: Support customers with a range of enquiries, from orders to account questions, always aiming for an effective resolution.
- Invite collaboration: Work with internal teams and International couriers to investigate and resolve queries quickly, contributing to a seamless experience.
- Learn to evolve: Use our internal systems to keep accurate records, maintaining attention to detail while looking for ways to improve our processes.
- Keep it real: Build lasting relationships by being honest, showing empathy, and providing a high level of care.
- Take it on: Handle challenging conversations with a calm, professional manner to ensure every interaction remains positive.

What you'll bring:

- Fluency in German: You can communicate clearly and confidently in both written and spoken.
- Strong English skills: You’ll support a diverse customer base with ease.
- Customer experience: You have previous experience in a customer-facing role or contact centre and understand what great service looks like.
- A problem-solver mindset: You have strong attention to detail and the ability to think on your feet.
- Tech savvy: You are confident using computer systems and CRM platforms, with the ability to learn new tools quickly.
- A positive approach: You are proactive, professional, and have a genuine passion for helping people.

About International:

Connect globally. Support confidently. Make a real impact.

You'll be part of our expanding International team, supporting customers from around 130 countries (we've got over 1.5 million of them!), supported by our contact centre teams in Manchester, Poland, and Pune.

There’s never been a better time to become part of the International team.

What's NEXT:

All successful applicants will be subject to criminal & credit checks in line with our Reference Policy. In order to apply for this position you must not have had an unsuccessful application for a similar role in 6 months.

In accordance with Home Office guidance successful candidates will be required to evidence their right to work in the UK before commencement of employment. This role is not one we would typically consider for sponsorship under the Skilled Worker route due to, for example, the relevant Home Office requirements on skills level, not being met. Candidates are therefore encouraged to consider their own right to work options without Next sponsorship.

Please note that we are aware of fraudulent recruitment adverts on some third party sites. NEXT does not request or require any payment at any stage of the recruitment process.

About Us

You know Next, but did you know we’re a FTSE-100 retail company employing over 44,000 people across the Next group. We’re the UK’s 2nd largest fashion retailer and for Kidswear we’re the market leader. At the last count we have over 450 stores, plus the Next Online and it’s now possible to buy on-line from over 80 countries around the world! So we’ve gone global!

About The Team

- 25% off most NEXT, MADE*, Lipsy*, Gap* and Victoria's Secret* products (*when purchased through NEXT)
- Quarterly bonuses
- Free parking on Next authorised sites
- Early VIP access to sale stock
- Access to fantastic discounts at our Staff Shops
- 10% off most partner brands & up to 15% off Branded Beauty
- Restaurants with great food at amazing prices
- Hot deals and exclusive offers from over 3,500 retailers through our online benefits platform
- Access a digital GP and other free health and wellbeing services
- Sharesave scheme
- Financial Wellbeing - Save, track and enhance your financial wellbeing
- Direct to Work - Discount online and instore, collect your items the next day for free from your place of work or local store
- Support Networks - Access to Network Groups to empower and celebrate each other
- Wellhub - Discounted flexible monthly gym memberships, with apps, PT sessions and more

Conditions apply to all benefits. These benefits are discretionary and subject to change.

We aim to support all candidates during the application process and are happy to provide workplace adjustments when necessary. Should you need support with your application due to a disability or long-term condition, feel free to get in touch with us by email nextonline_careers@next.co.uk (please include 'Workplace Adjustments' in the subject line), or call us on 0333 777 8166 and leave a voicemail.

title: Senior SACT Nurse (Bristol)
description:
Are you an experienced oncology nurse looking for an opportunity to take your SACT expertise to the next level?

Join GenesisCare at our Bristol Cancer Centre, where you'll be part of a specialist team delivering personalised cancer care and the latest systemic anti-cancer treatments in a modern outpatient environment.

As a Senior SACT Nurse, you'll have the opportunity to combine hands-on clinical excellence with leadership, education, service development and research. You'll manage your own patient caseload, run nurse-led clinics, work closely with leading oncology consultants and provide expert support to patients throughout their treatment journey.

The Role

As a Senior SACT Nurse, you'll play a key role in delivering a high-quality chemotherapy and SACT service at our Bristol centre, providing specialist nursing advice and support to patients and their families from diagnosis through treatment.

You'll work autonomously while providing clinical leadership within the SACT team, ensuring patients receive safe, evidence-based and personalised care.

You'll also have the opportunity to deputise for the Lead SACT Nurse when required, support the development of junior colleagues and contribute to the ongoing development of our nursing practice and services.

Our Bristol centre provides patients with access to a comprehensive range of SACT alongside advanced radiotherapy and integrated cancer care, creating an environment where you can work closely with a genuinely multidisciplinary team.

What You'll Do

- Manage your own patient caseload and provide specialist nursing advice throughout the cancer treatment pathway
- Run nurse-led clinics and assess patients' health, treatment and nursing needs
- Deliver chemotherapy and other systemic anti-cancer therapies safely and effectively
- Use your advanced clinical skills in venepuncture, cannulation and central venous access
- Recognise and manage treatment complications, including anaphylaxis, extravasation and neutropenic sepsis
- Provide telephone triage and out-of-hours support as part of the 24-hour on-call team
- Work closely with medical consultants, pharmacists, radiographers and the wider multidisciplinary team
- Deputise for the Lead SACT Nurse when required
- Support and develop junior members of the nursing team through education, mentorship and competency assessment
- Contribute to clinical audit, research and service improvement initiatives
- Support the development of clinical protocols and evidence-based nursing practice
- Keep up to date with current research and clinical trials within oncology and SACT
- Promote high standards of patient safety, quality and experience across the service

The role combines advanced clinical practice with opportunities to influence how the service develops, including leading areas of nursing practice, supporting research and contributing to clinical audit and service improvement.

What You'll Have

- NMC Registered Nurse
- Minimum of 2 years' nursing experience
- Previous oncology experience, with experience delivering chemotherapy/SACT
- Experience and competence in intravenous drug administration
- UKONS SACT Passport, or willingness to complete this within three months of appointment
- Experience and competence in venepuncture, cannulation and different types of central venous access devices
- Experience of oncology telephone triage and recognition and management of neutropenic sepsis
- Experience in blood transfusion and bone marrow biopsies
- Strong clinical judgement with the ability to work autonomously and make decisions under pressure
- Excellent communication and organisational skills
- A genuine commitment to delivering outstanding patient care

You'll also need to be comfortable working flexibly to meet the needs of the service, including participation in the 24-hour on-call rota.

Why GenesisCare Bristol?

Our Bristol centre is a specialist outpatient cancer centre serving patients from across the South West and beyond.

You'll work in a centre offering chemotherapy and SACT alongside advanced radiotherapy, including stereotactic ablative radiotherapy (SABR), image-guided radiotherapy (IGRT), surface-guided radiotherapy (SGRT), volumetric modulated arc therapy (VMAT) and deep inspiration breath hold (DIBH).

The centre also has access to Exercise Medicine and Penny Brohn, supporting GenesisCare's whole-person approach to cancer care.

You'll be surrounded by experienced oncology professionals and work alongside consultants from local and nationally recognised hospitals, giving you the opportunity to develop your knowledge and broaden your experience within specialist cancer care.

Discover what's in store for you when you join the GenesisCare UK team:

- 26 days' annual leave, plus bank holidays, with the option to buy more or sell back annual leave
- Private medical and dental cover
- Income Protection
- Employee Assistance Programme
- Access to world-class radiotherapy, free to you and your immediate family if required
- Competitive company contributory pension scheme
- Access to wellbeing support including Headspace
- Free parking at our Bristol centre
- Exclusive retail discounts
- Paid professional memberships and opportunities for continued professional development
- Opportunities to attend training and conferences and develop your specialist expertise

GenesisCare actively invests in professional development, including training, professional memberships and conference opportunities, with a focus on helping employees grow within their roles.

Who We Are

GenesisCare is the UK's leading independent provider of specialist cancer care, with 14 state-of-the-art centres across the UK.

We bring together highly experienced clinicians and healthcare professionals to provide personalised cancer care, including advanced diagnostics, medical oncology, radiotherapy and Theranostics.

Our SACT services offer a comprehensive range of systemic anti-cancer therapies, including chemotherapy, immunotherapy, targeted therapies, hormone therapies and monoclonal antibodies, supported by specialist oncology nurses and dedicated pharmacy teams.

We believe in treating the whole person, not just the cancer, combining clinical excellence with Exercise Medicine and our partnership with Penny Brohn UK to support patients throughout their treatment and beyond.

We're passionate about innovation, evidence-based care and giving our people the opportunity to develop, learn and make a genuine difference.

If you're an experienced oncology nurse ready to take the next step in your SACT career, we'd love to hear from you.

Please note: we may close this vacancy early if we receive a high volume of strong applications, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

title: QBI Manager
description:
Quality & Business Improvement Manager

Chemring Energetics UK (CEUK) is a global business providing a range of equipment based on energetic materials for defence, civil defence and key commercial customers.

It’s an exciting time to join CEUK. The business has experienced significant growth, creating new opportunities to develop, improve and shape how we work. As we continue this journey, we are looking for talented people to join us and play an important role in our ongoing success.

We have an exciting opportunity for a Quality & Business Improvement Manager to join our QBI and Proof function. This is a key leadership role responsible for maintaining and continually improving CEUK’s Quality Management System, while leading and coordinating quality assurance, proof and business improvement activities across the business.

The successful candidate will provide assurance to customers and regulatory bodies that the quality of CEUK’s products and services meets the required standards and requirements. You will act as a champion for innovation and continuous improvement, challenging existing processes and supporting Business Units to deliver measurable improvements.

You will have line management responsibility for the QBI and Proof teams, as well as functional responsibility for Quality Assurance Engineers across our Business Units. You will support the development of team capability, provide leadership on quality and improvement initiatives, and ensure the integrity of our product verification, proof and release processes.

Key Accountabilities & Duties

- Ensure all activities within your area of responsibility are undertaken in full compliance with HS&E legislation and company and local procedures and policies.
- Promote a strong safety culture and report unsafe acts and conditions through the appropriate Near Miss reporting system.
- Uphold the integrity of the product verification, proof and release processes, ensuring all relevant measurements, inspections and tests are completed to the required standards and satisfactory results obtained before products are issued with a Certificate of Conformity (CoC) and released to customers.
- Maintain and continually improve the Quality Management System, ensuring quality engineering, assurance and control activities meet the needs of internal and external stakeholders and support the maintenance of ISO 9001 accreditation.
- Ensure the effective management and delivery of proof activities, maintaining the required standards, controls, records and processes.
- Educate and support employees across CEUK in understanding and applying the Quality Management System and associated quality processes.
- Work with the QBI and Proof teams and Business Unit Quality Assurance Engineers to develop and manage an effective audit programme, monitoring the effectiveness of and compliance with business and manufacturing processes and procedures.
- Lead and support effective Root Cause Analysis and resolution of non-conformances from all sources, with a focus on identifying trends and reducing the cost of non-conformance year on year.
- Lead investigations into significant or cross-business quality issues and ensure appropriate corrective and preventative actions are implemented.
- Mentor and support Business Unit Quality Assurance Engineers with customer engagement, product and process audits, inspections and other quality-related activities.
- Work collaboratively with managers across the business to identify, prioritise and facilitate business improvement projects, ensuring the improvement pipeline, prioritisation matrix and project boards are maintained and regularly reviewed.
- Champion a culture of continuous improvement through education and training in Lean Six Sigma tools and techniques, supported by standardised processes, templates and effective project management.
- Scrutinise and challenge projects and programmes across the Business Units to ensure continuous improvement is embedded as a key driver and that measurable outcomes are achieved.
- Provide leadership, coaching and development to the QBI and Proof teams, ensuring effective delivery of quality, proof and business improvement activities while building capability across the function.
- Ensure appropriate resources, skills and training are in place within the QBI and Proof teams to meet current and future business requirements.

About You
We are looking for an experienced quality professional with a strong background in manufacturing, quality management and continuous improvement. You will be confident working across functions, challenging existing practices and engaging with colleagues at all levels to drive improvements.

Essential:

- Engineering degree in a mechanical or electrical discipline.
- Diploma in Quality Management.
- Lean Six Sigma qualification or equivalent training.
- Lead Auditor qualification/training.
- At least two years’ experience in a Quality Management role within a manufacturing environment.
- Experience of Quality Management System implementation, maintenance and auditing.
- Strong problem-solving and Root Cause Analysis skills.
- Experience of leading successful improvement projects, including DMAIC reviews.
- Strong technical report writing and presentation skills.
- Advanced Microsoft Office skills and experience of working with business management systems.
- Strong communication, influencing and leadership skills, with the ability to work effectively across different functions and levels of an organisation.

Desirable:

- Chartered status with the Chartered Quality Institute (CQI) or equivalent.
- Technical understanding or experience of energetic materials and/or energetic products.
- Experience of working within a regulated or high-hazard manufacturing environment.

What We Offer
In return, we offer a competitive salary and a comprehensive benefits package, including pension, Bupa healthcare, an Employee Assistance Programme and a range of flexible benefits, including Cycle2Work and access to a variety of local and national employee discounts.

Join CEUK
This is an exciting opportunity to take a leading role in quality, proof and business improvement within a growing manufacturing business, working alongside colleagues across CEUK to maintain high standards while identifying new ways to improve how we work.
If you have the skills, experience and ambition to lead our QBI and Proof teams and make a meaningful contribution to our continued growth and success, we would love to hear from you.

Based in Manchester with hybrid working, you will be the financial partner to our property managers and clients, turning complex numbers into clear insight and dependable outcomes.

- Continuous improvement mindset that streamlines processes and strengthens financial controls.

How You'll Spend Most Of Your Time

- Preparing monthly bank reconciliations, journals, accruals and prepayments for your portfolio.
- Producing draft service charge year-end accounts, supporting schedules and audit packs.
- Partnering with property managers to build and review annual budgets and expenditure forecasts.
- Monitoring cashflow, processing supplier payments, and allocating receipts accurately.
- Investigating and resolving accounting queries from clients, leaseholders, auditors and suppliers.
- Maintaining accurate records, controls and compliance with internal policies and client agreements.

Who This Role Is For

- You balance precision with pragmatism, delivering accurate work at pace and owning outcomes.
- You’re a clear, considerate communicator who can explain financial information simply.
- You enjoy collaborating across teams and building positive relationships with clients and colleagues.
- You are organised and resilient, able to prioritise effectively across a varied portfolio.
- You’re curious and improvement-focused, always looking for smarter ways to work.

Experience That Helps

- Experience in client or property accounting, ideally within residential block management.

- Working with auditors, external stakeholders and multi-site portfolios.

title: Client Accountant

CLIENT ACCOUNTANT

- Scanlans Property Management

Role Overview

You will play a key role in delivering accurate, timely client accounting for a diverse residential block management portfolio. Based in Manchester with hybrid working, you will be the financial partner to our property managers and clients, turning complex numbers into clear insight and dependable outcomes.

You will thrive in a team that values accountability, care, and collaboration. Your expertise will ensure service charge funds are safeguarded, year-end accounts land on time, and clients receive proactive, professional support that builds trust and long-term relationships.

ROLE EXPECTATIONS

You will own the end-to-end service charge accounting cycle for an allocated portfolio, from bank reconciliations and accruals to draft year-end accounts and audit liaison. Most days you will collaborate with property managers, resolve queries from clients and suppliers, and keep ledgers, statements and budgets accurate and up to date.

What Success Looks Like

- Consistently accurate ledgers, reconciled bank accounts and clean month-end close within agreed timelines.
- Year-end service charge accounts delivered on schedule, with clear working papers and minimal audit queries.
- Proactive communication that keeps property managers and clients informed, with queries resolved promptly.
- Forecasts and budgets that are realistic, well-evidenced and easily understood by non-finance stakeholders.
- Strong cash management: timely supplier payments, robust credit control support and clear client statements.
- Continuous improvement mindset that streamlines processes and strengthens financial controls.

How You'll Spend Most Of Your Time

- Preparing monthly bank reconciliations, journals, accruals and prepayments for your portfolio.
- Producing draft service charge year-end accounts, supporting schedules and audit packs.
- Partnering with property managers to build and review annual budgets and expenditure forecasts.
- Monitoring cashflow, processing supplier payments, and allocating receipts accurately.
- Investigating and resolving accounting queries from clients, leaseholders, auditors and suppliers.
- Maintaining accurate records, controls and compliance with internal policies and client agreements.

Who This Role Is For

- You balance precision with pragmatism, delivering accurate work at pace and owning outcomes.
- You’re a clear, considerate communicator who can explain financial information simply.
- You enjoy collaborating across teams and building positive relationships with clients and colleagues.
- You are organised and resilient, able to prioritise effectively across a varied portfolio.
- You’re curious and improvement-focused, always looking for smarter ways to work.

Experience That Helps

- Experience in client or property accounting, ideally within residential block management.
- Familiarity with service charge accounting, audits and year-end processes.
- Confidence using accounting/property management systems and Excel for reconciliations and analysis.
- Working with auditors, external stakeholders and multi-site portfolios.
- Exposure to budgeting, forecasting and variance analysis.

What We Offer

- Competitive salary
- 25 days holiday plus bank holidays
- Perkbox membership, discounts across retail, travel and entertainment
- Free eye tests
- Fully funded training and professional development, including paid study leave (up to £1,500)

About Scanlans Property Management

Scanlans Property Management is a well-established residential block management business, known for delivering a high standard of service to clients, leaseholders and residents across the North and Midlands. We manage a varied portfolio and take pride in providing proactive, professional support that makes a real difference to the communities we look after.

Scanlans is part of Trinity Property Group (TPG) and the wider Odevo Group, giving our teams the backing of a leading international property management business, with the investment, stability and career development opportunities that come with being part of a growing group.

title: HGV Driver
description:
Job Introduction

HGV Driver

Location: Wick Lane, London

Hours: 06:30 – 15:30, Monday to Friday

Job Introduction

At Riney, we play a vital role in delivering infrastructure, highways and construction projects across London. We're looking for a professional and safety-focused HGV Driver to join our Plant & Transport team and help keep our operations moving safely and efficiently. Based from our Wick Lane depot, you'll be responsible for transporting plant, materials, equipment and machinery to sites across the business while maintaining the highest standards of safety, compliance and customer service

This is a varied role that offers more than just driving. You'll become a key member of a supportive team, working closely with operational and workshop colleagues, supporting fleet activities and contributing to the ongoing success of a busy and growing business.

What You'll Be Doing

- Safely operating HGV vehicles in line with road traffic legislation, DVSA requirements and company standards
- Delivering and collecting construction materials, plant, equipment, machinery and waste materials across company sites, depots and supplier locations
- Carrying out daily vehicle inspections, reporting defects and ensuring vehicles remain roadworthy and compliant
- Planning routes efficiently and completing transport documentation and digital records accurately
- Ensuring compliance with Drivers' Hours Regulations, tachograph legislation and transport compliance requirements
- Supporting wider business operations through flexible working across different vehicle types, contracts and operational requirements
- Assisting the Plant & Transport team by moving vehicles, plant and equipment between sites, workshops and testing facilities
- Using the Syrinx 365 fleet management system and Driver App to maintain accurate driver and compliance records
- Completing mandatory FORS training and promoting best practice in road safety, fuel efficiency and environmental performance
- Representing Riney professionally when interacting with customers, suppliers, site teams and members of the public

What We Are Looking For

We're seeking a reliable and conscientious driver who takes pride in delivering a first-class service while maintaining the highest standards of safety and compliance.

You'll ideally have:

- A full UK Driving Licence
- A valid HGV Class 1 (Category C+E) and/or Class 2 (Category C) Licence
- A valid Driver CPC Qualification Card and Digital Tachograph Card
- Experience operating HGV vehicles within construction, highways, infrastructure or a similar environment
- A strong commitment to health, safety and compliance
- Good communication, organisation and teamwork skills
- Basic IT skills and confidence using digital systems and mobile applications
- The flexibility to adapt to changing operational priorities and support the wider business when needed

It would be advantageous if you also hold a HIAB qualification, have experience transporting plant and machinery, possess construction-related certifications such as MPQC or CSCS, or have previous experience with FORS training and fleet management systems.

If you're a professional HGV Driver looking to join a business where safety comes first, where no two days are the same, and where you can make a real contribution to delivering essential infrastructure projects, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Sales Executive

description:
Full job description

About us
We're a leading SaaS ecommerce shipping platform helping retailers streamline fulfilment through intelligent, automation-first software. We've become one of the biggest shipping platforms in the UK by being the best - in customer service, carrier selection, and functionality. Now we're scaling further, with US operations underway, and we need experienced sales professionals to drive that growth.

Our culture
We operate in a results-driven, democratic environment where data wins arguments and your voice genuinely shapes the product. We're honest about our weaknesses, deliberate about our strengths, and we move fast. If you want autonomy and real commercial impact, you'll fit right in.

The role
This role is based full-time out of our Bristol, United Kingdom HQ. We're looking for an experienced sales executive who can work both sides of the pipeline - converting inbound trial leads and building outbound pipeline from scratch. You'll be the first human touchpoint for prospective customers, responsible for qualifying inbound leads quickly and moving them efficiently through a defined process: initial conversation, intro demo, handoff to an Account Executive for a deeper platform walkthrough, commercial send, close, and handover to onboarding.
You won't be winging it. You'll follow a clear, proven sales process and execute it consistently and at pace. The AE handles the in-depth demo and onboarding - your job is to qualify well, build trust early, keep deals moving, and get agreements signed.

On top of inbound, you'll be expected to prospect proactively and build your own pipeline - so you need to know how to generate interest, not just respond to it.

The sales process you'll own

- Inbound qualification - Contact trial leads promptly, understand their business and assess fit
- Intro demo - Walk prospects through the platform at a high level and generate excitement
- AE handoff - Brief the Account Executive and join a deeper-dive demo to answer commercial questions
- Commercials - Send agreements, handle objections, and drive the deal to signature
- Closed/won handover - Pass signed customers to an AE for onboarding
- Outbound prospecting - Proactively build pipeline alongside inbound through calls, email and LinkedIn

Day to day

- Working inbound trial leads quickly and converting them into qualified opportunities
- Running intro demos confidently and tailoring the narrative to each prospect's business
- Coordinating with AEs to ensure smooth, well-briefed handoffs
- Sending commercials and following up persistently and professionally to get deals over the line
- Prospecting outbound to generate your own pipeline on top of inbound volume
- Keeping the CRM accurate and your pipeline well-managed at all stages
- Hitting and exceeding activity and revenue targets

What we're looking for

- 2+ years in a B2B sales role with experience following a structured sales process end-to-end
- Comfortable running demos and early-stage discovery conversations independently
- Knows how to prospect - you can build pipeline through outbound, not just work warm leads
- CRM disciplined - pipeline hygiene and accurate forecasting are second nature
- Strong communicator with high EQ - you adapt your style to different buyers and know when to push and when to listen
- Organised and able to manage multiple deals at different stages without dropping the ball
- Coachable - you take feedback, apply it, and keep improving
- A university degree or equivalent professional experience

Benefits

- Uncapped commission
- Up to 30 days holiday + bank holidays
- Opportunity for international travel
- Close collaboration with the founding team and leadership
- A real voice in how the company grows
- Strong career progression as we scale into new markets
Job Type: Full-time

Benefits:

- Company events
- Profit sharing
Application question(s):

- Give a brief overview of your B2B Saas Sales experience
- Work Location: In person, Bristol United Kingdom

description:
Elizabeth Casson House (ECH) is an 8‑bed female Psychiatric Intensive Care Unit, and we’re looking for a compassionate and confident Band 6 Nurse to join our experienced and supportive team. Our staff bring strong clinical skills, good judgement and a genuine commitment to providing safe, trauma‑informed care to women during periods of crisis. You will also have the opportunity to develop knowledge in women’s mental health and understanding the gender specific factors that influence presentation, risk and recovery.

You will be part of a team that values openness, reflection and shared learning. Staff wellbeing is really important to us! We work closely together, support each other day‑to‑day, and make sure people feel appreciated and equipped to do their best work.

You’ll have opportunities to develop your leadership skills, contribute to service development and build confidence in areas such as de-escalation, relational security and culturally informed practice. We’re committed to developing both our staff and our practice, and to continually improving the experience we offer to the women in our care.

ECH is a bright, calm and therapeutic environment. We are one of the few wards with a dedicated sensory room! A space to support emotional regulation, reduce distress and promote wellbeing.

If you’re looking to join a welcoming, skilled team who are passionate about delivering excellent care and supporting one another, we’d be very happy to hear from you.

As a Band 6 Nurse on ECH, you will take a key leadership role in the day‑to‑day running of the ward. This includes clinically leading shifts, supervising junior staff, and helping to maintain high standards of safe, compassionate care. You will also support the Ward Manager with operational duties and may provide cover in their absence to ensure continuity for the team.

You will support staff to recognise and respond to rising levels of distress, using relational approaches and de‑escalation skills to maintain a calm and therapeutic environment.

The role includes participation in the Duty Nurse rota, offering support and guidance to other wards across the Callington Road Hospital site outside of core hours. This provides valuable experience in site‑wide coordination and leadership.

You will be an experienced RMN or RNLD with a strong commitment to clinical excellence, emotional resilience and service development. Professional growth is important to us, and you will be supported to take responsibility for your own learning through training, supervision, reflective practice and involvement in ward‑based quality improvement projects. Rotational posts can be considered for those wishing to broaden their experience.

ECH is based within Callington Road Hospital, which hosts a range of mental health units. Wards work closely together and support one another when needed, creating a collaborative and responsive environment.

We are the lead provider of healthcare for people with serious mental illness, learning disabilities and autism across Bath and North East Somerset (BaNES), Swindon and Wiltshire, and Bristol, North Somerset and South Gloucestershire.

We aim to provide High Quality, Compassionate Care everywhere, every day. This means our services will be safe, clinically effective and provide a positive all round experience for our patients, families and carers. And we believe passionately in treating everyone with kindness, respect and empathy.

Key to this is providing a supportive and safe environment for our 4,000 staff where we all feel welcome and able to do the best we can for those we support. Our staff and teams work incredibly hard delivering services across more than 90 locations, covering 2,200miles, to more than 1.8million people.

At AWP we actively encourage applicants from all backgrounds; we are particularly keen to encourage applications from people from Black, Asian and minority ethnic backgrounds, those with disabilities and from the LGBTQ+ community. We want people to bring their unique blend of experiences, backgrounds, perspectives and knowledge to AWP, as diversity makes us stronger.

For further details / informal visits contact: Name: Meg Petersen Job title: Ward Manager Email address: m.petersen@nhs.net Telephone number: 01179195220

title: Lecturer in Maths
description:
As one of the fastest-growing Colleges in the UK, delivering courses from entry level right up to Masters degrees, Weston College is an inspiring place to work. Why not join us as a Lecturer in Maths?

Interviews for this role will take place on-site, at one of our college campuses in Weston-super-Mare.
Day to day duties of the role

title: Head Chef
description:
Organization- Hyatt Regency London Blackfriars

Summary

About Hyatt Regency London Blackfriars

Hyatt Regency London Blackfriars is located next to Blackfriars Station in the heart of the City of London, within walking distance of St Paul's Cathedral, Tate Modern and the South Bank. This Grade II listed five-star hotel stands on the historic site of King Henry VIII's Bridewell Palace and features 205 stylish guestrooms and suites along with versatile meeting and event spaces.

Dining experiences include NYnLON , a sophisticated yet relaxed bistro bringing the flavours of New York dining culture to London with East Coast classics and seasonal produce, and Leaf and Cane, a vibrant late-night bar offering premium beverages, live entertainment, and a dynamic social atmosphere.

Colleagues have the opportunity to work in a distinctive historic setting while welcoming both international business travellers and leisure guests to central London.

Duties And Responsibilities Related To The Head Chef Role

- Lead the day-to-day kitchen operations of NYnLON, ensuring exceptional standards of food quality, consistency, presentation, and guest satisfaction.
- Work closely with the Executive Head Chef to deliver the restaurant's culinary vision, seasonal menu offerings, and brand standards.
- Supervise and support the NYnLON kitchen team, fostering a positive, collaborative, and high-performing working environment.
- Oversee food preparation, cooking techniques, and plating standards, ensuring consistency in taste, quality, and presentation throughout every service.
- Assist with menu development, recipe implementation, and the introduction of new dishes while maintaining the restaurant's New York-inspired identity.
- Monitor food costs, stock control, ordering, and waste management to support the efficient operation of the restaurant kitchen.
- Ensure compliance with all hygiene, food safety, and health and safety standards, maintaining a clean, organised , and well-run kitchen environment.
- Collaborate with restaurant management and wider Food & Beverage team to deliver seamless service and memorable guest experiences. Support the training, coaching, and development of kitchen colleagues, helping to build skills and encourage continuous improvement.
- Act as a key ambassador for NYnLON's culinary offering, ensuring every dish reflects the restaurant's quality standards and reputation.

About You

You are an experienced and talented chef with previous experience as a Head Chef, Senior Sous Chef, or similar role within a quality restaurant or luxury hotel restaurant.

You are committed to delivering exceptional food and memorable guest experiences, combining strong culinary expertise with a hands-on approach to kitchen leadership. You enjoy working closely with your team, leading by example during service, and maintaining consistently high standards across every aspect of the operation.

Reporting directly to the Executive Head Chef, you are organised , dependable, and solutions-focused, with a strong understanding of food cost control, kitchen administration, and team development. You thrive in a fast-paced restaurant environment and take pride in creating memorable dining experiences through high-quality food and excellent execution.

Benefits You Will Enjoy As a Head Chef

- 12 complimentary nights a year across Hyatt Hotels worldwide
- Discounted hotel stays across Hyatt not just for you but also your family and friends from the day you start!
- Free meals on duty
- 50% discount on food and beverages when you dine as a guest at selected Hyatt Hotels
- Uniform provided and laundered complimentary
- Headspace membership and access to our Employee Assistance Programme
- Continuous learning and development opportunities to provide you with a clear career path as well as job promotion opportunities across Hyatt Hotels worldwide

At Hyatt, our purpose is to care for people so they can be their best. Guided by our values of Empathy, Integrity, Respect, Inclusion, Experimentation and Wellbeing, we create an environment where colleagues feel supported and empowered to grow.

With more than 1,450 hotels and all-inclusive resorts across over 80 countries, Hyatt offers opportunities to build your career within a global hospitality company featured in Fortune's 100 Best Companies to Work For.

At Hyatt, we open doors and turn jobs into careers. Here, individuality is celebrated, people are supported to thrive, and everyone is empowered to make a meaningful impact.

Next steps: Apply today for this Head Chef role and start your journey with Hyatt Hotels!

title: HE Lecturer in Electrical & Electronic Engineering
description:
Application Deadline: 12 October 2026
Department: Engineering
Location: Graig Campus
Compensation: £26,387 - £48,288 / year

Description

Coleg Sir Gâr is seeking an enthusiastic and innovative HE Lecturer in Electrical & Electronic Engineering to join our growing Engineering team.

This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced engineering professional to deliver high-quality teaching and learning across Further and Higher Education programmes, including Level 4–6 provision. The successful candidate will bring a strong background in Electrical and Electronic Engineering and a passion for developing the next generation of engineers through engaging, industry-focused teaching.

Working closely with colleagues, employers and learners, you will contribute to curriculum development, support learner achievement and help ensure our programmes continue to meet the needs of industry and higher education progression routes.

Applicants should hold a relevant Engineering degree and have experience of teaching within Further and/or Higher Education. Industrial experience within the electrical, electronic or automation sectors and assessor/verifier qualifications would be advantageous.

If you are committed to delivering outstanding learning experiences and want to play a key role in the future development of Engineering at Coleg Sir Gâr, we would welcome your application.

Key Responsibilities

Teaching & Learning Delivery
- Plan, prepare, and deliver high-quality, engaging lectures, tutorials, workshop sessions, and open learning courses across FE and HE levels (up to Level 6).
- Teach a wide-ranging and diverse curriculum, including but not limited to:
- Electrical & Electronic Principles
- Digital and Analogue Electronics & Communications
- Instrumentation & Control Theory
- Mechatronics
- Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs)
- Motors, Drives, and Power Systems
- Power Electronics & Power Systems Modelling
- Electronic Production, Testing, and Products Management
- C Programming & Embedded Systems
- Electronic Design and Simulation
- Engineering Mathematics (for technicians and higher levels)
- Supervision of student Electrical and Electronic Projects

- Contribute to school-linked 14–19 initiatives, essential/key skills development, and elements of the Welsh Baccalaureate.
- Embed digital literacy and industry-relevant software/hardware tools seamlessly into practical sessions.
- Contribute to supporting learners to compete in local, national and international ‘Skills Competitions’.
Assessment & Quality Assurance
- Design, invigilate, and mark assessments, coursework, and examinations in line with awarding body and university partner regulations.
- Provide constructive, timely, and detailed feedback to students to support their academic and professional development.
- Act as an internal quality assurer (IQA) or participate in internal verification, moderation, and quality assurance procedures.
Role of Course Leader, Personal Tutor & Student Support
- Act as a Course Leader for an assigned programme, supporting curriculum planning and ensuring the thorough tracking and monitoring of progress is kept up to date, and the data is accurately evidenced and recorded for exam boards and quality assurance.
- Act as a Personal Tutor to an assigned group of students, fostering strong relationships to help them develop good study habits, security, and responsibility.
- Monitor, discuss, and report on student attendance and progress using the College's database systems.
- Consult and communicate with parents, guardians, and employers regarding student achievement and progress.
- Deliver a College programme of personal studies under the guidance of the Director of Learner Support.
- Offer guidance on personal welfare, referring students to appropriate internal and external specialist agencies when necessary.
- Ensure students are aware of careers and Higher Education guidance, and prepare references for HE or employment.
Institutional & Commercial Engagement
- Work flexibly to meet departmental needs. This includes daytime teaching, scheduled evening teaching sessions, and attendance at promotional events (e.g., Open Evenings, Parents' Evenings, student interviews, and enrolment days).
- Contribute to the development and delivery of commercial, in-company courses, and external projects.
- Support curriculum development within the faculty, college, partner schools, and other educational establishments.
- Effectively manage any resources or equipment allocated within an agreed budget.
- Engage in continuous professional development (CPD), participate in relevant in-service training, and work towards full compliance with National Occupational Standards.
- Implement targets outlined in the bilingual development plan, College equal opportunities policies, and monitor Health & Safety compliance.
- Attend special events annually in support of learner achievements eg Graduation Ceremonies and Awards of Excellence Celebrations.
- When required, participate in community exhibitions to promote engineering courses and careers with ‘have-a-go kits’ or displays.
- On occasion escort learners on trips and educational visits

Skills Knowledge and Expertise

Essential Criteria:
- A relevant Honours Degree (BEng / BSc) in an engineering discipline or a closely related field
- PGCE, Cert Ed, or equivalent recognised teaching qualification. (Candidates without this qualification must obtain a PGCE within 2 years of the employment date, during which the Associate Lecturer Scale will apply).
- GCSE English and Maths at a minimum Grade C or O Level equivalent
- Proven experience teaching Engineering successfully across multiple levels, specifically including both FE and HE up to Level 6. Previous experience at all levels is required.
- A thorough understanding of current relevant issues within Further and Higher Education.
- High level of competence in utilising industry-standard software (e.g. MATLAB/Simulink, MULTISIM, CAD, PLC programming software) and hardware tools for laboratory and practical sessions
- Ability to confidently teach a wide range of modules spanning theory, design, simulation, and practical testing.
- Good communicator with diplomacy and tact
- Good interpersonal and organisational skills
- Ability to work harmoniously with students and colleagues
- Ability to work under pressure and to tight deadlines
- Excellent punctuality and ability to work flexibly
Desirable Criteria:
- Relevant Assessor (A1/TAQA) or Verifier (V1) awards
- Industrial experience within the electrical, electronic, or automation sectors.
- Willingness to drive a college minibus
Welsh Language Requirements:
- Welsh Oracy (Listening/Speaking) - Level 0/1 Desirable
- Welsh Literacy (Writing/Reading) - Level 0/1 Desirable
(See detailed language descriptions attached)

Persons are welcome to apply for posts in Welsh and applications made in Welsh will not be treated less favourably than an application made in English.

Benefits

- You will receive 46 days holiday, plus bank holidays and five closure days which totals at 59 days holiday per year.
- Extremely generous pension scheme with employer contributions of 23.68%.
- Award-winning professional learning and development programme.
- Cycle to work scheme
- Free on-site car parking
- Online and instore retail discounts

Equality, Diversity & Inclusion
At Coleg Sir Gar & Coleg Ceredigion, we inspire learners to fulfil potential and achieve excellence. To do this, we need the best employees to continue our culture of respect, unity and professionalism. We are proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer and therefore welcome applications from all backgrounds and areas of the community to the college.

Visit our dedicated page to find out more.

Disability Confident
Coleg Sir Gar and Coleg Ceredigion are proud to be a disability confident employer. As a result, we ensure our recruitment process is fully inclusive and accessible to all, communicate and promote all opportunities, anticipating and providing reasonable adjustments, support existing employees who acquire a disability or long term health condition to stay in work, and offer an interview to disabled people who meet the minimum criteria for the job.

title: Senior Backend Developer
description:
We’re looking for a Senior Backend Developer who enjoys solving complex problems and building systems that scale. You’ll be part of a tight-knit, cross-functional squad that owns its products from idea to production.

You’ll have the freedom to lead and make technical decisions, the space to experiment, and the support to keep developing your skills. We’ll encourage you to grow into a T-shaped developer, with opportunities to get involved in architecture, DevOps and other areas of development.

We work together in our Liverpool HQ three days a week because we value collaboration, fast feedback and a strong team culture.

Role: Senior Backend Developer

Location: Liverpool City Centre HQ / Hybrid (3 days in office) **

Salary: £65,000–£75,000 depending on experience**

What You’ll Do:

- Build and maintain scalable backend services using .NET 8.0 and Azure
- Write clean, testable and performant code that’s built to last
- Design and implement APIs and database solutions
- Deploy and run services using Docker and Azure Cloud
- Work closely with product owners and designers to bring features to life
- Mentor other developers and help raise the standard across the team
- Share ideas and contribute to how we build and improve our systems

Our Tech Stack:

Backend: C#, .NET 8.0, Mediator, MassTransit

Database: SQL Server, Entity Framework, Redis, Mongo

Infrastructure: Docker, Azure, K8s, RabbitMQ

Monitoring: Grafana, Loki Stack

Tooling: Git, CI/CD pipelines, Unit and Integration Testing, Agile methodologies

It’s a bonus if you’re familiar with Clean Architecture or the Mediator pattern, but curiosity and a willingness to learn are just as valuable.

Engineering Practices:

We care deeply about quality and maintainability.

- We use CI/CD pipelines for fast and reliable deployments
- Automated testing and peer reviews are part of our daily rhythm
- Our systems are monitored with Grafana and Loki, giving full visibility across environments
- We encourage experimentation, retrospectives and continuous improvement in everything we build

What We’re Looking For:

- Solid experience with C#, .NET and Dockerised microservices
- Strong understanding of SQL Server and Entity Framework
- Understanding of event driven architecture and modern microservice patterns
- Experience with testing, CI/CD and cloud deployments
- A team player who enjoys mentoring and collaborating
- A pragmatic problem solver who writes clean, maintainable code
- A genuine desire to learn and help others grow

Why Join Us:

- Modern tech stack and a strong culture of engineering excellence
- A collaborative squad where your ideas make a real impact
- Clear path into technical leadership or architecture
- Freedom to innovate and take ownership
- Top-tier tools and a workspace built for creativity and collaboration

Team and Culture

You’ll be joining a collaborative squad of engineers, designers and product thinkers who enjoy building great software together.

We believe in ownership, curiosity and craftsmanship. Everyone has a voice, and we trust each other to make good decisions. We support one another, share knowledge and celebrate success as a team.

We’re passionate about technology, but even more passionate about building a team that trusts, respects and learns from each other.

Grow with Acorn

At Acorn Insurance, we’re proud of our Liverpool roots — and even prouder of how far we’ve come. As part of the Acorn Group, we bring over 40 years of specialist insurance expertise to the table. From humble beginnings, we’ve grown into a national leader, now employing 1,700+ people across the UK and reached a milestone £750 million in total value of insurance policies written in 2024.

Our Commitment to our colleague’s:

These aren’t just words — they’re the principles we live by. And we’re proud to back them up with real action, earning recognition and accreditation from leading organisations that share our commitment to people and growth:
