title: Registered Nurse
description:
Immacolata House Dementia Nursing Home in Langport is surrounded by the picturesque Somerset countryside. This purpose-built home offers exceptional Dementia and Nursing care for up to 49 residents.

Registered Nurse RGN or RMN Contract

- £23.92 per hour
- Contracted to 36 hours per week
- Paid DBS, pension, uniform provided
- 5.6 weeks annual leave (based on a full time contract)

Ongoing training, clinical updates and funded development, with clear and supported progression into Senior, Clinical Lead and Management roles, within a well led, professional environment where your skills are recognised and developed.

Role Overview

As Registered Nurse, you will play a central role in delivering high quality, clinically led care while taking responsibility for maintaining safe, effective and person centred practice across your shift. This role combines clinical expertise with leadership, ensuring standards are upheld and care is delivered consistently in line with best practice.

You will assess needs, develop and review care plans, administer medication and monitor changes in physical and mental health. Leading shifts, you will support and guide the care team, make informed clinical decisions and respond promptly to changing needs, ensuring continuity and quality of care at all times.

Working closely with residents, families and healthcare professionals, you will use your judgement and experience to maintain high standards, ensure accurate documentation and contribute to a well organised, professional environment where dignity, independence and wellbeing are always prioritised.

What We Are Looking For

- Confidence in leading shifts and supporting a team
- Good communication and leadership skills

About Us

Immacolata House Care Home is part of Care Concern Group, a family owned, market leading care provider with a strong and growing presence across the United Kingdom. We are committed to delivering high quality care and developing supportive, rewarding workplaces where our teams can thrive.

title: Registered Veterinary Nurse
description:
At inspiring vet care, our people are at the heart of everything we do. As the UK’s number one vet care provider, we're trusted with the care of over 2 million animals, delivering our purpose of healthier animals and happier owners.

We are seeking an enthusiastic, team-orientated Registered Veterinary Nurse to join our team at Alpha Vets on a full-time basis.

Since opening in 1996, Alpha Vets has continually invested in providing excellent facilities for both our patients and our team. We’re also excited to be relocating our Risca branch to a brand-new, purpose-built practice at the end of 2026.

How You’ll Make a Difference

As a Registered Veterinary Nurse, you’ll be an integral member of the clinical team, delivering high-quality nursing care while supporting excellent experiences for our clients and patients.

You’ll work collaboratively with Veterinary Surgeons and the wider practice team across our Risca and Langstone sites, taking responsibility for a varied first opinion caseload and contributing to high clinical standards throughout the practice.

Your role will include nurse consultations, weight management clinics, cat clinics, inpatient and kennel care, theatre nursing, dispensary duties and supporting our reception team. You’ll also play an active role in our surgical caseload, including laparoscopic spays and orthopaedic procedures, with opportunities to work with our K-Laser therapy service to support patient rehabilitation and pain management.

Working Pattern

- 38 hours per week
- 4 days per week, 8:00am - 6:30pm
- Either 8 or 9 Saturdays per year, 8:00am - 12:30pm
- No out-of-hours requirement
- Based across our Risca and Langstone sites

Key Responsibilities

- Deliver high standards of nursing care across a varied first opinion caseload
- Run nurse consultations, weight management clinics and cat clinics
- Provide inpatient and kennel nursing care
- Support theatre and surgical procedures, including laparoscopic and orthopaedic cases
- Monitor patients throughout procedures and recovery
- Support dispensary duties and the safe management of medications
- Work with our K-Laser therapy service to support rehabilitation and pain management
- Communicate professionally and compassionately with clients
- Work collaboratively with clinical, nursing and reception colleagues across both sites

You Might Be a Great Fit If...

We’re looking for a confident and motivated Registered Veterinary Nurse who enjoys working as part of a team and delivering high standards of care. You’ll bring:

- Registration as a Veterinary Nurse with the RCVS
- Experience working in clinical practice, with growing confidence in medical and surgical nursing
- Strong communication skills and the ability to build positive relationships with clients and colleagues
- Good organisational skills and the ability to manage your workload effectively
- A proactive approach to learning, reflection and continuous improvement
- A collaborative approach and enthusiasm for contributing across a varied nursing caseload

How We’ll Support You

At inspiring vet care, we’re committed to supporting your ongoing development and wellbeing. When you join us, you’ll benefit from:

- A varied and rewarding nursing role within a supportive primary care environment
- Graduate: Join a dedicated Nurse Graduate Programme designed to build your clinical confidence and support your first steps in practice
- Experienced: Develop your specific nursing interests through subject-specific learning pathways in our dedicated Nurse Academy
- Clear career development with progression opportunities into Senior Nurse, Referral and leadership roles, alongside clinical supervisor, mentoring and certificate pathways
- Ongoing learning and development supported by experienced colleagues and practice teams
- A collaborative, values-led culture focused on care, community and continuous improvement

What We Offer Our Team

- 6.6 weeks' annual leave
- Additional annual leave for your birthday, added to your holiday allowance
- Increasing annual leave accrued through length of service
- Enhanced family-friendly policies, including maternity, paternity, adoption, shared parental and surrogacy pay

- RCVS and VDS fees covered

- Voluntary benefits including Green Cars salary sacrifice scheme and access to discounts and cashback with hundreds of participating retailers

We’re committed to supporting our people through career development opportunities, wellbeing initiatives and access to world-class learning resources.

Whether you’re just starting out or looking to take the next step in your career, inspiring vet care offers the support, opportunity and community to help you grow.

title: Senior Chef
description:
In 2012, Thom & James drove a Piaggio ape Tuk Tuk all the way from Sicily to London on a 'Pilgrimage' to learn the secrets of perfect Italian pizza. They went on to set up a market stall in Soho with an oven in the back of the van before opening their first actual pizzeria on Dean Street. If you think that sounds as ridiculously cool as we do, and you love pizza, then read on…

Nowadays we have over 20 award-winning pizzerias across the UK, we’ve got our own Pizza Academy where we run training workshops every day, and we’re also a BCORP - something we’re extremely proud about achieving. We pride ourselves on using the best ingredients from Naples including Caputo flour, fresh fior di latte, salsiccia e friarielle , to make the best Neapolitan pizza every day.

At Pizza Pilgrims, we aspire to create an inclusive environment where everyone can be themselves, feel genuinely cared for and have equal opportunities for growth and progression. We are committed to building a diverse team that includes and respects a variety of voices, identities, backgrounds, experiences and perspectives; which creates proper happiness, just like our pizzas do!

We work hard because we think pizza makes people happier.

As a Senior Chef, you’ll be a specialist in creating the best Neapolitan Pizza’s, and for every guest to leave with a full belly, and already planning their next visit. You’ll also be accountable for:

- Team leadership.
- Heath & safety compliance.
- Stock management.
- Successful guest pizza launches.
- Kitchen maintenance management.
- Pizza quality.

Whilst skills are important, representing our values is just as important too. These shape our team culture.

- ‘Push Yourself’ because we believe learning new skills and coming out of your comfort zone will help us improve as a team.
- ‘Be Yourself’ means you can bring your own personality to work. Your hair colour is yours, not ours. We think tattoos are cool. And we love hearing about your interests outside of work.
- ‘Respect Others’ because everyone is welcome at Pilgrims and we’re committed to creating an inclusive environment where people feel they belong.
- ‘Enjoy Yourself’ because hospitality is an industry we love, and we want every Pilgrim to create happiness for each other and to have fun at work.

What's in it for you?

- £14.95 ph +tronc.
- Serious career development - We are opening 5 pizzerias this year & next.
- On top of the standard 28 days holiday (full time), you will get an extra day for every year you work for us (up to 5 Years).

Some of our favourite Pizza Perks include...

- 1 extra day holiday as “Happiness Day’ so you can do something that you love and makes you happy about outside of work.
- Team trips to Naples & beyond to meet suppliers & try new pizzerias
- A tasty bonus every time you refer a friend to join.
- Free food & espresso every day - whole menu available & also deals with other restaurants
- A free after-work drinks (soft, beer or gin)
- 2 huge company-wide parties every year to celebrate Christmas and Ferragosto (We close all the pizzerias for these!)

title: Group Financial Accountant
description:
Group Accountant

Location: Castleford, West Yorkshire

Salary: £60,000–£70,000 + benefits

Working pattern: Hybrid – up to two days per week from home

PTSG has grown rapidly through acquisition and now comprises more than 40 specialist businesses operating across five divisions. We are looking for an accomplished Group Accountant who can bring strong technical accounting knowledge and immediately take ownership of several critical Group finance processes.

This is not a developmental position. We need a fully qualified accountant with a strong track record in group accounting, consolidation and financial reporting who is comfortable working independently within a large, complex organisation.

Based within our Central Group Finance team, you will manage the monthly consolidation process, fixed assets and VAT returns while supporting statutory reporting, acquisition accounting and the year-end audit. You will also help standardise accounting practices across the Group, strengthen financial controls and improve how our systems and processes operate.

The role offers considerable exposure across PTSG’s subsidiaries and provides the opportunity to influence accounting standards and processes throughout a growing, acquisition-led business.

What You’ll Be Doing

- Managing the monthly Group consolidation process, including consolidation adjustments.
- Driving a timely, controlled and accurate period-end close.
- Managing the Group’s fixed assets and reviewing the associated reconciliations.
- Ensuring central accounting transactions relating to tax, insurance, professional fees and investments are recorded accurately.
- Completing or reviewing assigned balance sheet reconciliations.
- Preparing and submitting VAT returns.
- Supporting technical accounting matters and the implementation of the Group accounting manual.
- Assisting with acquisition accounting as new businesses join the Group.
- Acting as a key contact for the external audit and supporting the preparation of two sets of consolidated accounts.
- Assisting with unaudited statutory accounts across the Group.
- Working with professional advisers on consolidated corporation tax calculations.
- Reviewing and improving accounting processes and financial controls.
- Identifying opportunities to improve the use of Sage and other finance systems.
- Supporting wider finance projects and process improvements.

What We’re Looking For

This position requires someone who can operate confidently from the outset and take responsibility for complex Group accounting activities with limited supervision.

You will need:

- A recognised accounting qualification – ACA, ACCA or CIMA.
- A strong track record in group accounting within a large, multi-entity organisation or centralised Group finance function.
- Hands-on responsibility for monthly consolidations and Group reporting.
- Strong technical accounting knowledge and the ability to apply it in practice.
- A sound understanding of balance sheet controls, statutory reporting and audit requirements.
- The ability to establish and improve accounting processes and controls.
- The confidence to work independently, manage competing deadlines and challenge existing practices when necessary.
- Strong communication skills and the ability to work effectively with finance teams across multiple businesses.

Knowledge of acquisition accounting, intercompany recharges, Sage or OneStream would be beneficial.

What’s In It For You

- Salary of £60,000–£70,000.
- Hybrid working, with up to two days per week from home.
- 25 days’ holiday plus bank holidays.
- Life assurance at three times your salary.
- Salary sacrifice pension scheme.
- 24/7 online GP service.
- Discounts on shopping, technology, holidays, meals out, gyms and more.
- Free on-site parking.

Our open-plan Castleford head office is approximately five minutes’ walk from the train station, close to the M62 and A1, and has on-site parking.

About PTSG

PTSG Group is a leading provider of specialist services across the UK and Europe.

Through the acquisition of high-quality specialist businesses, PTSG has built a group of industry-leading companies delivering services across Access and Safety, Electrical Services, Building Access, Fire Solutions and Water Treatment.

With approximately 4,000 specialists supporting more than 90,000 customers across 200,000 buildings and delivering over 170 different services, we are committed to providing safe, compliant and high-quality services nationwide.

Our aim is simple: to be a great place to work and a great company to do business with.

Armed Forces Covenant

PTSG Group is proud to support the Armed Forces community and has formally signed the UK Armed Forces Covenant.

We recognise the valuable skills that service leavers, veterans, reservists and military families bring to the workplace, including leadership, teamwork, resilience and technical expertise.

We guarantee an interview to ex-Forces applicants who meet the minimum criteria for the role and are committed to supporting Armed Forces personnel in building long-term civilian careers across our business.

PTSG Group is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive and supportive workplace where everyone is treated fairly and with respect. We welcome applications from all backgrounds and are dedicated to promoting diversity, equality and inclusion throughout our recruitment process and across the wider business.

title: HGV Class C Driver
description:
Overview

HGV Class C Driver

At Solus, all roles are critical in delivering quality repairs for our customers and keeping our workshops moving. As we continue to invest in our future and strengthen our operational capability, we’re looking for a HGV Class C driver.

This role is ideal for someone who understands the pace and pressure of an accident repair environment and takes pride in organisation, accuracy and supporting members of the wider team.

Responsibilities

What you’ll be doing

Our HGV drivers are kept busy in this role to get our customers back on the road quickly. We'd love you bring your previous experience to this role. You will work within a team of other drivers reporting to your Transport Controller

As a Class C HGV Driver, we want you to bring your previous experience to the team. You will collect and deliver vehicles before and after repair, working to deadlines to meet our customer's needs.

This will include

- You will have responsibility for collecting and delivering cars within the agreed timescales, ensuring that the customer receives the very best possible service on collection and delivery of their car, ensuring all cash and credit card transactions are accounted for and that all transactions are processed following company procedures.
- You will complete forms to indicate any damage on the car and specify accident-related damage and highlight any old damage, take digital photographs - and gain a signature from the customer.
- You will highlight any defects identified during loading/unloading of vehicles or as identified at the handover of the vehicle to the customer and bring to the attention of the Production Manager.
- You will also ensure all jobs are referenced and filed on completion of job.

Qualifications

Who we’re looking for

- All roles are at the heart of our business, and you'll need be enthusiastic, upbeat and committed to delivering the best repair service.
- You would have previous experience in a similar role with the following skills
- You will have experience driving HGV class 2 vehicles and within recovery.
- You will be very customer-focused and have great customer handling skills.

Solus, who are owned by Aviva, are one of the UK leaders in vehicle repairs, returning cars to the road in just 11 days on average and a 4.6/5 star customer rating. With an award-winning apprenticeship programme and winners of other recognised industry awards Solus are proud to be shaping the future of vehicle repair.

Why Join Solus?

We have so much to offer when it comes to being a Solus colleague:

- Competitive salary based on location, skills, experience, and qualifications.
- Bonus opportunity tied to your performance and the overall success of Solus.
- Company pension scheme with employer contributions.
- 33 days’ holiday (including bank holidays), with the option to buy or sell up to 5 days.
- Save money with up to 40% discount on Aviva products and other retailer discounts.
- Share in Aviva’s success through the Aviva Save As You Earn scheme.
- Supportive policies including parental and carer’s leave.
- Wellbeing focus with tools like Group Income Protection and 24/7 GP access.

We guarantee an interview for disabled applicants meeting the minimum criteria—just email us after applying to let us know.

Ready to join us? Apply online today, and our team will be in touch within 14 days.

description:
*Salary - Up to £58,000 per year*

JKS Restaurants and Plaza Khao Gaeng are seeking a Head Chef to lead their kitchen operations. The successful candidate will have a passion for Thai/Asian cuisine and have previous experience as a Head Chef.

This is a fantastic opportunity for an experienced Head Chef looking for a new role in an award winning, critically acclaimed group

### The Restaurant

Plaza Khao Gaeng celebrates Thailand’s coast-to-jungle cooking through the tradition of khao gaeng, broadly translated as “curry over rice”. Expect a kaleidoscope of curries rich with fresh coconut milk, aromatic curry pastes and fermented seasonings, alongside searingly hot stir-fries cooled with fresh herbs - all designed for mixing, matching and sharing.

In Thailand, the most popular khao gaeng restaurants expand to fill whatever space they can. Plaza takes inspiration from one such spot in Bangkok, now spread through an old cinema, where curries sit in gleaming trays beneath a faded façade and climb the stairs to the former box office. This is anytime comfort food: a pause from the heat, noise and movement of the street outside.

Our third Plaza Khao Gaeng opened in Covent Garden in May, turning to Thailand’s deep south - the historic borderlands of Pattani, Yala, Narathiwat and beyond. Anchored by a large charcoal grill, the menu draws together smoke, spice and acidity in a generous, khao gaeng-style spread made for the table - our most Southern menu yet, inspired by rural kitchens.

### The Position

As Head Chef, you will be responsible for ensuring the delivery of consistent, high quality and innovative dishes and specials; you will play a key role in menu development, working closely with the Group Exec Chef and Chef Director. You will manage the overall kitchen operation, including prep schedules, stock control, budgeting and maintenance, as well as the day to day management of the kitchen team.

If you have the following, then we want to hear from you:

- Previous experience as a Head Chef or Senior Sous Chef in a high quality restaurant;

Within Care and Rehabilitation Services, the philosophy of our prisons is to rehabilitate offenders and equip them to re-integrate into mainstream society on release. The prisoners in your care will have a variety of different needs and it will be your role to ensure those individuals are treated with dignity and respect and helped to find a new way of life whilst maintaining a safe, secure and structured environment.

title: Financial Accountant
description:
Financial Accountant
Full-time, Permanent
Hybrid | Salford Quays, Manchester | 2 days per week in the office

The Role

The Financial Accountant is part of the Financial Control team within the wider Bupa Dental Care Finance function. This role is responsible for supporting day-to-day accounting activities, with a particular focus on financial control, reporting, audit and compliance across a portfolio of legal entities.

You'll play a key role in the month-end and quarter-end reporting cycle, ensuring the accurate reporting of profit and loss, balance sheet and cashflow information in line with accounting standards and principles. You'll also support the Senior Financial Accountants with external and internal audits, statutory accounts submissions across 135 legal entities, and corporation tax and VAT activities.

What You'll Be Doing

- Supporting monthly and quarterly reporting activities, ensuring deadlines are met, including balance sheet and cashflow reporting, IFRS submissions and Solvency II requirements.
- Working closely with Senior Financial Accountants to ensure the end-to-end reporting cycle is completed, reconciled and reported in line with month-end timetables.
- Preparing reconciliations and supporting balance sheet reviews, ensuring reporting is accurate, compliant and supported by appropriate documentation.
- Validating accruals, prepayments, provisions and related charges, maintaining robust supporting evidence and escalating any issues where required.
- Supporting the completion of corporation tax and VAT returns.
- Assisting with the preparation of statutory accounts, responding to audit queries and providing supporting documentation.
- Maintaining and running the depreciation cycle.
- Supporting the implementation and ongoing maintenance of financial controls, reconciliations and reporting processes across the business.

What We're Looking For

- Part-qualified or newly qualified accountant (ACA/ICAEW or ACCA).
- Strong financial accounting knowledge, including a solid understanding of double-entry accounting principles.
- Experience working to tight deadlines and managing multiple priorities.
- Strong analytical and numerical skills with excellent attention to detail.
- Advanced IT skills, including Excel and financial systems. Experience of Oracle would be advantageous.
- Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with a customer-focused approach.
- The ability to build and maintain effective working relationships across the business.
- A proactive mindset, with a willingness to learn and adapt to changing business needs.
- A positive, can-do attitude and a strong sense of ownership.
- Commercial awareness and a commitment to ongoing professional development.

Benefits

The benefits here are industry-leading, and we’ll be able to tell you more about them in the process (or jump to the benefits and rewards page on our careers site for a flavour). But here’s a snapshot:

- 25 days holiday, plus the option to buy more.

- Early access to your earned wages through Wagestream.

title: Registered Nurse Band 5 - Sulis Ward
description:

As a Registered Nurse Band 5 you will be part of our valued team in our Sulis Ward at St Martins Hospital Bath team, receiving access to exclusive rewards and benefits including:

- Band 5 AfC Salary with NHS Pension and full Agenda for Change terms and conditions
- Membership of My Reward Hub, giving you access to discounts on every day purchases like grocery shopping as well as cashback and voucher offers for treats for you and those special to you
- Access to your wages as you earn them to help cover life’s emergencies and avoid overdraft fees or high interest rates
- Online and face to face help with your mental and physical wellbeing – from healthy recipes and activity challenges through to post trauma support, legal, debt and life management help, as well career coaching and counselling
- Access to eLearning, bespoke career pathways and opportunities for continuing professional development through our ‘Outstanding’ learning and development team, The Learning Enterprise
- An open, just culture where you’re encouraged to have and implement ideas which can help us deliver our purpose: changing lives through transforming health and care – backed up by at least £100,000 of ringfenced innovation funding each year
- The pride of working for an organisation committed to the highest clinical and quality standards: with the majority of our rated services holding “good” or “outstanding” ratings from the Care Quality Commission

Job Introduction

We have an exciting opportunity for a Registered Band 5 Nurse to join our team at St Martin's Hospital, Sulis Ward.

In this role, you will play a crucial part in the provision of high-quality patient care by assessing care needs, developing, implementing, and evaluating care programs. You will demonstrate the ability to perform all relevant forms of nursing care competently without direct supervision, ensuring the highest standards of quality and safety .

Additionally, the role involves active participation in teaching, supervision, and preceptorship/mentorship of learners and other staff and in the absence of a more senior nurse, the post holder will take charge of the ward.

Whether you are a compassionate and experienced Band 5 Nurse committed to excellence or a motivated, we invite you to apply for this rewarding opportunity .

Does this sound like something that would interest you? If you are interested or would like further information please contact: Jessica Bowler

Recruitment Advisor: Louise Ledward on 07884 659608 or

We are happy to answer any questions that you may have.

Main Responsibilities

- To provide and be responsible for the assessment of care needs, the development, implementation and evaluation of programmes of care.
- To carry out all relevant forms of care competently without direct supervision.
- Communicate with members of the multidisciplinary team to facilitate continuity of care and promote effective team working.
- To participate in the teaching, supervision and preceptorship/mentorship of learners and other staff.
- Take charge of the ward in the absence of a more senior nurse.
- The post holder will work in partnership with the Ward / Department Sister to ensure that the standards of nursing care are met at all times. This includes assisting the ward / department Sister and the whole team to meet the agreed standards of hospital cleanliness within the work environment.

The Ideal Candidate

Essential

- Registered Nurse
- Must have UK NHS experience working on a ward
- Willing to undergo training as necessary
- Ability to demonstrate and explain skills to other staff
- Knowledge of current issues in health care
- Standards of Professional Practice
- Good verbal and written skills
- Ability to organise and prioritise workload
- Understanding of skills and knowledge required to develop team members
- Enthusiastic and self-motivated
- Committed to working with people
- Flexible and adaptable
- Ability to work as part of a team
- Demonstrate a commitment to self-development

Desirable

- Mentorship qualification
- Awareness of speciality
- Capable of lateral thinking

About The Company

We change lives by transforming health and care.

Established in 2006, we are one of the UK's leading independent providers of community health and care services, working with health and care commissioners and communities to transform services with a focus on experience, efficiency, and improved outcomes. We deliver and transform adult and children community health services, primary care services including urgent care, sexual health, dermatology and MSK services as well as adult social care and wellbeing services. Across England, we support communities of many millions and directly help more than half a million people each year - guided by our simple values: we care, we think, we do .

We're committed to equal opportunities and welcome applications from a broad, diverse range of people who want to join our team. We’re a Disability Confident Committed company, so we work to provide facilities, work environment adjustments and technical solutions to be as inclusive of everyone .

While it doesn’t happen often, sometimes a role is very popular, and we’ll need to close it earlier than the date we’ve shown here. If you’re keen to join our team, we’d love to hear from you so please apply as soon as you can.

If you would like to know a little more about how we use your information, please see our website's privacy policy.

Company Information

Oak Furnitureland launched in 2006. Our brand was built on ensuring our customers could access high-quality hardwood furniture at affordable prices, and we were predominantly known for our range of well-crafted cabinetry.

Fast-forward to today, and you’ll discover our commitment to using quality materials and creating furniture built to last hasn’t changed. We still offer great value for money, too, but what you’ll discover now is an evolution that’s seen us expand our categories and styles of furniture so that we can offer something for every home.

Not only do we offer fantastic pieces of furniture for the home, but we are also a great place to work. It is one where colleagues are valued, feel connected to the business, and are provided with an environment where they can flourish, contribute, and develop their careers.

To Support Us, We Are Guided By Our Company's Purpose Of ‘helping People Make Their House a Real Home’, Which Is Underpinned By Our Values

- We are adaptable
- We are experts

- We put our customers first.

Equal Opportunities Employer

Our mission is to build an open and inclusive work environment where all colleagues have equal opportunity and access to development, progression and growth. We strive to recruit and retain diverse talent representative of our customer demographic.

We have an inclusive environment where everyone can be themselves and are driven by the same purpose and values. As we endeavour to create a workplace that reflects our diverse customer base and the communities in which we live and work, we strongly encourage applications from individuals belonging to minority and underrepresented groups. We are committed to fairness in the way we hire new colleagues, and if you require any additional support to help you through the process, we’re happy to make the necessary adjustments for anyone who needs them.

title: Senior Financial Accountant
description:
Senior Financial Accountant - Europe East Region - Cheshire (near Manchester Airport)

We're hiring on behalf of a US multinational scientific instruments and technology business with a significant and growing European presence. This is a hands-on senior accounting role with real end-to-end ownership, not a support function with a vague remit.

Please note: a car and full driving licence are essential. The office is in regional Cheshire - easily reached from Manchester, Stockport, Macclesfield, Alderley Edge and the wider Cheshire and Greater Manchester commuter belt, and adjacent to Manchester Airport.

The role: You'll take full responsibility for US GAAP and statutory accounting across one to two legal entities within the Europe East region, own the audit process end-to-end for your entities, and drive harmonisation of accounting activities across the broader region. You'll work closely with regional and global finance stakeholders - internal teams, external auditors and local tax authorities - and be expected to identify process improvements rather than wait to be told where they are.

What you'll actually be doing:

• Full US GAAP and statutory accounting responsibility for one to two legal entities - accruals, prepaids, local tax accounting, trial balance reviews, clearings and reclassifications
• Acting as primary point of contact for internal and external audits for your entities, end-to-end, not just providing schedules
• Owning intercompany reconciliations across the entire Europe East region
• Executing daily and monthly regional accounting - fixed and demo asset management, recurring journal entries, P&L reviews, cost centre control, T&E accounts and stock count coordination
• Preparing and completing BlackLine reconciliations for entities within the region
• Collaborating with Finance, AP, Tax, Country and Regional leadership, and with external partners including Big 4 audit firms and local tax authorities
• Participating in and driving local, regional and global finance projects, with real scope to lead harmonisation and efficiency initiatives

What we need:

• Master's degree in Finance, Accounting or a related field
• Solid senior-level accounting experience in an international environment
• US GAAP knowledge - a core technical requirement, not a nice-to-have
• Fluent English and either Hungarian or Polish, written and spoken to a high professional standard. One of these two languages is non-negotiable for this role
• Hands-on SAP experience
• Strong Excel skills - you'll be in it daily
• Full driving licence and access to a car - the office location requires it
• Self-motivated, comfortable using your own initiative to improve processes rather than waiting to be directed
• A genuine team player who can build relationships across internal and external partners in a complex, multi-stakeholder environment

Nice to have:

• Experience with BlackLine
• Additional European languages
• Previous experience in a US-listed multinational, or a Big 4 practice background

The reality of the role: this is genuine end-to-end ownership of accounting across a multinational's European entities, not a task-based role where someone else sets the priorities. You'll deal directly with Big 4 auditors, tax authorities and regional leadership. The language requirement is real - candidates without fluent Hungarian or Polish will not be progressed.

Cheshire - hybrid, office-based three days per week. Adjacent to Manchester Airport. Own transport essential.

You must have the right to work in the United Kingdom to be considered.

title: Warehouse Manager
description:
Defence Munitions Beith, Beith, Ayrshire KA15 1JT

Job Summary

At Defence Equipment & Support (DE&S), we supply and maintain vital equipment and services for the Royal Navy, British Army and Royal Air Force. Together, we deliver a vast range of essential defence programmes, and strive for what's next. Because it helps keep our military at the top of their game and our nation safe – for today, and tomorrow.

DE&S has recently been integrated into the National Armaments Director (NAD) Group. The NAD Group brings together key Ministry of Defence (MOD) organisations to unite expertise across science, technology, procurement, infrastructure, and support to provide integrated capabilities faster and more efficiently for our armed forces and our allies. This is an exciting new opportunity to enable better ways of working and empower greater collaboration across Defence. For further information about the NAD Group, please visit: National Armaments Director Group - GOV.UK

We offer 25+ days’ holiday, flexible and hybrid working, enhanced parental leave schemes, shopping discounts, and an exceptional employer pension contribution of 28.97%, to help make work work for you.

This role requires you to have lived in the UK for the last 5 years and obtain Security Check (SC) security clearance. Clearance must be obtained without any caveats that prevent you from carrying out the role you’ve been recruited for. If it isn’t obtained, or is obtained but with caveats that prevent you from carrying out the role, any conditional offer made to you will be withdrawn. Obtaining SC security clearance can be a lengthy process, and we reserve the right to withdraw any conditional offer made if the necessary security clearance isn’t obtained within 12 months.

Job Description

As a Warehouse Manager within Defence Munitions, you will lead the safe, secure and efficient management of weapons, explosives and associated equipment that support UK Defence operations across the globe. You will be accountable for the end-to-end management of warehouse activities, including the receipt, inspection, storage, maintenance, accounting, distribution and disposal of high-value and highly regulated inventory. This includes ensuring that mechanical handling equipment and munitions are available, serviceable and ready to meet operational demands while maintaining strict compliance with safety, security, environmental and transport regulations.

You will lead teams of warehouse operatives, providing clear direction, coaching and performance management to deliver operational outputs safely and effectively. The role carries responsibility for planning of weapon selection and transportation, balancing customer requirements, workforce capacity, storage constraints and operational priorities to ensure delivery against demanding timescales. You will have direct responsibility for the safe operation of warehouse, explosives storage facilities, acting as a custodian for infrastructure and equipment.

A key aspect of the role is maintaining the physical and financial accountability of Defence inventory. You will ensure stock records are accurate, audit requirements are met, logistics information systems are maintained correctly, and inventory movements are processed in a timely manner. You will lead investigations into stock discrepancies, losses and anomalies, identify root causes and implement corrective actions to maintain confidence in inventory integrity.

Working within a highly regulated environment, you will be responsible for ensuring all activities are conducted in accordance with explosives safety regulations, dangerous goods legislation, quality management requirements, health and safety standards and security policies. This includes assessing operational risks, developing and implementing safe systems of work, assuring workforce competence, investigating incidents and accidents, and embedding lessons learned to drive continual improvement. The role requires sound judgement and the ability to make operational decisions that balance safety, compliance, customer requirements and business performance.

You will collaborate extensively with delivery teams, engineers, supply chain specialists, customers, suppliers and senior leaders across Defence, providing authoritative advice on munitions management, logistics operations, ammunition safety and inventory governance. You may represent Defence Munitions at safety panels, project reviews and stakeholder forums, contributing specialist expertise to support future capability, operational readiness and risk management activities.

On appointment into this role, you must be willing to undertake the National Occupational Standards (NOS) qualification.

Please note that this is a 37 hour a week full-time role and carried out fully on-site 5 days a week.

What You’ll Be Doing

- Lead and develop teams delivering receipt, storage, maintenance and issue activities for Weapons Ordnance Munitions and Explosives (WOME).
- Manage complex warehouse operations, ensuring delivery against operational priorities and customer requirements.
- Act as the focal point for safety, security and compliance within your area of responsibility.
- Lead risk assessments and implement safe systems of work in highly regulated environments.
- Manage operational facilities, ensuring compliance with explosives, health and safety, environmental and security regulations.
- Provide expert advice to customers, stakeholders and senior managers on WOME logistics and operational activities.
- Drive continuous improvement through effective planning, problem solving and performance management.
- Lead investigations into incidents, inventory discrepancies and operational issues, ensuring lessons are identified and embedded.
- Support major operational activities, including those involving the Front-Line Commands (FLCs) and large scale complex-weapons.

title: Trainee Maths Teacher (Initial Teacher Training) - Salaried route (P850)
description:
Start your teacher training journey with Lift Schools: Train to teach Maths

Are you looking to become a Maths Teacher and start a rewarding career in education?

Our school-based Initial Teacher Training (ITT) programme gives you the opportunity to learn directly in the classroom, supported by experienced teachers and mentors. Delivered in partnership with Ark Teacher Training, the salaried route let's you earn while you learn whilst working towards your Postgraduate Certificate in Education (PGCE) and Qualified Teacher Status (QTS).

You will spend the majority of your time gaining practical classroom experience, putting pedagogical theory into practice, and building your teaching confidence throughout the school year.

Programme key details

- Role title: Trainee Maths Teacher (Salaried route)
- Qualifications earned: Postgraduate Certificate in Education (PGCE) & Qualified Teacher Status (QTS)
- Programme duration: 1 Year (Full-time)
- Key dates: Summer School (2 – 13 August 2027)

Why choose our Initial Teacher Training Programme?

Our school-based teacher training gives you the perfect balance of practical classroom experience and expert academic grounding:

- No tuition fees: On the Salaried route, your university fees are already paid
- Practical classroom experience: Gain hands-on teaching practice as an unqualified Maths teacher, backed by dedicated 1-on-1 mentoring.
- Fully supported progression: Your personal tutor and in-school coach guide you as you gradually take on more independent teaching responsibility.
- Network & community: Spend half a day every week in dedicated training sessions alongside fellow trainees from across the Ark Teacher Training and Lift Schools networks.

What The Teacher Training Programme Includes

Two-week Summer School (August 2027)

Prepare for your training year with two weeks of focused learning. Our Summer School (2 – 13 August 2027) helps you enter the classroom with a strong foundation in educational theory, lesson planning, and behaviour management.

Personalised mentoring & coaching

You will never feel on your own. A dedicated subject tutor and in-school mentor provide ongoing advice, weekly feedback, and tailored career support.

Targeted weekly training

Weekly training modules enhance the practical teaching skills you apply in the classroom every day.

Nationwide support network

Connect with current trainees and alumni across our 62 schools nationwide. As part of Lift Schools, you will benefit from a collaborative peer network throughout your training year and into your Early Career Framework (ECF) years.

Recognised PGCE & QTS Qualifications

Graduate with both a Postgraduate Certificate of Education (PGCE) and Qualified Teacher Status (QTS).

Eligibility Requirements

To be eligible for our Maths Teacher Training, applicants must meet the following criteria:

- Degree: An undergraduate degree with a 2:2 classification or above (or equivalent) by the start of the programme. A degree in Maths, STEM, (or a related field) is preferred. Alternatively, a strong A-Level in Maths (Grade C or above) will be considered.
- GCSEs: Grade 4 (C) or above in GCSE English & Mathematics (or equivalent).
- Status: Right to live and work in the UK for the duration of the training year.
- Teaching status: Must not currently hold Qualified Teacher Status (QTS).

About Our School

Lift Broadlands is a small school with an inclusive approach where every child is ‘known and nurtured' across our community. Our smallness is our strength with us having the ability to do whole school assemblies and whole school enrichment within the school day. Our size gives us the chance to come together as much as possible and means that children are truly known as individuals. This leads to strong relationships across all members of the community ensuring our students are happy, safe and successful.

Our commitment to equal opportunities

We are committed to building a diverse teaching workforce reflecting the communities we serve. We provide robust support systems to ensure every trainee teacher reaches their full potential regardless of background.

Ready to train to teach?

Take the first step toward a rewarding career in education. Join our Maths Teacher Training Programme:

Apply today

title: Electrical Engineer or Senior Engineer - Birmingham
description:
Electrical Engineer or Senior Engineer

Birmingham

About Us

Hoare Lea is a human-centric and planet-conscious engineering consultancy. We offer intelligent and sustainable solutions to complex design challenges for the built environment throughout the UK and further afield.

We provide a wide range of engineering and consultancy services, including acoustics, air quality, building services (MEP), fire, lighting, security and sustainability to name but a few. Together, our highly skilled teams use technical expertise and problem-solving skills to bring buildings to life. We ensure that whatever the building, its design is outstanding, and its operations meet the needs of the communities it serves.

We are as committed to providing an environment where everyone can realise their unique potential. So, in joining Hoare Lea, you will experience a business that enriches your knowledge, supports your wellbeing, and welcomes your individuality. You’ll have the opportunity to participate in our 9-day fortnight scheme, thriving community groups, varied social and networking events, and extensive professional and technical development schemes. We also offer an extensive benefits package, including private medical cover, an electric vehicle salary sacrifice scheme, stock options, and 25 days of annual leave (increasing with service), alongside flexible and hybrid working.

Whatever your ambitions or circumstances, our aim is to enable everyone to develop their knowledge, give their best, and enjoy what they do.

About The Role

We have an opportunity for an Electrical Engineer or Senior Engineer to play a key role in delivering high quality, sustainable electrical engineering solutions across multiple projects in the built environment.

Hoare Lea is a market-leading built environment consultancy with a proud history stretching back 162 years to our roots in Birmingham. Today we focus on delivering high-quality consultancy that addresses the issues our clients care about most. We’re looking for people who want to help shape the future, enjoy tackling complex challenges, and want their work to make a tangible difference to the communities where they live.

Are you ready to get stuck in?

You will own project deliverables, manage elements of the internal delivery team, and liaise with multidisciplinary colleagues, clients and contractors to ensure holistic, compliant and commercially aware solutions. You will typically lead defined elements and smaller projects (Engineer) or take full lead responsibility for larger schemes and broader client engagement (Senior Engineer). You will be helping to develop junior staff and foster relationships that support future business growth.

In this key and varied role, you can expect to:

- Take briefs and deliver electrical design work from inception through to completion.
- Produce electrical calculations, drawings and technical documentation that comply with relevant regulations, design guides and client standards.
- Ensure quality standards and technical accuracy across deliverables.
- Coordinate electrical design with other disciplines (MEP and our specialist groups) and third‑party consultants.
- Review and comment on technical information provided by contractors and sub‑contractors; check site installations against the design intent.
- Attend and report at design team meetings, client meetings and project meetings.
- Witness selected testing and commissioning activities and support handover documentation.
- Manage own workload to meet programme deliverables and report progress to your line manager.
- Contribute to the professional development of junior colleagues.

Additional Responsibilities For Senior Engineer

- Develop briefs and take responsibility for delivering a small project or the electrical discipline on a significant/complex scheme.
- Exercise considerable autonomy and take ownership for technical decisions and project delivery within cost constraints.
- Delegate, manage and check work undertaken by others; mentor and motivate colleagues across project teams.
- Play an active role in commercial aspects (scope, risk, cost control) and ensure outputs meet project and budgetary requirements.

About You

To be successful in this role you’ll need:

- Degree or equivalent in Electrical/Building Services Engineering; industry membership preferred.
- Working towards or holding IEng/CEng.
- Strong technical competence in LV distribution, lighting, earthing/protection and emergency/standby systems; able to produce calculations and drawings.
- Proficient with industry software (Revit, AutoCAD, Dialux, OM Electrical) and MS Office.
- Able to work independently: deliver an element of a project (Engineer) or lead discipline/small projects and larger schemes (Senior).
- Effective communicator with experience coordinating multidisciplinary teams and liaising with clients/contractors.
- Experience of site checking, witnessing testing/commissioning and reviewing contractor submissions.
- Demonstrable commitment to meeting programmes and quality standards; commercially aware.
- Supportive team player who mentors junior staff and pursues continuous professional development (Senior expected to supervise; Engineer to support).

How To Apply

To apply simply complete a CV profile and submit your application, or for further information please contact jessicamartin@hoarelea.com.

If shortlisted, one of our recruitment team will be in touch to arrange an introductory call (about 30 minutes) to discuss the role and your experience in more detail. From there, successful candidates will be invited to attend a panel interview, either via Microsoft Teams or in person at one of our offices. We aim to provide feedback at each stage of the process.

Adjustments and accommodations

If there are adjustments or accommodations that we can put in place to help you participate and give your best at any stage of the recruitment process (whether relating to disability, neurodivergence or anything else) please let us know.

Data privacy

We have updated our terms and conditions for candidates, click here to find out more.

Recruitment agencies

We have a Preferred Supplier List of trusted partners who assist us when required. We do not acknowledge speculative CVs or unsolicited candidate introductions from agencies not on the list.

title: Bid Manager
description:
Ready for a new challenge?

Are you looking for work that makes a difference? Do you want to work with people who learn and grow together? If so, Opencast could be the place for you. We’re a growing tech consultancy that creates user-centred solutions with purpose for our clients in government and business.

The role

We’re looking for a Bid Manager to join the Opencast Bid Team. The ideal candidate will have experience managing proposals across the procurement lifecycle, from EOI/RFI though to ITT. Opencast works with both public sector and private sector clients, so an understanding of Government frameworks and/or private sector procurement will be helpful.

The role will involve planning and co-ordinating the end-to-end delivery of proposal responses of varying size, complexity and value. This will involve working in collaboration with colleagues across the wider Opencast team and partner organisations to manage, prepare, format and submit winning proposals.

You’ll need to take the lead running key sessions including kick-offs, storyboarding, reviews, signoff and bid retros, so you should also have experience in working with a range of contributors and stakeholders, and leading activities across the bidding lifecycle.

In addition to proposal management, you will also have an opportunity to get involved in presentations and continuous improvement activities, which will involve leading on and contributing to process improvements.

Essential experience

We’ll want you to demonstrate experience in bid management, with strong time management, attention to detail and communication skills, and a good understanding of the procurement lifecycle. You don’t need to have had the job title of bid manager before, and we encourage applications from candidates that can demonstrate those core skills.

In your CV and interview, please show you have:

- Worked within a busy bid team across public and/or private sectors.
- Led key sessions such as bid kick-offs, storyboarding, quality gate reviews, and retros.
- Developed bid templates, trackers, and storyboards to support structured bid responses.
- Managed relationships within the bid team and across the organisation.
- Successfully organised and delivered bids within tight timescales.

As well as bid management experience, there are essential core skills you’ll need to excel in this role.

In the interview, please show how you:

- Develop bid strategies based on client requirements.
- Review and analyse client documents to identify key requirements and deliverables.
- Gather and submit clarification questions, and keep the team updated.
- Review, provide feedback on, and format bid responses effectively.
- Coordinate multiple priorities in parallel, with excellent organisation and attention to detail.
- Coach bid teams on best practices and ensure quality.
- Demonstrate strong written and verbal communication skills, with a natural ability to lead and collaborate.

In the interview, we’ll ask you to describe how you approach bid management, deliver successful proposals, and engage stakeholders. If you’re successful in the first interview, we’ll invite you back to meet with colleagues that you will be working with outside of the bid team, which will give you an insight into the stakeholders that you would typically collaborate on bids with.

Desirable experience

- Experience with Public Sector Frameworks such as DOS, G-Cloud, and Technology Services
- Responding to proposed commercial scenarios and preparing rate cards

Salary

Salary range for this role: £50,000-£65,000

What we offer

A competitive package including a 7% employer pension contribution, share options, and a discretionary bonus. You’ll also benefit from 25 days’ holiday and access to 3 annual “life happens” days to support unexpected situations. We provide wellbeing support, ongoing professional development, volunteering opportunities, and the chance to be part of a genuinely supportive team.

Where you’ll work

Your working time at Opencast will be split between multiple locations, including from our HQ and hub locations, client site or home. Travel across the UK is part of life at Opencast. This varies in frequency, and takes into account requirements of your work, our clients and your team.

We include you

We welcome candidates from all identities, attributes, ways of thinking and backgrounds to thrive in a career at Opencast. Our aim is for the diversity of our people to be reflected in the solutions we deliver, to help create a fairer society for all.

Interview

Job interviews are on Microsoft Teams. We’ll make any adjustments to help you.

Want to know more? Visit our website or email careers@opencastsoftware.com

We are not working with recruitment agencies on this vacancy. If you are interested in this position, please apply directly with Opencast.

description:
Job Description

SHIFTS YOU ARE APPLYING FOR: 37.50hrs p/w; Sun 10:00 - 18:00; Tue 13:00 - 21:00; Wed 09:00 - 17:00; Thu 07:30 - 15:30; Fri 13:00 - 21:00

To be a successful Delivery Manager, you will lead and inspire your team to prioritise outstanding stock processing, stockroom organisation and achieve performance targets. Every day will be varied, fast paced, challenging but ultimately rewarding. People are at the heart of what we do so your experience in leading, coaching and motivating a high performing team will be crucial to your success. You can count on us to invest in your personal development from day one. Flexible working options are available.

About the Role:

To be a successful Delivery Manager you will:

- Manage a team to deliver outstanding stock processing and stockroom organisation in an environment which is commercial, operationally efficient, safe and where performance targets are achieved
- Demonstrate a hands-on approach for all operational activities by working alongside the team, supporting the sales floors and store management team when needed
- Create an atmosphere where supporting, motivating and inspiring your team to be at their best is at the core of everything you do
- Ensure smooth running of the stockroom processes by continuously improving, identifying and solving problems – driving the highest stockroom and stock processing standards
- Always strive to ensure our beautifully presented stock is available to our customers as soon as possible

We’ll offer amazing benefits (see list further below)

About You:

- You are passionate about our customers, our people and our products. This passion and energetic approach to work inspires and motivate others, creating a great working atmosphere and team spirit
- A team player who works at their best in a results driven, fast paced and challenging environment. You have the ability to adapt to change quickly, bringing the rest of the team on board with the new objectives
- A great communicator and can work naturally with people at all levels. You stay calm and approachable even under pressure - always realistic with your expectations of others
- Able to demonstrate the ability to problem solve, make sound business decisions, confidently challenge processes and generate innovative ideas to take the business forward
- Confident when dealing with people issues
- An effective multi tasker who can plan, organise and prioritise your workload
- Experience in working to productivity related performance targets is desirable but not essential

In accordance with Home Office guidance successful candidates will be required to evidence their right to work in the UK before commencement of employment.

This role is not one we would typically consider for sponsorship under the Skilled Worker route due to, for example, the relevant Home Office requirements on skills level, not being met. Candidates are therefore encouraged to consider their own right to work options without Next sponsorship.

What’s Next

Press the apply button now to start your application. Once you have applied for the job, we will initially consider your skills and experience based on your application. If you match our criteria we will be in touch to arrange a Telephone or Video Interview to find out more about your job history and more about you as a person. The next stage would be an in store assessment.

In order to apply for this position you must not have had an unsuccessful application for a similar role in 6 months.

About Us

You know Next, but did you know we’re a FTSE-100 retail company employing over 44,000 people across the Next group. We’re the UK’s 2nd largest fashion retailer and for Kidswear we’re the market leader. At the last count we have over 450 stores, plus the Next Online and it’s now possible to buy on-line from over 80 countries around the world! So we’ve gone global!

About The Team

- Fantastic rewards for doing a great job and achieving great results
- 25% off most NEXT, MADE*, Lipsy*, Gap* and Victoria's Secret* products (*when purchased through NEXT)
- 10% off most partner brands & up to 15% off Branded Beauty
- Sharesave Scheme
- 60% off a generous (optional) working wardrobe allowance to buy clothes to wear for work (minimum 6 week contract)
- Early VIP access to sale stock
- Hot deals and exclusive offers from over 3,500 retailers through our online benefits platform
- Access to fantastic discounts at our Staff Shops
- Access a digital GP and other free health and wellbeing services
- Life assurance
- You can register for a discounted health plan for you and your family
- Financial Wellbeing - Save, track and enhance your financial wellbeing
- Apprenticeship - Earn, learn and gain a qualification (England stores only)
- Direct to Work - Discount online and instore, collect your items the next day for free from your place of work or local store
- Support Networks - Access to Network Groups to empower and celebrate each other
- Wellhub - Discounted flexible monthly gym memberships, with apps, PT sessions and more

Conditions apply to all benefits. These benefits are discretionary and subject to change.

We aim to support all candidates during the application process and are happy to provide workplace adjustments when necessary. Should you need support with your application due to a disability or long-term condition, feel free to get in touch with us by email careers@next.co.uk (please include 'Workplace Adjustments' in the subject line), or call us on 0116 479 2223 / 0044 116 479 2223 (line opening times are Monday to Thursday 9am - 5pm; Friday 9am - 4.45pm; Saturday 9am - 5pm & Sunday 9am - 4pm. Excludes bank holidays).

title: Clinical Homecare Nurse (Tzield)
description:
HealthNet Homecare is a specialist provider of home-based healthcare services, supporting over 240,000 patients across the UK. Working alongside the NHS and pharmaceutical companies, we deliver medications, nursing care, treatment administration and training, and patient support programmes in the comfort of patients' own homes. Our goal is to help patients access high-quality care outside of hospital, enabling them to manage their treatment safely, confidently, and independently.

We are looking for Clinical Homecare Nurses to join our nursing team in providing professional services to our clients, patients, and healthcare providers.

If you're a qualified and registered nurse looking for a career where you can be part of making a difference to the quality of life for patients by applying your passion, drive, and skillset in an ever-changing healthcare environment, then HealthNet Homecare is the place for you to join our busy, growing team!

Who We Are

Our Nurse Team is made up of specifically trained homecare professionals with the capability to support both straightforward and complex end-to-end therapies in a patient-focused and quality-driven manner.

Our vision is to be seen as the first choice for patient-centred homecare and to realise this vision, we work closely with the NHS and Pharmaceutical Companies to provide an array of services - from medication delivery and nursing services to patient support programmes. This allows patients to undertake treatment in the comfort of their own homes, with the correct support and to the same standards that would normally be received in a hospital or clinical environment.

Why us?

As a business, we realise that it is our people - aligned with a clear focus -that will ultimately deliver our vision. We focus on training programmes that allow our Clinical Nurse Team to go out into the community with confidence, backed by the knowledge of a strong business support network and the ability to promote our culture of patient-centred care.

We strongly believe in continuous professional development and providing the investment that enables colleagues to progress in their careers.

You will work 37.5 hours per week on a 5 days from 7 rota, with weekend working required as part of the rotation.

Main Responsibilities:

- Assist in providing excellent standards of patient care on behalf of the client and associated healthcare professionals
- Teaching patients, carers or family members to self-administer therapy, or the administration of therapies to patients in accordance with service-specific protocols in the comfort of their own homes
- Participating in telephone calls, virtual calls and home visits as part of Patient Support Programmes
- Assist in providing solutions that will support the patient and healthcare professional in delivering a seamless service between hospital and home
- Ensure a high standard of service is established and always delivered for all customers and patients

Travel Expectations

Travel is an essential part of this role. As a Clinical Homecare Nurse, you’ll visit patients across a wide geographical area, and routes can vary daily depending on clinical requirements. There isn’t a set location radius, so on some days travel between patients may be longer than others.

We aim to plan routes efficiently to reduce travel time where possible, and all travel between patient visits is included within your working hours. It’s important that applicants are comfortable with regular driving, as travel forms a significant part of the working day.

Your time on the road is balanced with the reward of providing essential care to patients in their own homes, helping them remain comfortable, confident, and independent.

What experience and skills are we looking for?

You will be a registered nurse and passionate about delivering first-class patient care.

Essential Skills

- Registered Nurse on NMC register
- Subcutaneous injection experience
- Computer literate

Desirable Skills

- 5 years post-registration experience
- Previous homecare experience
- Cannulation experience
- Venepuncture experience
- Previous experience in the administration of IV therapies

What we offer:

- Competitive salary structure
- Annual car allowance of £5,000 & a fuel card for field-based Nurses
- 25 days holiday + bank holidays
- Pension Scheme
- Ongoing training and development
- Professional registration fees paid
- Employee Assistance Programme including 24/7 access to remote GP appointments
- Refer-a-friend scheme
- Uniform provided
- Kit bags for all Homecare Nurses
- Eyecare vouchers
- Perks and benefits via Perkbox
- Long service awards

If the role sounds of interest and you want to be part of a company that truly places patients at the heart of everything we do, please apply through our careers page and join us in making a difference.

Please note: Due to the high volume of applications we usually receive, we’re unable to contact each applicant individually regarding the status of their application. If you are selected for an interview, we will be in touch shortly.

title: Warehouse Operative
description:
Location: Motherwell | Full-time, Permanent | Salary Range: £29,857.11 to £30,230.69 + Benefits

Never be tied to a desk again with this varied and active role!

Do you have previous experience working in a warehouse and want to develop your career within the supply chain and logistics industry?

If so, our Warehouse Operative role is the job for you!

What We Do

STEF Langdons delivers chilled and frozen food to almost any location across the UK and Ireland within 24 hours, supported by 12 depots and a fleet of over 500 vehicles.

The Role

As a Warehouse Operative, you’ll help ensure customer goods are received, handled, stored and dispatched safely, efficiently and to the required standards.

You’ll be responsible for:

- Receiving and checking incoming loads, including packaging and labelling.
- Handling and securing stock in line with food safety requirements.
- Operating designated mechanical handling equipment safely.
- Preparing loads for dispatch and loading vehicles.
- Completing quality, cleanliness and hygiene checks.
- Identifying and addressing hazards to maintain a safe working environment.

What You’ll Bring

- Experience working in a warehouse or similar environment.
- An up-to-date licence for designated mechanical handling equipment.
- Good IT and Microsoft Office skills.
- Knowledge of warehouse, food safety and health & safety procedures.
- Good communication, organisation and arithmetic skills.
- The ability to work to targets and deadlines, use your initiative and work effectively as part of a team.

Available Shift Patterns

- Monday to Friday 04:00am - 13:30pm
- 4 On 4 Off Nights 22:00pm - 08:00am

Why STEF Langdons?

We work as a team. We take pride in what we do. We do what we say we will do. We get better every day.

In return, you’ll receive:

- Annual pay review
- Long Service Bonus Payments
- Company uniform and onsite parking
- Company sick pay
- Employee Assistance Programme
- Staff Discount Scheme
- Company Share Incentive Plan
- Warehouse to wheels scheme
- Free inhouse job specific training and development
- Opportunity for career relevant apprenticeships

If this role sounds like the right fit for you, click apply today to become our new Warehouse Operative, we would love to hear from you!

For more information, contact feedyourfuture@langdons.co.uk.

STEF Langdons is an equal opportunities employer. We welcome applications from all backgrounds and particularly encourage applications from groups underrepresented in our industry, including women, LGBT+ and Black, Asian and Minority Ethnic applicants.

title: Senior Full Stack Engineer
description:
Senior Full-Stack Engineer

Salary: £60,000-£85,000 DOE
Location: Manchester - Hybrid

Maxwell Bond have partnered with a rapidly growing AI SaaS business who are looking for a Senior Full-Stack Engineer to join their growing engineering team.

The company is entering an exciting period of growth, with further investment, a growing customer base and several new products in development. As a result, they're continuing to build out their engineering team to support the next phase of the business.

Their product is AI-native from the ground up, built around real-time and conversational experiences.

As Senior Full-Stack Engineer, you'll be joining a growing engineering team and working closely with Product, Design and Senior Leadership. There's plenty of scope to get involved beyond development, contributing to product ideas, solving technical challenges and helping shape how the platform evolves as the business scales.

What you'll do as Senior Full-Stack Engineer:

- Own significant product and platform initiatives from discovery and requirements gathering through to design, development, release and ongoing improvement.
- Build user-facing features across a React/TypeScript frontend and Python backend, working with Django and FastAPI.
- Lead technical and architectural decisions, considering scalability, reliability, performance and maintainability as the platform grows.
- Build and improve real-time voice AI experiences, with a focus on performance, responsiveness and creating great interactive user experiences.
- Take ownership of projects and technical decisions, helping the team continue to improve its engineering practices as the business scales.

What We're Looking for:

- Proven experience building user-facing products and taking features from initial idea through to production, ideally across React/TypeScript and Python/Django.
- Strong system design skills, with the ability to make pragmatic technical decisions and understand the trade-offs involved.
- A good understanding of computer science fundamentals, including data structures, algorithms, system architecture and distributed systems.
- A practical understanding of AI coding tools and how to use them effectively, while still being able to review, challenge and correct AI-generated code.

What You'll Get:

- Salary up to £85,000 DOE, depending on experience.
- Equity options
- 32 days paid holiday.
- Competitive pension.

This is a great opportunity for a Senior Full-Stack Engineer who enjoys being involved beyond just writing code.

You'll have genuine ownership over what gets built, work closely with Product and Design, and help shape the technical direction of an AI-native product as it scales.

If you enjoy solving complex technical problems, building great user-facing products and want to work in a fast-moving AI environment where you can have a real impact, apply now!

title: Card Games Tutor
