title: Assistant Accountant
location: Sutton In Ashfield, England, United Kingdom
description:
At Bellway we recognise that people are the key to our success, and we are committed to building an inclusive culture that values and respects difference combined with creating a safe and inclusive working environment for all colleagues. This means we are positive about making adjustments as well as providing flexible working and we would be happy to talk to you about how this could work for you.

As the next step of long term growth and to support our sustainability priorities - Bellway has opened a new, highly automated, Timber Frame Manufacturing facility located in Sutton in Ashfield.

This new Division, Bellway Home Space, became operational in 2026 and there is an exciting opportunity to join the team at our new state of the art facility. Our Home Space Division is looking to recruit an Assistant Accountant to join the Division's Finance team.

The Role

The role of the Assistant Accountant involves assisting in the production of accurate and timely financial transactions and reports in addition to maintaining the business's accounting records and production of the monthly management accounts. To assist Head of Finance with maintenance and development of cost management reporting, cost control initiatives and KPI review.

Principal Accountabilities Of The Role Include

- Effectively assist the Head of Finance in preparing monthly journals, management accounts and account analysis, including for audit purposes and at interim and financial year end.
- Ensure the weekly bank reconciliations, weekly cash forecast and movement reports are prepared accurately and submitted appropriately.
- Manage the maintenance of all banking and cashbook entries.
- Prepare monthly/quarterly statistical returns for Group including National Statistics.
- Transactional finance, including sales and purchase ledger processing and reconciliation.
- Reviewing Standard Costing activities, Recoveries and Inventory movements including variance analysis.
- Credit control (minimal as all inter company transactions).
- Assist with the CIS & VAT returns.
- Assist in the monthly preparation of Trial Balance and management accounts.
- Prepare balance sheet reconciliation and backup documentation.
- Assist with cost control and KPI reporting.
- Assist with management of fixed assets and capital expenditure tracking.
- Work with non-financial managers to drive control and continuous improvement.
- Ensure all activities and carried out in line with company policies and procedures.
- Carry out any other reasonable tasks as directed by the Divisional and Group Finance Management Teams.

The above list of accountabilities are not exclusive or exhaustive. The post holder will be required to undertake any such duties as may be reasonably expected.

Experience, Qualifications And Skills

Knowledge and Experience

- Strong educational background, possibly studying towards an Accountancy Qualification
- Previous accounting experience - essential
- Experience in manufacturing environment with standard costing
- Good IT skills and an ability to interrogate and develop ERP/MRP system
- High skill level in Microsoft Excel
- Be methodical and with a diligent approach to working
- Have good written and verbal communication skills, especially in liaison with non-financial managers
- Be organised to be able to cope with multiple tasks and priorities in a fast moving manufacturing environment and with a high commitment to quality standards.
- Microsoft Dynamics Business Central experience a strong advantage

Skills And Aptitude

- Excellent administration and organisation skills
- Analysis, numerical and report writing skills
- Strong people management and time management
- Strong communication, listening and problem solving
- Ability to prioritise workload and meet deadlines
- Demonstrates a high level of discretion and confidentiality.
- Excellent attention to detail
- Ability to work on own as well as part of a team
- Proficient IT skills along with a good working knowledge of Microsoft Office (Word, Excel and outlook) and the ability to adapt to and develop new systems.
- Committed to diversity and inclusion

The Role and Working Conditions

- Office based role with some infrequent travel within the Group and to Head Office (Newcastle).
- Willing to be flexible in respect to day to day duties and hours worked
- Please note this role is subject to a basic DBS and financial pre-employment checks

In Return We Can Offer You

- Competitive salary
- Contributory pension scheme
- 25 days holiday, plus bank holidays
- Access to discounts and benefits portal
- ShareSave Scheme
- Cycle to Work Scheme
- Life assurance
- Holiday Purchase Scheme
- Earn and Learn Opportunities

We reserve the right to close this vacancy if a large volume of applications are received.

title: Digital Assessor
description:
If you would like to work for an organisation that demonstrates outstanding commitment to staff engagement, has gained a place on the Times Best 100 Companies to work for in the UK for the last eight consecutive years and that holds Investors in People Platinum accreditation we would love to hear from you!

Additional qualification uplift (subject to proof of qualification):

- Qualified in a digital subject to Level 4+ or equivalent: +£1,000 per annum
- Qualified in a digital subject to Level 7+ or equivalent: +£2,000 per annum

(Salary uplift is dependent on receipt and verification of qualification certificates.)

At ACT, our Behaviour Framework shapes everything we do. We are looking for a Digital Assessor who demonstrates genuine respect for every learner, communicates with openness and integrity, and brings innovation and creativity to their approach to learning and assessment. You will be motivated to inspire and empower learners to take ownership of their development and achieve their goals, while maintaining clarity in your planning, decision-making and communication. If you are proactive, adaptable and committed to delivering high-quality learning experiences, we would love to hear from you.

What you’ll do:

- Manage a caseload of learners, ensuring all key milestones are met, including initial contact with learners and employers, completion of induction and Individual Learning Plans within 28 days, and regular monthly progress reviews.
- Plan and deliver engaging, learner-centred training and assessment using a range of digital methods.
- Mark and provide feedback on learner work within agreed turnaround times, normally within two weeks.
- Monitor learner progress closely, setting clear and realistic targets and taking appropriate action where learners fall behind.
- Build strong working relationships with employers, ensuring they are actively involved in reviews and learner progress.
- Deliver a consistent, high-quality learning experience aligned to awarding body, Welsh Government and ACT requirements.
- Maintain accurate and up-to-date records, including OneFile and Vision, to reflect learner progress and compliance.
- Identify additional learning needs and put appropriate support in place.
- Support learners to develop their literacy, numeracy, ICT, digital and employability skills, alongside wider areas including sustainability, global citizenship, Equality and Diversity, Welsh Language and Culture, and Well-being.
- Support learners to plan, deliver, evaluate and reflect on substantial workplace-based digital projects.
- Contribute to curriculum development, learning design and continuous improvement of delivery.
- Undertake any other duties as requested by your Coordinator or Manager, which may be necessary from time to time.

Please See Job Description For Full Details Of Responsibilities.

ACT is committed to promoting the Welsh language for both staff and learners, and whilst it is not considered essential criteria, the ability to speak Welsh is desirable for this role.

What we are looking for:

We are looking for someone who thrives in a busy, target-driven environment and can manage competing priorities effectively.

You will demonstrate:

- Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage multiple learners, deadlines and priorities.
- Experience delivering training, coaching or assessment in a digital or IT-related area.
- Strong occupational experience within a digital or IT environment.
- Confidence using digital systems and managing learner data accurately.
- Experience supporting or delivering digital projects from planning and design through to delivery, evaluation and reflection.
- Knowledge of accessibility, inclusive digital design, data protection, copyright, intellectual property and the ethical use of digital technologies.
- Experience supporting learners to apply Level 4 knowledge and skills to substantial workplace projects.
- A proactive approach to tracking progress and resolving issues early.
- The ability to communicate clearly and professionally with learners, employers and colleagues.
- A focus on achieving positive outcomes while maintaining high standards of quality.
- The ability to adapt your approach and use digital technology creatively to enhance learning.

Why work for ACT?

At ACT, people are at the heart of everything we do. As Wales’s largest training provider, we’re passionate about making a real difference through high-quality learning — and we’re just as committed to supporting our staff to grow, develop and succeed.

We’re proud to be an Investors in People Platinum organisation, accredited for over 25 years, and recognised in the Best Companies 2025 awards as one of the UK’s top employers — ranked 26th Best Large Company to Work For and 5th in Wales.

Our Values:

At ACT, we pride ourselves on fostering a culture of respect, fairness, and dignity for all. We believe in creating an inclusive environment where every individual feels valued and empowered to thrive.

FREDIE has been central to promoting and recognising exceptional commitment to equality and diversity. FREDIE stands for Fairness, Respect, Equality, Diversity, Inclusion, and Engagement, and these values are at the heart of ACT’s philosophy, shaping our approach to both staff and learners.

Diversity statement

ACT is dedicated to fair and safe recruitment practices, ensuring equality for all applicants and staff. We do not discriminate based on gender, sexual orientation, marital or civil partner status, gender reassignment, race, colour, nationality, ethnic or national origin, religion or belief, disability or age. Our questioning and collating of information are intended to help us maintain equal opportunities best practice and identify barriers to workforce equality and diversity. The information collated from you will not be used in any decision affecting you.

We are happy to consider an reasonable adjustments that candidates may need during the recruitment process, please drop us an email with your requirements.

What next?:

The Advert will close 25th September 2026. We reserve the right to close this vacancy early if we receive sufficient applications for the role.

Applicants will be notified via email of application process (please check junk or spam folders)

An interview process consisting of:

A face to face at our Head Office with a work-based task (for example - a micro teach, full details will be provided before interview)

We’re keen to ensure our hiring process allows you to be at your best, so if you need us to make any adjustments, please just let us know.

If you have any queries about the vacancy, please feel free to contact us on recruitment@acttraining.org.uk.

Safeguarding:

Our organisation is deeply committed to safeguarding the welfare of all learners and staff. We expect all employees to uphold this commitment as part of their role. Please note that the successful candidate will be required to undergo an enhanced DBS check.

If you would like to work for an organisation that demonstrates outstanding commitment to staff engagement, has gained a place on the Times Best 100 Companies to work for in the UK for the last eight consecutive years and that holds Investors in People Platinum accreditation we would love to hear from you!

What you get in return:

- Excellent professional development opportunities
- Generous holiday package (up to 45 days per year)
- E-learning platform available to all staff.
- Annual salary increases

title: Bookkeeper / Accounts Assistant
description:
BC Financial Search is working with an established accountancy practice in Leeds to recruit an experienced Bookkeeper / Accounts Assistant to join their team on a full-time basis.

This is a broad, hands-on position suited to somebody with good experience working within an accountancy practice or bookkeeping environment who enjoys managing their own workload and having regular contact with clients.

The role will be predominantly office-based in Leeds, with occasional travel to client premises where required.

The firm is open-minded on qualification level. You could be studying towards AAT, already AAT qualified, or simply have strong practical experience and be qualified by experience. Study support can also be provided for somebody who would like to continue their professional development.

Salary is expected to be in the region of £32,000–£40,000, depending on experience.

Duties and responsibilities
The successful candidate will work across a varied portfolio of clients, with responsibilities including:

- Completing bookkeeping for a range of businesses and sole traders
- Preparing and submitting VAT returns
- Supporting clients with Making Tax Digital requirements and submissions
- Preparing management accounts
- Maintaining accurate accounting records and reconciliations
- Working extensively with cloud accounting software including Xero and QuickBooks
- Liaising directly with clients regarding their bookkeeping and accounting requirements
- Visiting client premises when required
- Supporting the wider accounts team with additional accounting work where appropriate

The position offers plenty of variety and would suit somebody who enjoys working directly with clients rather than performing a purely transactional bookkeeping role.

Experience and qualifications
The firm is flexible regarding formal qualifications and is particularly interested in candidates with strong practical bookkeeping experience.

Ideally, you will have:

- Previous bookkeeping experience, ideally gained within an accountancy practice or similar environment
- Good working knowledge of Xero and QuickBooks
- Experience preparing VAT returns
- Knowledge of Making Tax Digital requirements
- Some exposure to management accounts
- Good attention to detail and organisational skills
- Confidence communicating directly with clients
- The ability to manage your own workload and deadlines

Candidates may be:

- Studying towards an AAT qualification
- Already AAT qualified
- Qualified by experience with a strong bookkeeping background

Benefits
The role offers:

- Salary of £32,000–£40,000, depending on experience
- Full-time permanent position
- Study support available for candidates looking to continue their qualifications
- Broad bookkeeping and accounting responsibilities
- Regular client contact
- Exposure to a varied portfolio of businesses
- Opportunity to develop beyond traditional bookkeeping into areas such as management accounts

Company culture
The firm is a well-established Leeds accountancy practice providing a broad range of accounting, tax and advisory services to its clients.

This role would suit somebody who values being part of an office-based team and enjoys building strong relationships with both colleagues and clients.

The position provides a good balance between day-to-day bookkeeping responsibilities and broader accounting work, with the opportunity to continue developing technically and professionally.

For more information or a confidential discussion about the position, please apply or contact Ben Copsey at BC Financial Search directly.

As the face of Royal Mail you will work as part of a team ensuring we continue to deliver the high standards of service our customers expect.

When you think of jobs at Royal Mail, the first thing you might think of is the postal workers who deliver mail to your home day in, day out. From exam results and tax returns, to wedding invites or online purchases, joining Royal Mail gives you the opportunity to deliver much more than mail. It allows you the chance to deliver smiles and successes; new toys and old memories – making a real impact in the heart of your community, while working for one of the UK’s most well-loved brands.

Upbeat and self-motivated, you’ll be as happy working alone as you will be working as part of a team and getting to know the different people on your round. You’ll have a strong sense of community and the idea of doing a job that involves flexible shift patterns will appeal. We deliver mail come rain or shine, so we’re looking for people who like being outdoors whatever the weather, and because there is walking involved in every round, you’ll also be someone who likes the idea of doing a job that will help you keep fit. One of the UK’s leading companies, we’re undertaking one of the biggest industrial transformations in the UK in recent history. Letter volumes are declining. The position requires a strong technical accounting foundation, attention to detail and the ability to work independently in a manufacturing environment.

- Take a hands-on role in the preparation and production of the monthly Management Accounts in accordance with the corporate timetable.
- Analyse monthly P&L and Balance Sheet results against budget, forecast and prior year, identifying significant variances and preparing clear supporting commentary.
- Manage the month-end accounting process, including preparation and posting of general ledger journals in SAP and accurate preparation of accruals, prepayments and major accounting estimates.
- Ensure that monthly sales reporting reconciles to the Profit and Loss statement and prepare other monthly financial reports required by Group Finance.

- Prepare and maintain supporting schedules and documentation for key Balance Sheet accounts.
- Support daily and monthly cash-flow reporting by coordinating relevant information from Accounts Receivable, Accounts Payable and relevant budget owner.
- Support the annual budgeting and forecasting process, preparing financial information and analysis for the relevant areas of the business.
- Monitor CAPEX expenditure against approved budgets and prepare regular capital expenditure reports, including expenditure.
- Assist budget holders in the preparation of budgets and forecasts for their areas of responsibility.
- Work closely with budget holders to understand their cost base, investigate variances and provide relevant financial analysis to support decision making.
- Liaise with the Supply Chain team regarding goods receipting, purchase orders and invoicing issues and support the timely resolution of discrepancies.
- Support the preparation of insurance-related financial information and other finance reporting requirements as required.

- Experience in preparing monthly management accounts, analysing financial performance and explaining variances.
- Proven experience working with and communicating effectively with both Finance and non-Finance stakeholders

- Demonstrated ‘self-starter’ who is comfortable working either individually or as part of a cross-functional team with multiple internal and external stakeholders.
- Results-oriented, commercial operator focused on high quality outcomes.
- Highly organised and tenacious individual who will always seek a resolution with the ability to manage multiple projects with excellent attention to detail.

- Mature, reliable and comfortable dealing with internal and external customers – a collaborator.

Y Swydd

Rydym yn chwilio am addysgwr cymwys gyda phrofiad o addysgu’r Gymraeg yng Nghyfnod Allweddol 3, TGAU a Safon Uwch a Blynyddoedd 5 a 6 yn yr Ysgol Gynradd. Mae’n bwysig bod yr ymgeisydd yn barod i fynychu ymweliadau addysgol, gan gynnwys rhai rhyngwladol a phreswyl yn ôl y galw, a chynorthwyo a chefnogi sesiynau a chlybiau. Addysgwr graddedig gyda Statws Athro Cymwysedig (SAC) neu brofiad perthnasol.

Profiad llwyddiannus o ddysgu Cymraeg yng Nghyfnod Allweddol 3, TGAU a Safon Uwch gyda thystiolaeth o alluogi dysgwyr i gyrraedd safonau uchel.

Tystiolaeth o lwyddiant academaidd yn y pwnc.

Y gallu i arddangos sgiliau rheoli dosbarth rhagorol a chymryd rhan flaengar a chadarnhaol yng ngofal bugeiliol dysgwyr.

Agwedd flaengar ac arloesol at addysgu gan gynnwys gwybodaeth am y datblygiadau diweddaraf o fewn y proffesiwn.

Agwedd gefnogol a chynhwysol wrth ystyried gwahanol ddiwylliannau, cefndir, gallu a dewisiadau personol.

About The Department

The Welsh Department is a well-established department within Languages comprising of one full-time member of staff and a part-time member of staff who currently teach students from Years 5 to Year 13. The department is accommodated in two teaching rooms in the Senior School. Students achieve outstanding results at GCSE, AS and A Level Welsh Second Language and progress to study a variety of subjects at universities such as Oxford, Durham, Queen’s University, Belfast, Central School of Speech and Drama, Cardiff University. All students study Welsh in Year 7 along with French and Spanish and it is studied as a language option in Years 8 and 9 with French, Spanish and Latin. At GCSE, Cymraeg Craidd and Cymraeg Estynedig are offered as options also and the teaching groups are smaller. We offer Welsh 2nd Language AS and A level and AS and A level First Language as required. Some students from Welsh medium primary schools join the Senior School annually and the College in Year 12. The department plays an integral role in supporting these students by assisting them with the transition from Welsh to English medium language teaching.

We also have members of staff in other departments who are Welsh speaking and support the department in promoting the Welsh ethos in the school.

The successful candidate will be expected to contribute to the department’s extra-curricular activities such as day trips, residential trips to Llangrannog and Glan-llyn as well as the Bore Coffi Cymraeg, the school’s annual Eisteddfod as well as the Urdd Eisteddfod. As a department we are passionate about promoting the Welsh ethos within the school and being part of the national plan to have a million Welsh speakers by 2050.

Adran y Gymraeg

Mae Adran y Gymraeg yn adran sefydledig o fewn y Gyfadran Ieithoedd gydag un aelod amser llawn ac un aelod rhan amser sy’n gyfrifol am ddysgu myfyrwyr o Flwyddyn 5 hyd at Flwyddyn 13. Mae gan yr ysgol aelodau o staff mewn adrannau eraill sy’n siaradwyr Cymraeg ac yn cefnogi’r adran wrth hyrwyddo natur Gymreig yr ysgol.

Disgwylir i’r ymgeisydd llwyddiannus gyfrannu at weithgareddau allgyrsiol yr adran fel teithiau diwrnod a phreswyl i Langrannog a Glan-llyn yn ogystal â Bore Coffi Cymraeg yr adran, Eisteddfod yr Ysgol ac Eisteddfod yr Urdd. About The School

Howell’s School, Llandaff, is one of the oldest girls’ school in Wales, having opened in August 1860. Since then, it has steadily expanded, both in terms of student numbers and physical size. The school now caters for girls from the age of 3 to 16 and girls and boys 16-18. Since 1980 it has been a member of the Girls’ Day School Trust, the largest organisation of independent schools in the UK. Its 25 member schools all have a reputation for consistently high academic standards, superb pastoral support and enviable co-curricular programmes.

The facilities inside the Victorian building and its more modern extensions are first-class and the opportunities for extracurricular activities, teamwork and confidence-building numerous. Academically, the school provides great added value, with results at both GCSE and A level regularly greatly exceeding expectations.

title: Maintenance Electrician
description:
Job Introduction

Job Introduction:

Tarmac is the UK’s leading sustainable building materials and construction solutions business. Our innovative products and solutions not only deliver the infrastructure needed to grow the UK economy today but also help to create a more sustainable built environment for the country’s long-term future .

We are currently looking for an Maintenance Electricianto join our team based at Tarmac Stowfield Quarry and Asphalt Plant, Coleford . Working 40hrs per week Monday to Friday plus overtime. This role is easily accessible from Monmouth, Cinderford, Lydney, Gloucester, Chepstow, Newport and the surrounding areas .

We’re working hard to create a dynamic and inclusive environment and it’s important that our people come from a variety of different backgrounds .

Main Responsibilities

Reporting to the Plant Manager, the role of Maintenance Electrician will be responsible for undertaking plant maintenance, repairs and improvements to ensure maximum reliability of all plant associated areas and to assist team members in all aspects of plant operation .

Your responsibilities as the Maintenance Electrician will include:

- Respond to plant breakdowns, when necessary and be responsible for the correct and efficient repair of equipment keeping downtime to a minimum with timely and safe adherence to the maintenance plan whilst complying to all relevant statutory legislation and the internal company Safety, Health and Environmental standards
- Continue to improve plant performance whilst maintaining safety, maintenance and asset reliability
- In support of the maintenance and operations functions, you will utilise documents, and maintain policies, procedures, and associated guidelines for the safe and efficient maintenance of equipment within the Electrical Engineering department as appropriate

The ideal candidate:

The ideal candidate for the role of Maintenance Electrician will be self-motivated, enthusiastic and able to work with minimal supervision . You should also demonstrate proven experience working within an Industrial, Factory or similar environment .

Suitable candidates for the role of Maintenance Electrician will have:

- Level 3 Apprentice trained Electrician and ONC/NVQ Level 3 in Electrical Engineering
- 17th Edition - BS7671 I.E.E Regulations and Legislation as a minimum (18th Edition preferred)
- Testing & Inspection qualification (preferred)
- Experience of Total Productive Maintenance (TPM) methodology and Continuous Improvement
- Working knowledge of relevant electrical and control engineering maintenance principles and practices, and experience of working in a relevant heavy engineering industry
- Working knowledge and experience of Industrial Low Voltage power distribution systems
- Good working understanding of PLC’s and use of associated tools and techniques for interrogation of software
- Knowledge and understanding the operation of AC Drives and Motors
- Knowledgeable in the area of Pre Planned Maintenance
- Experience in working with a Computer Maintenance Management System
- Experience with Root Cause Analysis, Failure Mode & Effect Analysis tools/techniques
- Ability to design simple electrical systems and draw schematic diagrams then transfer the information into practical use
- Ability to perform electrical statutory tests and inspections and understand safe use of electrical test and measuring instruments
- An understanding of mechanical systems including hydraulics and pneumatics and understand National and International codes and symbols used on drawings and specifications
- Ability to learn Health and Safety rules applicable to each department regarding their own and other operators’ safety

Why Tarmac

We don't just offer a job, we offer a career.

Alongside this role, you'll have access to industry-leading rewards, development opportunities, and a culture that puts people first, including:

- Bonus scheme
- Enhanced holiday entitlement
- Contributory pension scheme
- Access to the Tarmac Reward website with discounts on retailers, holidays, etc.
- Access to our Employee Assistance helpline for free and confidential advice
- Access to our Employee Communities, where you can network, learn from others, and increase your awareness of the support available to you. Our three Employee Communities are: Health and Wellbeing, Inclusion and Identity, Personal Growth and Development
- Training and development opportunities

Tarmac is committed to being a Forces‑friendly employer. If you're coming from a military background, we'll support your transition and help you build a successful career with us.

We’re proud to be part of CRH, and even prouder to be an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for everyone. If you need any reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process, just let us know, we’re here to support you .

description:

title: Dermatology Specialist Nurse
description:
Are you a dynamic, forward-thinking, and self-motivated Dermatology Nurse who wants to come and join our friendly supportive Community Dermatology Team?

This is an exciting opportunity to be in a leading role delivering high quality care and providing support to community dermatology patients and their families and helping to develop- and expand our service. The community dermatology team offer a variety of clinics so patients from birth upwards can choose where they would like to be seen.

The team consists of GPs with extended roles as well as a team of Nurse Specialists who run clinics for patients with diagnosed skin conditions. We plan care, treatment regimes an provide emotional support as well as supporting self care strategies. current working hours of the service are Monday to Friday 0800-1700 and we see patients from birth upwards.

- To work independently and with the BNSSG Dermatology Team across the organisation and in partnership with secondary care
- To provide specialist dermatology nursing care in a variety of settings by undertaking holistic assessment and following guidelines and protocols
- To deliver nursing management of dermatological conditions in a range of settings, working in partnership with other health care providers at times

- Where appropriate prescribe for patients using independent or supplementary nurse prescribing or request changes in medication directly from the patients GP or Consultant.
- To make referrals to other health care professionals or agencies where appropriate. Maintaining effective communication and feedback to the original referrer.
- To ensure effective delivery of service and adhere to all policies of the organisation by prioritising, organising and delegating appropriately, responsibilities and workloads.

Ever dreamt about a career that sparks excitement and fosters your professional growth? Picture yourself waking up eager to make a real difference in our community, surrounded by teams who value your unique ideas.

We are Sirona care & health – England’s largest provider of Adult’s and Children’s Community Services and we’d love for you to join us in Bristol, North Somerset or South Gloucestershire.

Agenda for Change Salary, full NHS benefits, 27+ days’ annual leave, and participation in the NHS Pension Scheme – just a glimpse of the benefits you’ll receive.

We welcome and encourage all applicants. We are committed to having a workforce that reflects the communities we support and are proactively seeking to improve the diversity of our workforce. We know diversity fosters creativity and innovation.

We are committed to equality of opportunity, to being fair and inclusive, and to being a place where all belong. We aim to draw upon the widest possible range of views and experiences to meet the changing needs of our colleagues, partners and communities we serve.

title: Fundraising Manager
description:
Salary: £40,000 - £45,000 per annum
Location: The Pavilion, Campbell Park, Milton Keynes

This is a new and exciting role created to deliver The Parks Trust’s ambitious five-year Fundraising Strategy and support the diversification of the Trust’s income. The postholder will lead the development of sustainable income streams across trusts and foundations (including Lottery funders, where we have had the most recent success), corporate partnerships, individual giving and legacy fundraising.

The successful candidate will lead innovative fundraising campaigns, appeals and build lasting and meaningful relationships with donors, partners and supporters at local and national levels.

You will work closely with the Senior Leadership Team, setting clear objectives, and driving high performance aligned to the Trust's values and culture. Working collaboratively with other colleagues across the organisation, you will ensure fundraising activity is well-coordinated, compliant and impactful, helping to secure the income needed to realise the Trust's ambitions.

Personal Attributes
We're looking for someone who is:

- A natural relationship builder who enjoys connecting with people and developing lasting partnerships.
- Self-motivated, proactive and able to spot and pursue new opportunities.
- An excellent communicator with the ability to engage, influence and inspire a wide range of audiences.
- Resilient and determined, with the drive to achieve ambitious fundraising goals.
- Organised and able to manage multiple priorities while maintaining attention to detail.
- Creative in developing fundraising ideas, campaigns and supporter engagement activities.
- Collaborative and supportive, with a positive approach to working across teams.
- Passionate about making a difference and motivated by the impact of The Parks Trust's work.

Essential

- Degree level qualification or equivalent experience, with evidence of recent and ongoing professional development relevant to fundraising.
- Experience of fundraising across multiple income streams, including successful applications to charitable trusts, foundations, Lottery and statutory funders.
- Experience of building and implementing individual giving and/or corporate fundraising programmes.
- Experience of creating and implementing a successful fundraising strategy that has significantly increased revenues.
- Familiarity with CRM software, databases and Microsoft Office.
- Exceptional research and written communication skills, with the ability to write compelling funding applications and persuasive cases for support. Strong networking and relationship-building skills, with confidence presenting to donors, funders and partners.
- Strong financial acumen and the ability to work within agreed budgets.
- Self-motivated, proactive and resilient, able to manage competing priorities and deliver high-quality work to deadlines.
- Collaborative team player who inspires and supports colleagues.
- Ability to attend events and activities outside normal working hours.

Desirable

- Appreciation of The Parks Trust estate, including its greenspaces, ancient woodlands and lakes, and the environmental, health, education and social outcomes they deliver.
- Membership of a relevant professional body (e.g. Chartered Institute of Fundraising).
- Experience of fundraising within the environmental, conservation, parks, heritage or charitable sectors.
- Experience of developing legacy and major donor fundraising programmes.
- Knowledge of local authority and Section 106 funding mechanisms.

title: Community Mental Health Nurse
company: Dorset HealthCare University NHS Foundation Trust
description:
We are excited to recruit a registered Mental Health Nurse to join the Wimborne Adult CMHT team.

We would welcome applicants who are passionate about recovery, person centred in their approaches and driven to be part of a close working team.

You will be supported in your clinical work, and professional development, and with ongoing close & supportive supervision from the Team Leader.

You will provide specialist care and interventions, assessments, treatments and managing patients on a caseload, as part of the wider multi- disciplinary care team.

You will provide a high-quality person-centred approach to care delivery which always considers people’s safety, privacy and dignity.

If you are looking for a challenging, varied and rewarding job this could be the post for you, and we would welcome you to come and meet us and apply.

Employment in this post requires an Enhanced Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check, which the Trust will cover the cost of.

The post holder will work as part of an established integrated multi-disciplinary team, this team is made up of a Psychiatrist, Nurses, other mental health practitioners and Support Time Recovery Worker with further support from the business support team and psychologist.

We are looking for someone who is reliable, committed, dynamic, and a motivated professional with excellent communication, organisational skills and the ability to prioritise work.

Having experience of working in a community mental health environment would be useful, but not essential, you will need to be able to apply the philosophies of engagement and recovery within your work with service users.

A good level of IT literacy is an essential requirement.

The team is based in Wimborne and covers the surrounding area. The post holder will need to have a valid driving licence and use of a car as they will be required to assess and monitor patients in their own homes and within other community settings.

Please note visa sponsorship for this role is unfortunately not available. Please ensure you hold valid right to work in the UK and will not require sponsorship if successful.

At Dorset HealthCare we’re on a mission to empower people to make the most of their lives through our outstanding, joined-up healthcare services. We’re a dynamic, forward-looking Trust, running 12 community hospitals, specialist inpatient facilities and a wide range of integrated community and mental health services for a population of almost 800,000 people.

We do things differently here – it’s one of the reasons the CQC rated us ‘outstanding’ in 2019. It’s also why 95% of patients across our services say they have a good or very good experience of our services and 89% of staff feel they can really make a difference. Whether you’re looking to work with us in one of our bustling market towns, vibrant urban locations, thriving seaside spots, or among the rolling hills of Dorset, there are lots of ways you can make a difference in our communities.

Our 7,000-strong workforce is at the heart of what we do, and our success is a testament to our brilliant people. We're all about building a workplace for the future, we believe in equal opportunities, and we celebrate diversity. We’re an inclusive workplace, where everyone is welcome, everyone can be authentic, and we are all encouraged to be the best version of ourselves.

Working with us you’ll be part of a strong team, challenge yourself, build a career, and teach us what we don’t know. And you’ll be working towards our vision to be better every day through excellence, compassion, and expertise in all we do.

description:
Work Schedule

Standard (Mon-Fri)

Job Profile Title: Engineer II, Manufacturing Engineering

Direct Report To: Manufacturing Engineer Manager

Band: 5

Career Track: Professional Position

Location: Loughborough

Job Title: Manufacturing Engineer

Location: Loughborough

As part of the Thermo Fisher Scientific team, you’ll discover meaningful work that makes a positive impact on a global scale. Join our colleagues in bringing our Mission to life every single day to enable our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer. We provide our global teams with the resources needed to achieve individual career goals while helping to take science a step beyond by developing solutions for some of the world’s toughest challenges, like protecting the environment, making sure our food is safe or helping find cures for cancer.

DESCRIPTION:

Join our manufacturing engineering team and make a meaningful impact on advanced technology and processes. As an Engineer II in Manufacturing Engineering, you'll support continuous improvement, ensure quality standards, and optimize production processes while collaborating with cross-functional teams. Lead technical projects and provide manufacturing support to help deliver innovative solutions that enable our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner, and safer.

You will participate in new product introductions, process improvements, and equipment optimization initiatives. Using data-driven approaches and lean methodologies, you'll identify opportunities to enhance efficiency, reduce costs, and maintain the highest quality standards. Work closely with operations, quality, maintenance, R&D, and other teams to implement sustainable solutions that drive manufacturing excellence.

Our site:

At our sites in Loughborough, Thermo Fisher Scientific are forging partnerships that are transforming the industry.  We are pioneering solutions that are driven by client needs. To help enable us to strengthen and further develop the technical capability within our manufacturing suites, we are seeking Maintenance Engineers to join our growing site.

How you will make an impact:

In this role you will be participating a wide range of maintenance engineering activities throughout our production footprint. You will engage with colleagues at multiple levels and from several subject areas, to work together to ensure we deliver an exciting and robust production facility to our clients. You will take part and take accountability for maintenance activities (planned and unplanned), utilising operational excellence and continuous improvement activities. With the aim of improving equipment reliability and ensuring minimal equipment downtime.

What you’ll do:

During maintenance incidents, you will effectively engage problem solving and lean manufacturing techniques. Identifying the true root cause of the issue – and implement the corrective actions. Wider, we will drive improvements across the maintenance team to improve efficiency, hold high standards of 5S, eliminating or reducing waste and/or non-value add activities. This gives you the opportunity to actively participating in upgrading and improving equipment or engaging in projects.

- The team will complete important documentation, including highlighting errors or bad practices and making suggestions for improvements. Leading the progression of documentation (e.g. Change Controls, Validation documents, etc) through to completion.
- Utilising external resource where appropriate, you will acquire services/components. Generating, completing (with approvals) the appropriate documentation (e.g. Purchase Orders, spares requests, quotations, etc).
- You will have awareness of, and control spares in an efficient manner.
- Holding accountability and responsibility for ensuring all personal activities are reliably closed on time, against agreed targets (e.g. PPM, Deviations, Change Controls, Training, etc). Where required, you will complete training to ensure a current aseptic license is kept up to date.
- You will write clear and accurate maintenance instructions. Where appropriate you will assist with the organising and delivering of training and / or instruction of engineering and non-engineering staff.
- On occasion, providing cover for team members, including Technical Specialists and Engineering Coordinators as defined (e.g., point of contact).
- For this role is it important to understand emergency procedures and follow safe systems of work. There is an expectation you will ensure compliance with EHS and security policies and procedures, rules, signage and instructions at all times. In addition, you will conduct timely report

What we need from you:

- We are searching for a multi-skilled engineer with a good understanding of electrical control and automated systems.
- A standard of technical skills of HND level or higher and the ability to demonstrate your expertise of working within a manufacturing environment.
- As a proactive and logical person, you can use problem solving, utilising the companies’ lean philosophies.
- Be available to support Manufacturing through the Engineering Call-Out process. You are compensated for this.
- The ability to work to critical timelines and effective interpersonal skills are key to high level performance in this position.
- As we work within a COMAH environment, alignment to these standards is critical.

The role requires site coverage between 6:00 am and 6:00 pm. While the standard working hours are 8:00 am to 4:00 pm, flexibility will be required during certain weeks to provide coverage until 6:00 pm when necessary.

title: Registered Nurse (RGN) - Care Home

Tamworth Borough Council,

TAMWORTH BOROUGH COUNCIL

Customer Service Officer

Located in the heart of Staffordshire, Tamworth is a vibrant and well‑connected borough with a rich heritage and a growing population of over 77,000. title: Logistics Manager | SEC
description:
Logistics Manager - SEC | Full-Time

£36,000 + excellent benefits including healthcare, wellbeing support, 23 days' annual leave plus bank holidays, life assurance, meals on duty, and more.

We're looking for...

The Logistics Manager is responsible for the end-to-end back-of-house beverage supply operation for live events, conferences and exhibitions at SEC. This includes beverage procurement, supplier management, cellar/warehouse operations, stock control, financial management of liquor, delivery and distribution to event outlets, and the planning and execution of large-scale event beverage setups.

The role will oversee the movement of significant volumes of beverage stock from supplier delivery through to storage, distribution and post-event reconciliation, ensuring accurate stock control, cost management and minimal wastage.

The role will work closely with operational and commercial teams to ensure that beverage requirements are accurately forecast, ordered and delivered, with the right stock available at the right location and at the right time. The successful candidate will be comfortable operating in a fast-paced live-event environment and managing complex logistical requirements across multiple event spaces and outlets.

We are Levy

We are a visionary venue partner. We design and deliver bespoke guest experiences that prioritise people and the planet.

Trusted by some of the world's most iconic stadiums, entertainment venues, and major events from Wimbledon and Twickenham to Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, Edgbaston, the SEC and ExCeL London we bring experiences to life with passion and precision.

Our mission is to succeed the right way. From pioneering tech and seamless operations to show-stopping menus and exceptional service, we use insight and innovation to understand guests, improve the customer journey, reduce environmental impact, and support local communities.

We are a passionate, diverse team of venue specialists dedicated to making the planet better for future generations.

Logistics Manager - The Role

Event Planning And Coordination

- Collaborate with event organisers to understand specific logistics requirements for each live event, conference, or exhibition.
- Develop comprehensive logistics plans that encompass resource allocation, transportation, and setup schedules.
- Ensure effective communication and coordination with internal teams, external vendors, and third-party service providers.

Resource Management

- Cellar management – from placing orders to overseeing Beverage stock arrivals, deliveries and distribution
- Oversee the procurement, storage, and distribution of event materials, equipment, and supplies.
- Optimise resource allocation to minimise waste and reduce costs while maintaining high standards of quality.
- Implement efficient inventory management systems to track and control event-related assets.

Vendor And Supplier Relations

- Identify, negotiate, and manage contracts with external vendors and suppliers to secure the best possible services and pricing.
- Build and maintain strong relationships with key partners to ensure reliable and consistent support for events.

Budget Management

- Develop and manage budgets for logistics operations, ensuring financial goals are met and costs are controlled.
- Monitor expenses, identify cost-saving opportunities, and report on budget performance to senior management.

Transportation And Logistics Coordination

- Coordinate transportation logistics for equipment, materials, and personnel, ensuring timely and efficient delivery to and from the venue.
- Implement and optimise transportation routes to minimise environmental impact and reduce overall logistics costs.

Risk Management

- Identify potential logistical challenges and develop contingency plans to mitigate risks.
- Proactively address issues that may arise during events, finding swift and effective solutions to ensure minimal disruption.

Compliance And Safety

- Ensure compliance with relevant regulations, health and safety standards, and venue policies.
- Implement and enforce safety protocols for logistics operations to create a secure environment for staff, vendors, and attendees.

Technology Integration

- Stay abreast of technological advancements in logistics and implement relevant tools and software to enhance efficiency and accuracy.
- Utilise technology for real-time tracking of assets, transportation, and other logistics components.

Post-Event Evaluation

- Conduct thorough post-event evaluations to assess the effectiveness of logistics operations.
- Gather feedback from internal teams, vendors, and clients to identify areas for improvement and implement lessons learned in future events.

Leadership And Team Management

- Lead and motivate a team of logistics professionals, providing guidance, training, and support.
- Foster a collaborative and positive work environment that encourages innovation and continuous improvement in logistics processes

Experience

What we're looking for:

- Proven experience managing a large-scale beverage, liquor, cellar, warehouse or BOH operation.
- Experience managing beverage financials, including purchasing, stock valuation, cost control, variance and/or beverage GP.
- Experience managing the physical movement and distribution of beverage stock across multiple outlets/event spaces.
- Proven experience coordinating large-scale event setup, delivery and breakdown.
- Experience managing beverage suppliers and negotiating commercial terms.
- Experience leading a BOH, logistics, warehouse, cellar or beverage team.
- Strong understanding of stock control and inventory reconciliation.
- Experience working in a high-volume, time-critical environment.

What You'll Get In Return

- Competitive salary with bonus and full company benefits
- 23 days' annual leave plus bank holidays, your birthday off, and a holiday purchase scheme

Collins Aerospace is a global leader in technologically advanced and intelligent solutions for the aerospace and defence industry.

This is an exciting new role within Collins and a unique opportunity to be part the ASG electric thrust reverser actuation centre of excellence, working as part of a team of technical innovators in the development of new technologies to position the business for success on next generation of aerospace nacelle electric actuation. What You Will Do

As a Senior Design Engineer, you will be responsible for the design and development of electric actuation systems and associated subsystems, supporting projects from concept through to manufacture and qualification.

Your responsibilities will include:

- Generating innovative design concepts and product configurations for electro-mechanical actuation systems
- Supporting all stages of the design lifecycle, from requirements capture and proposals through detailed design, manufacture, and qualification
- Developing robust, lightweight, and cost-effective engineering solutions
- Producing high-quality manufacturing data packages, including drawings and tolerance analyses
- Leading and supporting detailed design activities within multidisciplinary engineering teams
- Ensuring compliance with customer, regulatory, and in-service requirements
- Supporting system integration and installation activities across actuation systems and interfacing equipment
- Conducting design reviews and delivering technical presentations to internal and external stakeholders
- Supporting risk identification, risk mitigation, and design assurance activities
- Investigating product issues during development, qualification, production, and in-service operation
- Supporting failure investigations and corrective action programmes
- Providing technical guidance and mentoring to junior engineers, graduates, and placement students
- Supporting technology roadmap development and future capability growth initiatives
- Collaborating with global engineering teams to share best practices and drive continuous improvement
- Supporting customer engagement activities and new business opportunitiesThe role will be based in a new Collins Aerospace facility in Wolverhampton, UK, with <10% international travel.

What You Must Have

- Degree in Mechanical Engineering or equivalent engineering qualification
- Demonstrated experience in a design engineering environment
- Strong understanding of machine design and electro-mechanical product development
- Experience developing mechanical or electro-mechanical systems throughout the product lifecycle
- Proven problem-solving and analytical skills

title: Early Careers Trainee
description:

Description

BHP is proud to be part of the Sumer Group, one of the UK’s fastest-growing accountancy practices. Together, we’re creating brighter futures for our people, our clients, and our communities.

Whether your passion lies in Audit, Accounts or Tax, you’ll gain the skills, qualifications and experience to become a fully qualified professional, supported every step of the way.

You’ll be joining a friendly, professional team where enthusiasm, curiosity and commitment are valued as highly as experience. From day one, you’ll work with a range of clients, gaining hands-on experience within Audit, Accounts or Tax. Depending on the team you join, this could include preparing accounts, supporting audits, or providing insightful tax and business advice.

You’ll join a training contract, combining practical client experience with professional study towards your qualification (AAT, ACA or ATT).

Rexel is a worldwide expert in distributing electric and energy-efficient products and services. Our goal is to provide smart electrical solutions that improve the comfort, safety and security of our customers’ homes, businesses, and industries.

Job Description

As a Warehouse Person, you will work in a high-volume warehouse and cable distribution environment, handling stock receipt and storage, picking and packing orders, using mechanical handling equipment to move palletised materials efficiently. Your responsibilities will include ensuring orders are accurate, packaged correctly, and dispatched on time, while maintaining a safe and organised work area. Handling heavy cable drums and operating machinery safely are key aspects of the role, requiring attention to detail and a commitment to health and safety standards.

Key Responsibilities

- Receive, check and store incoming deliveries; label and put-away to correct locations to maintain stock order and traceability.

- Facilitate all inward and outward stock movements for the hub following company procedures and using IT/WMS systems to update inventory.
- Carry out cycle counts and stock-takes, report discrepancies and help maintain stock integrity.
- Use mechanical handling equipment (counterbalance forklifts, pallet trucks, etc.) safely and in line with company procedures to move palletised drums and reels.
- Maintain high housekeeping standards: ensure cables, drums, reels and packaging are stored tidily and safely to prevent damage and trip hazards.
- Follow all Health & Safety policies and safe working procedures at all times, including correct lifting techniques, PPE use, and safe operation of equipment.

Qualifications

At Rexel, we prioritise hiring individuals based on behaviours and potential, rather than requiring specific formal qualifications for roles, the behaviours that will set you up for success as an Warehouse Person colleague include:

COLLABORATION: Building partnerships and working collaboratively with others to achieve shared objectives

TAKES ACCOUNTABILITY: Taking action, overcoming obstacles, and meeting commitments.

CUSTOMER FOCUS: building strong customer relationships and delivering customer-centric solutions.

What We Are Looking For....

- LICENCE: Hold a valid in-date Counterbalance or Reach FLT Licence
- EXPERIENCE: Proven Warehouse & FLT experience, with the ability to show good understanding of Stock Management Processes
- 12 months minimum of Counterbalance experience

- COMMUNICATION: Good approach to interacting with colleagues and management

Additional Information

At Rexel UK, we’re all about welcoming people from different backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives because we know that diversity drives fresh ideas and great results.

By coming together as one team, we’re building a high-performance culture that not only drives success but also creates real value for our customers and communities.

Creating an environment where individuality is celebrated and creativity flourishes, we're making sure everyone feels supported and confident to be their best.

title: Senior Protection & Control Engineer - Transmission & Distribution (Birmingham, UK)
description:
Description

Chart your own course and change the world — with the support of people whose interests are aligned with yours. At Burns & McDonnell, opportunity is waiting. It’s those kinds of people who’ve helped us grow from a small consulting business back in 1898 to a global leader in engineering, architecture and construction solutions. Today, we’re a thriving company with more than 10,000 professionals working in 75 offices worldwide and recognised as a leader in transmission & distribution services.

To Act In a Senior Technical Capacity In Producing Burns & McDonnell’s UK Engineering-related Project Deliverables Relating To Power System Protection & Control (P&C), Within The (power) Transmission & Distribution Global Practice. This Includes (but Not Limited To)

Undertaking senior and lead technical roles on project specific multi-disciplinary engineering teams;

- Being a senior technical authority on P&C engineering within the wider company;
- Supporting the Protection & Control Section Manager in growing and enhancing the P&C Section engineering capability in the UK business; and providing guidance and mentorship to less experienced engineers with the engineering team, particularly those in the P&C Section.
- Lead successful output of P&C engineering deliverables in the UK business, working with the P&C Section Manager to determine suitable P&C engineering personnel from across our global offices, as required.
- Be a lead technical role on P&C design project deliverables, ranging from 11kV up to 400kV (with a particular emphasis on 132kV voltages and above), including undertaking the role of Lead Project Engineer on project teams, as required and when appropriate.
- Produce detailed electricity substation P&C design packages, compliant to required client and national technical standards (ENA/BS/IEC/IEEE etc.).
- Power system studies (fault level and load flow) required to determine protection settings requirements and production of various relay protection files, as required.
- Prepare calculations and technical/equipment specification documentation.
- Execute complex assignments requiring the use of advanced techniques, resulting in the development of new or improved processes, equipment, and/or technological methods.
- Undertake consultancy role on FEED stage projects, including production of technical reports and presentations.
- Maintain compliance to CDM Regulations and all other legal and regulatory requirements associated with the nature of substation/P&C and electrical system design.
- Undertake technical quality assurance reviews and provide design approval/sign-off, as required, on P&C related designs and deliverables.
- Work closely with other sections with the UK T&D Engineering Team, particularly the Substation Section and Distribution Section, to enable effective collaboration on multi-disciplinary projects and facilitate an optimal engineering function in the UK business.
- Maintain technical compliance to applicable Burns & McDonnell and client design management standards, processes, and procedures on all work delivered.
- Assist with developing and implementing policies, processes, procedures, standards, and technical guidance, as required, to continually improve the engineering capability within the P&C Section.
- Plan and lead client meetings (or meeting sections) relating to P&C, as required.
- Where appropriate and required relating the P&C work, act as Contractor Design Approval Engineer (CDAE), as defined by National Grid’s TP137 procedure, or equivalent role as defined by other clients.
- Where appropriate and required, act as TP141 Protection Setting Engineer, as defined by National Grid’s TP141 and TP107 procedures.
- Support the preparation of project proposals and tender presentations.
- Drive ‘Safety by Design’ approach on all projects, at all times.
- Support nurturing of a safety and technical excellence culture through emphasis on staff competence, diligence, and responsible attitude.
- Understanding wider industry best practices and client technical standards/procedures for construction, operations & maintenance, and decommissioning, in order to drive safety, constructability, and operability throughout whole asset lifecycles.
- Maintain project compliance to Burns & McDonnell’s UK Integrated Management System (IMS).
- Support nurturing of world-class customer service culture, to drive client success.
- Be an ambassador for Burns & McDonnell at all times through acting in accordance with expected high ethical and moral standards, and in adherence to Burns & McDonnell Code of Conduct.
- Provide support for continued professional development of less experienced engineers in team, including technical guidance, and recommending training needs to the P&C Section Manager.
- Actively support marketing and business development activities, building relationships with client technical contacts to aid generating new business, and elevation of the Burns & McDonnell brand.
- Identifying new skills and competencies required within the Burns & McDonnell team to meet business needs and actively supporting development and recruitment of talent, including candidate interviewing.
- Act as an industry technical leader in P&C design and contribute to relevant professional bodies and industry groups. Maintain Continued Professional Development (CPD).
- Support or lead portions of section meetings.
- Interpret and support with establishing policies, procedures, and strategic goals of the organisation.
- Assist in determining section objectives and requirements, organise projects and develop standards and guidelines.
- Demonstrate creativity, foresight, and judgment in anticipating and solving problems.
- Advance and develop P&C Section tools and workflows to increase efficiency of designs, specification development, and project execution.
- Undertake other duties and responsibilities as may reasonably be asked of this position by management.

Qualifications

- Bachelor’s degree in engineering (or related field) required AND
- Minimum of 7 years of protection & control engineering design experience in the electricity transmission & distribution sector, with at least 5 of those years being on UK transmission system related projects (required) OR
- Master's degree in engineering (or related field) and 6 years of relevant experience.
- Knowledge of engineering design management best practices with ability to implement this knowledge
- Understanding of the requirements of relevant UK Health & Safety legislation relating to design and construction work in the electricity supply industry.
- Understanding of the requirements of relevant UK Environmental and Waste Management legislation.
- Thorough understanding of current Construction (Design & Management) Regulations.
- Experience of working in a lead substation design role on National Grid Electricity Transmission projects in the UK and acting as a TP137 CDAE for Protection & Control and as the TP141 Protection Settings Engineer.
- Good knowledge of National Grid’s procedures: TP106, TP107, TP131, TP135, TP137, TP141, TP153, TP163, TP183, TP184, TP188, TP189, TP191, TP211, TP215, TP235, TP241.
- Thorough knowledge and experience applying National Grids Technical Specification, Technical Guidance Notes, and Design Handbooks relating to substation protection & control in the UK.
- Understanding of the causes and consequences of Impressed Voltage.
- Understanding of the general requirements of procedural control of Temporary Works, in accordance with British Standards.
- IT literate, with good knowledge of using Microsoft Office applications.
- Knowledge of applying CAD technology/software to substation and P&C design and strong understanding of BIM principles (PAS 1192 and ISO 16950)
- Excellent written & verbal communication skills.
- Strong persuasion and negotiation skills with clients and employees.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
- Ability to deal effectively with a wide variety of stakeholders across clients, industry, government and public.
- Able to manage tasks on multiple projects and conflicting deadlines.
- Able to work autonomously and/or as part of a project team.
- Pro-active in building knowledge and understanding of the electricity transmission and distribution industry.
- Capability to coach and develop the team.
- Engaged in the engineering community and how we can drive success for our clients.
- Ability to develop innovative and practical solutions to a range of problems, and an understanding of how one issue may be part of a much larger solution.
- Ability to make an effective and collaborative contribution to the team through sharing knowledge, promoting ideas, and valuing the contribution of all team members

title: Assistant Management Accountant
description:
ASSISTANT MANAGEMENT ACCOUNTANT / MANAGEMENT ACCOUNTANT

SALFORD, GREATER MANCHESTER (HYBRID WORKING)

£35,000 to £40,000 + BENEFITS + STUDY SUPPORT

THE OPPORTUNITY:

We're partnering with a well-established and growing business based in Salford that is looking to recruit an Assistant Management Accountant / Management Accountant to join their finance team on a permanent basis.

This is a fantastic opportunity for someone with strong management accounting experience who is confident using Xero and looking for a varied, hands-on finance role within a growing business.

Working within a small finance team, the successful candidate will be responsible for supporting the preparation of monthly management accounts, financial analysis, reconciliations and reporting, whilst also taking a hands-on approach to transactional finance activities including purchase ledger and sales ledger.

THE ASSISTANT MANAGEMENT ACCOUNTANT / MANAGEMENT ACCOUNTANT ROLE:

- Preparing and supporting monthly management accounts, including profit & loss, balance sheet and variance analysis
- Managing month-end processes, including accruals, prepayments, journal postings and reconciliations
- Completing balance sheet reconciliations, investigating discrepancies and ensuring accurate financial records
- Producing financial reports and analysing income, expenditure and performance against budgets
- Supporting budgeting, forecasting and cashflow reporting activities
- Preparing financial information and analysis to support senior management decision-making
- Supporting purchase ledger activities, including invoice processing, supplier reconciliations and payment runs
- Assisting with sales ledger processes, ensuring income is accurately recorded and reconciled
- Maintaining accurate accounting records within Xero and ensuring transactions are correctly allocated
- Identifying opportunities to improve finance processes, reporting and internal controls
- Supporting the wider finance team with ad hoc accounting and reporting duties

THE PERSON:

- Current experience within an Assistant Management Accountant, Management Accountant, Assistant Accountant or similar role
- Strong experience preparing or supporting the production of monthly management accounts
- Confident with month-end journals, accruals, prepayments and balance sheet reconciliations
- Experience using Xero is essential
- Strong Microsoft Excel skills, including financial reporting and analysis
- Experience with purchase ledger and sales ledger processes, with a willingness to support transactional finance duties
- AAT qualified, ACCA/CIMA part-qualified or Qualified by Experience would be advantageous
- Strong analytical skills with excellent attention to detail
- A proactive and hands-on individual who enjoys working within a small finance team

title: Lecturer in Environmental health and/or Public Health
description:
If you have a record of achievement that demonstrates the commitment, aptitude and enthusiasm to contribute to our global learning community through excellent teaching, scholarship, research and innovation, along with a shared passion for our values and vision, we look forward to receiving your application. We are particularly keen to hear from, and to support, applicants who will help develop our research standing and who will enhance the diversity of our university, our community and our partnerships.

Principal Duties And Responsibilities

The postholder will help develop students’ understanding of a range of subject areas related to environmental and public health. The post holder will demonstrate a firm commitment to all aspects of learning and teaching, especially being able to support students to develop their skills and confidence from undergraduate to postgraduate levels. The postholder will adopt a range of teaching and learning strategies to enhance students understanding of the topic and develop their digital literacy, through the use of blended learning. The post holder will be required to deliver teaching on modules within the BSc (Hons) Environmental Health programmes, MSc Applied Public Health, and contribute to the development of apprenticeship programmes.

The postholder will work closely with members of the environmental and public health team and contribute to teaching across the portfolio, and to develop and support their own research profile within the School of Sport and Health Science. The postholder will have a flexible approach and be interested in supporting students throughout their academic studies.

What we are looking for

- An in-depth knowledge of specialist subject and professional area.
- An in-depth understanding of pedagogy.
- An in-depth understanding of research/enterprise and scholarly activity.
- Ability to design, develop and deliver a range of programmes at various levels.
- Ability to review programme design on a regular basis to ensure compliance with quality standards and academic regulations and to make alterations where appropriate.
- Ability to contribute to the achievement of the School Development Plan and the institutions strategic planning processes.
- Ability to develop research objectives, prepare proposals, carry out independent research, referee and contribute to peer assessment.
- Ability to identify opportunities for strategic development/improvement e.g. research projects, new courses, consultancy.
- Ability to identify (through the analysis of appropriate management information) areas requiring improved performance e.g. student numbers, student satisfaction.
- Experience of HE teaching or equivalent.
- Experience of providing academic leadership and first line support/mentoring for other colleagues.
- Experience of engaging in pedagogic and practitioner research.
- A good honours degree and a Master’s degree in Public Health / Environmental Health / Sustainability or in a closely relevant discipline area.
- Ability to achieve Fellow Status as part of the Higher Education Academy’s Professional Recognition scheme, within agreed timescales (as soon as is practicably possible and definitely within three years of commencement of employment).

You will be an enthusiastic and friendly professional with excellent communication and interpersonal skills coupled with a commitment to providing an excellent student experience. An established or promising profile and very good teaching experience on relevant programmes is essential.

An established or promising profile in the field of Environmental Health and/or Public Health and very good teaching experience on relevant programmes is essential. To be successful you will further enrich our students’ experience through your expertise and subject knowledge as evidenced through your qualifications and experience.

Contact us

If you would like to talk with us about this opportunity please contact Declan Connaughton (Applied Psychology Lead), at DConnaughton@cardiffmet.ac.uk.

All applications must be submitted online.

The person specification will be used as a tool for shortlisting; so please make sure you use this information when writing your application. You can find useful hints and tips about how to apply by visiting our Application Guidance page.
