title: Southwest Early Years Apprenticeship Tutor
description:
We at Best Practice Network share the belief that every child, regardless of their background, should benefit from an excellent education. To achieve that, we support and train the educational professionals who work alongside them to be the best they can be, so in turn, they can transform the lives of children and young people.

We're a friendly, DfE accredited, Ofsted outstanding training company providing apprenticeships, professional development and the DfE's 'Golden Thread' (trainee teachers to school Executive Leaders). We are adaptable, collaborative, and genuinely value the work we do to support the education sector, as much as our trainees do.

Our people are at the heart of our business and our passion and commitment to education is what drives us. As a result, we have seen incredible growth over the last few years both nationally and internationally.

We aim to be an employer where everyone can be themselves, do their best in an inclusive working environment and where all colleagues can thrive and reach their full potential. We want to attract, develop and retain individuals with different experiences, backgrounds and perspectives.
About the Role:
This post will holistically plan, and support from interview stage through to completion of the programme. You will be providing high quality training and assessment for trainees based in the early years education sector. Your knowledge and experience will be shared with trainees to ensure they achieve Early Years Teacher Status (EYTS).

Job Responsibilities
Assessment:

- Complete termly skills reviews with trainees and identify skills and knowledge gaps against the EYITT curriculum themes
- Complete visits in accordance with the programme requirements completing observations in workplace and placement settings, liaising with mentors and lead trainers
- Maintain records relevant to individual trainees
- Support the delivery of high-quality curriculum mastery to meet the Teacher Standards (Early Years), as appropriate to the trainees' requirements
- Assess and feedback to learners using the portfolio system (Mosaic)
Training:

- Develop individual action plans tailored to trainees needs
- Support the delivery of training using approved training resources to cover curriculum themes
- Provide tutorial support including key training for the trainees (and employer around Prevent and British values), personal development, behaviour, and welfare, safeguarding and any additional learning support requirements
Coordination and Support:

- Monitor trainees progress and provide support in completion of evidence and uploading on to Mosaic. Ensuring other evidence is completed in a timely manner, setting targets to ensure timely completion
- Detailing, monitoring, recording and reporting of ALS
- Supply information to employees and employers to support ITT programmes
- Liaise with Line Manager's to facilitate reviews and appraisals
- Provide appropriate data and information regarding the programme and trainees as required and contribute to the regular self-evaluation monitoring process
- Review the teaching file and learning sequences on each visit, and provide feedback on work submitted
- Provide mental health and wellbeing support to trainees
- Ensure that any necessary placements are arranged and attended, giving suggestions for schools/settings if required. The Best Practice Network placement co-ordinator can also advise
Administration:

- Complete all relevant documentation in order to progress the signing up and recording of new trainees on the programme
- Maintain documentation that records the progress of trainees on programme against specified targets
- Complete documentation in relation to visits to employers, trainees reviews, assessment visits and any other such appointments that evidence, support and maintain relationships with trainees and employers
- Ensure timely achievement of all trainees on programme and complete all other required documentation
- Makes the recommendation about the award of Early Years Teacher Status and grading in June
Other

- Any other duties connected with the post as are reasonably required from time to time
- Ensure own CPD is kept up to date, and attend CPD and Standardisation events, as appropriate, delivered by BPN. Termly updates must be sent to the Programme Manager
- Participate in all BPN quality assurance and act promptly on all feedback
- Support Ofsted preparation and visits
- Interview potential candidates and ensuring timely completion of paperwork to strict deadlines
- Present EYITT briefings to potential applicants to boost recruitment within your locality
- Support and promote equality and diversity at Best Practice Network to ensure equality of opportunity for all trainees, visitors and staff and the elimination of discriminatory practices
- Support and promote the safeguarding agenda at Best Practice Network to ensure trainees, visitors and staff are safeguarded
The success of Best Practice Network rests on a very strongly felt and shared set of values which determine its strategic direction. It is crucial that the successful candidate shares our values of student-centredness, equality of opportunity and parity of esteem for staff and students.

At Best Practice Network we are:

- Passionate and excited about learning
- Inclusive and supportive
- Responsive to student, employer and community needs
- Always aspiring to the highest standards
- Professional and enterprising
- Innovative and creative
- Friendly and welcoming
The following criteria are used to shortlist applicants and assess candidates. Please show evidence of how you meet these criteria in your application.

Essential Criteria

- Hold a qualification or have experience in the subject area
- Have up to date industry knowledge
- Hold Level 2 Numeracy and Literacy qualifications
- Have experience of working with employers in a training or customer relations role
- Able to develop strong professional relationships with employers and learners
- Have strong IT skills and be willing to work with e-portfolio's
- Can motivate learners and ensure they complete on time
- Hold a full driving licence, have own vehicle and be willing to travel to customer sites
- Have high levels of motivation and the ability to use own initiative
Desirable Criteria

- Hold an assessor qualification
- Hold a relevant degree
- Hold an IV/IQA qualification
- Experience of working in Further Education or a similar environment
- Early Years Advanced Practitioner or Management experience
Our Benefits:

- 28 days holiday and get an extra day for each year you stay with us, up to max 33 days PLUS bank holidays
- Health Cash Plan, once you've passed probation, which includes access to a private GP
- From day 1, free life insurance covering up to x4 your salary
- We'll both add money into your pension pot after 3 months
- Choose what flexible benefits you want after you've passed probation - this could be buying extra holiday, dental, topping up your healthcare plan, bikes, gym membership, electric cars and give as you earn
- Learning and development opportunities
- Volunteer days - 3 paid volunteer days a year, with 2 dedicated to Education
By joining us, you will become part of a community that is dedicated to transforming lives and sustaining communities, where your voice is heard, your ideas are valued, and your individuality is celebrated. Together, we will continue to advance our passion for education and build brighter futures for all.

Employment offers are subject to satisfactory vetting checks. These checks will be run in line with the latest guidance and legislation. You will need to already have the right to work in the UK, as we are not able to offer any sponsorship(s) for visa applicants.

This role also requires criminal records checks in line with the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974 and safeguarding legislation. For roles in England, Wales, or Northern Ireland, this is a DBS check or PVG Scheme in Scotland. The level of check required will determine what you need to disclose.

title: Assistant Management Accountant
description:
Job Summary:

The Assistant Management Accountant will support the delivery of accurate financial reporting,
balance sheet control, budgeting, forecasting, and working capital analysis across MSS Entities - MSS
UK, MSS USA & MSS France. This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced accounts or a part
qualified person to join a busy finance team and working closely with Accounts Payable, Accounts
Receivable and Operations.

The successful candidate will support the production of monthly management accounts, preparation
of monthly balance sheet reconciliations, assist with key reporting processes, reconcile and post bank
reconciliations, and help identify opportunities to improve efficiency across the business. They will
also be flexible and willing to support other areas of the accounts function when required.
The Assistant Management Accountant will work closely with the Finance Business Partners, Finance
Operations team, external advisors, and operational stakeholders to ensure accurate financial
information and strong financial control.

Key Responsibilities:

Tariff Management
• Calculate monthly tariff recharges due to customers and ensure invoices are raised accurately
and on time

Management Accounts and Reporting
• Support the preparation of monthly management accounts, including Profit & Loss, Balance
Sheet, and Cash Flow reporting.
• Assist in ensuring financial reporting is completed in accordance with the monthly reporting
timetable.
• Analyse overhead expenditure and identify potential risks and opportunities through
engagement with operational stakeholders.
• Support the preparation of reports and analysis for management review.
• Assist with the preparation of management information submitted to Group Finance.

Financial Accounting and Control
• Prepare accurate balance sheet reconciliations and supporting schedules.
• Assist the Finance Business Partner with monthly balance sheet reviews.
• Investigate and resolve reconciliation differences and control account issues.
• Ensure the accuracy and integrity of financial records and management information.
• Support month-end and year-end accounting processes.
• Maintain compliance with Group accounting policies and financial controls.

Working Capital and Cash Management
• Perform working capital analysis, identifying risks and opportunities relating to inventory,
debtors, and creditors.
• Support cash flow forecasting through the provision of accurate financial information.
• Assist in monitoring aged debtors, inventory levels, and other key working capital metrics.
• Provide analysis and recommendations to improve cash conversion and working capital
performance.

Budgeting and Forecasting
• Support the annual budgeting process by preparing financial analysis and reporting.
• Assist with the preparation of quarterly forecasts and reforecasts.
• Support variance analysis against budget and forecast targets.
• Contribute to the development of financial plans that support business objectives.

Statutory Reporting
• Completing VAT & Intrastat returns
• Completing US Sales Tax Returns
• Assist with Statutory Reporting for UK, France, and USA

Qualifications, Skills & Experience:

Essential
• Part-qualified CIMA, ACCA or ACA or an experienced accountant
• 2-5 years’ experience in an accounting or finance role
• Strong understanding of double-entry bookkeeping and accounting principles.
• Strong Microsoft Excel skills.
• Strong analytical and numerical skills.
• Excellent attention to detail and accuracy.
• Strong organisational and time management skills.
• Ability to work to strict reporting deadlines.
• Strong written and verbal communication skills.
• Can work independently, use initiative, and manage their own workload.

Desirable
• Experience within a distribution, manufacturing, or supply chain environment.
• Experience using Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central.
• Experience using Power BI.
• Experience supporting budgeting and forecasting processes.
• Exposure to international accounting, tax, or customs environments.

Key Competencies

• Attention to Detail
Maintains a high level of accuracy across financial reporting, reconciliations, tariff accounting,
and data analysis.

• Problem Solving
Investigates issues thoroughly and develops practical solutions to maintain financial accuracy
and control.

• Communication
Communicates effectively with finance and non-finance colleagues, external advisors, and
operational stakeholders.

• Teamwork
Collaborates effectively across the Distribution Finance team and wider business functions

title: Senior Reporting Accountant

Reporting into the Head of External Reporting, you'll play a key role in the preparation of the Group Annual Report and Accounts, Half Year Results and statutory accounts, ensuring compliance with IFRS, UK GAAP and regulatory reporting requirements.

You’ll play a key role in providing technical accounting expertise across a range of complex business activities and lead accounting analysis for significant transactions, preparing clear and insightful papers for senior stakeholders and the Audit Committee.

Working closely with external auditors, you'll support the year-end and interim audit processes, helping to resolve queries efficiently and ensuring successful audit outcomes.

You'll also be responsible for ensuring all statutory and regulatory filings are delivered accurately and on time, while keeping abreast of changes in accounting standards and implementing new requirements across the business. This is an excellent opportunity to apply your technical expertise in a complex, listed organisation while working with stakeholders across the UK and North America.

title: Senior Graphics Programmer
description:
As a Senior Graphics Programmer in the Manchester Studio, you would be pushing forwards the rendering technology that powers a huge sandbox universe, spanning every conceivable scale from shading interstellar gas clouds, planets and asteroid belts, down to rendering individual human hairs.

You will also advance the core rendering technology that aspires to achieve photo-real visuals, such as physically based light, eye and lens simulations, as well as more low-level engine technologies such as shader building & compilation, content streaming systems, and the multi-threaded and cross-API renderer architecture.

All of this will be achieved using the latest PC hardware, technology and APIs to produce a fast and scale-able suite of visual technology to power some of the most ambitious games ever developed.

Founded in 2012, Cloud Imperium Games creates cutting-edge videogames that defy expectations. We're currently developing Star Citizen, a record-breaking multiplayer online space sim, and Squadron 42, a cinematic single-player adventure set in the same universe. Join us as we break boundaries and make videogame history.

For more information about life at Cloud Imperium Games, check this out - https://youtu.be/rH59z29Odfo

What does a Senior Graphic Programmer at Cloud Imperium Games do?
In short, on daily basis you will:

- Drive research and implementation of new cutting-edge graphics technology and tools.
- Analyse, refactor and improve upon existing graphics technology.
- Assist and advise other software developers in use of graphics/rendering features, while debugging and fixing problems.
- Profile and optimise the entire rendering pipeline, including lighting and shading components of the game.
- Keep up to date with latest graphics and rendering techniques and tools, helping us to innovate, plan, and deliver full features.

What do we expect from our Senior Graphic Programmers?

- Comfortable working with C++ in a large shared codebase, including testing, code-reviews, source-control as well as experience with a common shader language and modern graphics API.
- Good knowledge 3D rendering, 3D math, and optimization of the complete rendering pipeline.
- Strong software debugging skills to effectively track, diagnose and solve a variety of complex issues.
- Work well in a cooperative, cross-functional team environment; ability to translate technical jargon to non-technical audiences.

At Cloud Imperium Games we are looking for several Graphic Programmers with various levels of experience - from junior all the way to senior, and beyond! Therefore, if our Graphics team sounds like your perfect fit, please apply immediately!

title: Technical Trainer / Certified Instructor (VCI) – VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF)
description:
Job Description:

Position Summary & Purpose:

We are seeking an experienced VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) Technical Trainer to deliver enterprise-level Instructor-Led Training (ILT) and Virtual Instructor-Led Training (vILT).

This is a core instruction role designed for a hands-on technical facilitator who can step directly into the classroom as a Lead Instructor with minimal ramp-up time. While the primary mission is active classroom teaching (:70% estimated delivery focus), the instructor will also lend non-delivery bandwidth to partner with the Business Unit (BU) on curriculum review and content feedback.

Note on Role Scope: This is a customer-facing, delivery-first instructor position. Candidates coming from a dedicated curriculum design background should note that live teaching and lab facilitation form the primary core of this role.

Key Responsibilities

- Live Technical Instruction & Facilitation (Primary Role): Serve as a Lead Instructor delivering high-touch ILT and vILT sessions to enterprise customer teams, engineers, and administrators. Facilitate complex hands-on lab exercises, run live technical demonstrations, and navigate unscripted, deep-dive Q&A with authority. Troubleshoot live lab environments and technical edge cases during active training delivery.
- BU Collaboration & Curriculum Support: Lend subject matter expertise to the Business Unit (BU) during non-teaching windows to assist with courseware development, lab topology review, and student guide updates. Channel real-world classroom feedback and student insights directly back to the BU to keep training aligned with field needs. Help establish delivery best practices and assist in onboarding guest or peer instructors.
- Onsite Delivery: Travel to customer sites or corporate events for onsite classroom training as required.

Core Technical Domain Requirements

- VCF Platform Architecture: Multi-domain architecture, deployment, full-stack lifecycle management, and Day-2 operational strategies.
- Compute & Virtualization: vSphere, ESXi host tuning, vCenter Server, cluster management, high availability (HA), DRS, and workload lifecycle operations.
- SDDC Management & Domains: VCF management domains, workload domains, SDDC Manager / VCF management services, and upgrades.
- Software-Defined Networking & Security: VMware NSX ecosystem, including virtual routing and switching, micro-segmentation, and security concepts.
- Software-Defined Storage: VMware vSAN architecture, storage policy-based management (SPBM), resilience, and operations.
- Operations & Automation: Infrastructure monitoring, performance management, log analytics, and capacity management. Self-service automation concepts, governance frameworks, and API integrations.
- Cloud-Native Concepts: Modern Kubernetes concepts on VCF, including Supervisor services and Tanzu / VCF Kubernetes Services (VKS).
- Enterprise Infrastructure: DNS, NTP, certificates/PKI, identity, security, and high availability.

Qualifications & Credentials

- Certifications: Current VCI (VMware Certified Instructor) status strongly preferred. Active VCP or higher advanced VMware credential preferred/required.
- Professional Experience: Hands-on experience operating, implementing, or engineering VCF environments. Background as a VCI, authorized technical instructor, Systems Engineer, Solutions Architect, or Technical Lead.
- Customer Presentation Skills: Proven track record presenting complex platform architectures to sophisticated enterprise engineering teams.

Experience/Education:

Bachelor's degree preferred. Relevant year's experience in lieu of a degree may be considered.

12+ years related experience required

description:
Job title: Manager - CCDI (Centre for Cyber Defence & Intelligence)

Division: Operations

Department: Cyber & Information Resilience (C&IR)

- Your internal recruitment contact is Lauren McHale via Lauren.McHale@fca.org.uk
- Applications must be submitted through our online portal. Applications sent via social media or email will not be accepted.

About The FCA And Team

We regulate financial services firms in the UK, to keep financial markets fair, thriving and effective. By joining us, you’ll play a key part in protecting consumers, driving economic growth and shaping the future of UK finance services.

We are recruiting a Manager to lead the FCA's Threat, Detection & Response function, the Centre for Cyber Defence and Intelligence, part of Cyber & Information Resilience (C&IR) at the FCA. This is an exciting time to join the function as the FCA increases its adoption of AI and agent-based technologies. These developments create opportunities to modernise cyber defence, while also requiring a significant uplift in security monitoring, telemetry, detection engineering and response capabilities to manage new and evolving risks.

The FCA regulates over 35,000 financial services firms in the UK, setting standards for firms to meet and holding them to account if they do not. We enable a fair and thriving financial services market for the good of consumers and the UK economy. The CCDI Manager will operate and mature an intelligence-led cyber defence capability, translating current threat intelligence into monitoring priorities, detection improvements, exposure insight and measurable improvement in incident response. The role links Threat Intelligence, Security Operations, Detection Engineering, Cyber Assurance and Technology teams, including outsourced partners and maintains a data-driven view of detection effectiveness, response performance, service outcomes and coverage gaps.

Role Responsibilities

- Lead and develop the FCA's Threat Intelligence, Detection and Incident Response capability, delivering an intelligence-led approach to cyber defence and risk reduction
- Drive continuous improvement of detection coverage, telemetry, response effectiveness and security operations through data-led insights, automation and effective stakeholder engagement.
- Shape the security monitoring response to increased adoption of AI and agent-based technologies, ensuring that telemetry, detection logic and response capabilities evolve alongside the FCA’s technology environment.
- Own the detection improvement roadmap, working closely with SOC providers, technology teams and cyber security stakeholders to deliver measurable outcomes
- Lead and develop internal teams and third-party partners, ensuring effective performance, service quality and continuous professional growth
- Establish meaningful cyber security metrics, KPIs and executive reporting to measure performance, resilience and risk reduction
- Build trusted relationships across the FCA and external cyber security communities to improve threat awareness, influence priorities and share best practice
- Ensure alignment with industry frameworks and guidance, including NIST CSF, MITRE ATT&CK, MITRE D3FEND, INFORM and NCSC standards

Minimum

Skills required

- Experience leading Cyber Security, Security Operations, Threat Intelligence or Detection Engineering teams, including developing people and delivering results through others
- Solid knowledge of modern cyber threats, detection, threat intelligence and incident response, with experience managing cyber security partners and service providers
- Effective stakeholder management and communication skills, with the ability to translate complex technical risks, security metrics and data into clear executive insights and recommendations
- Advanced analytical and problem-solving skills, using data-driven approaches to improve security outcomes, operational effectiveness and cyber resilience

Essential

- Experience in one or more of Threat Intelligence, Security Operations, Detection Engineering, SOC Performance Management or Exposure Management, with a practical understanding of threat-informed defence methodologies, security monitoring, incident response and frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK for adversary behaviour, D3FEND for defensive countermeasures, and INFORM for measuring defensive maturity.
- Experience using security performance metrics, KPIs, KRIs, cyber maturity measures and operational reporting to support informed decision-making, continuous improvement and measurable cyber risk reduction
- Experience delivering improvements to detection coverage, signal quality, response effectiveness and cyber resilience, including the use of automation, SOAR, telemetry enrichment, attack simulation or purple teaming approaches
- Solid knowledge of cyber security controls across cloud, SaaS and enterprise environments, with experience using technologies such as Microsoft Defender, Microsoft Sentinel, CrowdStrike, AWS Security Services or similar security platforms
- Demonstrated ability to influence senior stakeholders, communicate complex technical concepts to a range of audiences and produce high-quality governance papers and executive reporting
- Knowledge of operational resilience, cloud security and regulatory expectations within complex or highly regulated environments
- Relevant cyber security certifications such as CISSP, CISM, GIAC, SANS, Azure Security, AWS Security or equivalent are advantageous

Benefits

- 28 days annual leave plus bank holidays
- Non-contributory pension (8–12% depending on age) and life assurance at eight times your salary
- Private healthcare with Bupa, income protection and 24/7 Employee Assistance
- 35 hours of paid volunteering annually
- Colleagues spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office each month (60% for Directors and Executive Directors) across our London, Leeds and Edinburgh offices. A flexible benefits scheme designed around your lifestyle

For a full list of our benefits and our recruitment process as a whole visit our benefits page.

Our values and culture

Our colleagues are the key to our success as a regulator. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive culture: one that’s free from discrimination and bias, celebrates difference and supports colleagues to deliver at their best. We believe that our differences and similarities enable us to be a better organisation – one that makes better decisions, drives innovation and delivers better regulation.

title: Experienced Mechanical Design Engineer
description:
Job Description

Our Honeywell Hymatic business in Redditch operates at the forefront of cryogenic sensor cooling, using Joule Thompson, high pressure gas stored energy and Stirling cycle technologies. For over 50 years this business has been the acknowledged world leader with applications in the industrial, aerospace and defence, and space environments. Today as part of Honeywell Aerospace, a global leader, the company is well placed to strengthen its position in the defence and infra-red technology sector, and capitalise on the growing homeland security systems market. The dedicated cryogenic site in Redditch employs approx 90+ people with an annual trevenue of ~£22m and ambitious 10% year on year growth plans, and is looking for a talented Design Engineer to support these plans.

Join a company that's reintroducing itself to the aviation community we've helped advance for more than a century. At Honeywell Aerospace (NASDAQ: HONA), we're launching as an independent, publicly traded aerospace and defense company built on a legacy of operational excellence and mission-focused execution.

Our new brand identity pairs that heritage with real momentum, as we build technology that helps pilots navigate with confidence, aircraft operate more efficiently, and operators stay ahead of change. With our systems on board 90% of the world's aircraft, your work here has reach that's rare to find anywhere else.

Focusing on our customers, investing in innovation, and building a culture of accountability and performance is how we're shaping what comes next.

Every horizon. Every mission. Every day.

Role Overview

Part of a small design group within an Engineering department of 18 (and growing), this design role will require a unique individual with a well rounded design capability. The appointed individual will need to be able to develop concept designs including supporting analysis, with a keen awareness of manufacturing methodologies and a mind on cost. Additionally, the role will also require detail design work and processing of engineering changes. Working as part of the design team, the Design Engineer has the overall responsibility for the concept and detailed design of new products and assembly tooling, together with all drawings and associated project documentation. The Design Engineer will also undertake wider ranging project engineering responsibilities when appropriate/ required.

Key Responsibilities

- Produce detailed design/layouts to meet customer requirement and specification.
- Support detailed estimates at the request of project leaders as a contribution to product development proposals.
- Ensure that ‘Design for Six Sigma’ principles are observed throughout all phases of the design process and apply data rational analysis to arrive at robust solutions
- Check design feasibility by performing design, stress and performance calculations using 3D CAD, finite element and traditional analysis methods.
- Work in accordance with procedures and design standards and to contribute to developing best working practices.
- Be responsible for the completion and checking of drawing packs and any other supporting documentation. This will involve prototype and production details and assembly drawings and associated tolerance analyses.
- Act as project leader when appropriate.
- To liaise with production engineering and production planning in order to achieve a design/detail package best suited to production and to be aware of changes in manufacturing technology.
- Support engineering change requests and process deviation/waivers where necessary.
- Be responsible for the accuracy and completeness of all database entries specific to current project.
- Be committed to delivering against project schedules and meeting project milestones whilst working within a multi project team environment.

Honeywell Hymatic currently uses Siemens NX 2212 and TeamCenter 13.2. Designs are created in accordance with ASME Y14.1.

Key Requirements

- Change oriented and able to develop innovative solutions in a fluid team environment

title: Graduate Electrical Engineer (13630)
description:
Graduate Electrical Engineer

At Tilbury Douglas, you won’t just be starting your career – you’ll be helping to deliver projects that make a real difference to people and communities.

As a Graduate Electrical Engineer within our Engineering division, you’ll gain hands-on experience from day one, working alongside experienced engineers, designers and project teams. You’ll support the development, coordination and delivery of electrical engineering solutions across a range of projects, helping to make them safer, more efficient, sustainable and buildable. Tilbury Douglas Engineering is recognised as one of the UK’s leading mechanical, electrical and plumbing (M&E) engineering contractors, delivering solutions that enable complex estates and facilities to operate safely, efficiently and sustainably.

You’ll develop your technical knowledge and practical engineering skills while seeing how electrical systems are designed, coordinated, installed and brought into operation.

This is a site-based role, with your initial project expected to be based in Birmingham. As you develop, you’ll have opportunities to gain experience across a variety of projects, clients and locations within the wider West Midlands, helping you build broad technical experience and a strong foundation for your electrical engineering career.

You’ll learn from experienced professionals, take on real responsibility and see first-hand how engineering design becomes project delivery – building strong foundations for your future career with Tilbury Douglas.

What You’ll Be Doing

As a Graduate Electrical Engineer, you’ll develop your skills across key areas of engineering and project delivery, gaining the experience you need to progress towards professional accreditation.

No two days are the same and, with the support of experienced colleagues, you’ll:

- Support the development and coordination of electrical engineering solutions across our projects.
- Assist with the review and development of electrical designs, drawings, specifications and technical information.
- Develop your understanding of electrical systems, equipment and installations, and how they integrate with other engineering disciplines.
- Undertake engineering calculations and technical assessments with support from experienced engineers.
- Work collaboratively with civil, structural, mechanical and other engineering disciplines to develop coordinated solutions.
- Support design reviews and help identify opportunities to improve buildability, efficiency, safety and project outcomes.
- Work with project and construction teams to ensure engineering solutions are effectively translated from design into delivery.
- Assist with resolving technical queries and engineering challenges throughout the project lifecycle.
- Liaise with designers, consultants, suppliers and specialist subcontractors to support effective engineering solutions.
- Support inspections, testing and commissioning activities, where required, to help ensure electrical systems perform as intended.
- Assist with the preparation and maintenance of technical documentation, engineering records and project information.
- Develop your understanding of relevant electrical engineering standards, regulations and industry best practice.
- Gain experience in digital engineering, sustainability, energy efficiency and emerging technologies.
- Build strong working relationships with colleagues, clients, consultants and supply chain partners.

Why this role?

This isn’t just about electrical systems, drawings and calculations – it’s about developing engineering solutions that make projects safer, more efficient, sustainable and buildable.

As part of our Engineering division, you’ll work alongside specialists from different disciplines and see how technical expertise influences projects from design through to construction, commissioning and handover. You’ll gain exposure to real engineering challenges and develop an understanding of how good design decisions improve project outcomes.

With mentoring, structured training and support towards professional accreditation with the Institution of Engineering and Technology (IET) or the Chartered Institution of Building Services Engineers (CIBSE), you’ll develop the technical expertise, problem-solving abilities and people skills to become a trusted engineering professional. You’ll be on a clear pathway towards becoming a Chartered Engineer.

As your knowledge and confidence grow, you’ll take on increasing engineering responsibility and develop a strong foundation for a long-term career within our Engineering division.

What We’re Looking For

We want to hear from people who are passionate about engineering and construction. You’ll bring:

- A degree, or be expected to graduate in 2027, in Electrical Engineering, Electrical and Electronic Engineering or a closely related discipline (2:2 or above).
- A full UK driving licence, or be working towards obtaining one by February 2027.
- A genuine interest in electrical engineering, design and how engineering solutions are developed and delivered.
- Strong organisational and problem-solving skills, with a proactive approach to challenges.
- Good written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work effectively with a range of people.
- A practical mindset, with attention to detail and quality.
- Previous site or construction-related experience is desirable but not essential.

What We Offer

- Start your career with a programme designed to help you learn, develop and succeed from day one.
- A structured two-year Graduate Development Programme, giving you the experience and skills to build a successful career.
- Support towards professional accreditation with IET or CIBSE.
- Mentoring and guidance from experienced engineering professionals.
- A competitive salary and benefits package, including car allowance, Performance Related Pay and up to 8% matched pension contributions.
- 26 days’ annual leave plus bank holidays, with the flexibility to buy or sell additional days.
- Private medical insurance, 24/7 wellbeing support and a wide range of flexible benefits and employee discounts.
- Two volunteering days each year, giving you time to make a difference in the community.

Selection Process Timeline

- Video Interview – Shortlisted candidates will be invited to complete a video interview. Invitations will be sent between 16 November and 1 December 2026, and candidates will have one week to complete and submit their interview.
- Interview – Successful candidates will progress to a formal interview, taking place between 11 and 27 January 2027.
- Offer – Successful candidates will receive an offer by the week ending 12 February 2027.

Who We Are

Tilbury Douglas is a leading UK building, infrastructure, engineering and fit-out company, delivering vital projects across a diverse range of sectors, including healthcare, education, highways, justice, defence, aviation, water and the environment.

People are at the heart of our success. We are committed to creating an inclusive culture where everyone is valued, supported and empowered to make a difference. Our values guide everything we do:Everyone has a voice, Do the right thing, Take pride in what you do, and Bring better to life.

Why Tilbury Douglas?

Tilbury Douglas offers the opportunity to work on meaningful, real-world projects while developing within a supportive and inclusive environment. The company places a strong emphasis oncareer development, innovation, wellbeing and practical learning, demonstrated by its Platinum membership of the 5% Club and recognition of Early Careers employees through national industry awards.

Start your career where it matters – building a better future together.

title: Delivery Driver
description:

Delivery Driver's play a crucial part of the team within GSF Car Parts. They are the face of our brand by delivering parts to customers and continuously providing excellent customer service. - Ensure high levels of customer service at all times

41 (average) hours Monday to Friday, including alternate Saturday working

About You

- Must hold a full UK Driving Licence with a maximum of 6 points
- Must have a minimum of 3 years driving experience
- Excellent knowledge of 40 mile radius of branch
- Previous experience within a delivery driver role
- Ability to understand necessity of excellent standards of customer service
- Work to deadlines with good time keeping skills
- Customer focused, driven to achieve and willing to go the extra mile

What We'll Offer

Benefits at GSF Car Parts are designed to support all aspects of our team members life throughout their career. Whether that’s their health, wealth or everyday lifestyle, we are here for our team members and their loved ones and there is something for everyone! To name a few of our benefits we offer:

- 28 days annual leave (including bank holidays) plus the opportunity to earn up to 5 more with time-served
- Free flu vaccine
- Health & wellbeing tools
- Free support from pension experts
- Life assurance scheme
- Discounts from 100’s of household names including Asda, Nike & John Lewis
- A suite of financial wellbeing products including advances and savings schemes
- Paid time off to volunteer
- Training qualifications and career progression opportunities

At GSF Car Parts, we're not just supplying car parts, we're driving the future of the automotive aftermarket.

As the UK's fastest-growing motor factor, we've achieved more than 25% year-on-year growth for three consecutive years and continue to expand at an unrivalled pace. With over 215 branches nationwide and a state-of-the-art 500,000 sq ft National Distribution Centre, we're building a business that keeps thousands of workshops moving every day.

But what really sets us apart is our people.

We're a business that invests boldly, embraces innovation and empowers our teams to make a real difference. From industry-leading digital tools like Mastercat to our nationwide Servicesure garage network and partnerships with over 70 OE-quality brands, we're constantly challenging the status quo and finding better ways to serve our customers.

We're ambitious about where we're going and equally ambitious for the people who join us. Whether you're looking to develop your skills, progress your career or help shape the future of our industry, we'd love to hear from you.

This is an exciting time to join GSF Car Parts.

Make an impact. Grow with us. Do yourself proud!

title: Customer Service Advisor
description:
Please note this role is required to work between Birmingham & Wolverhampton Branches
If you enjoy connecting with people and making a difference, a career in Customer Service within our Branch Network could be a fantastic opportunity for you. As one of the largest and most impactful teams at YBS, our Branch Network plays a vital role in shaping the success of our organisation. We’re always looking for ways to enhance the customer experience, improve efficiency, and explore new ideas. And as we embark on an exciting digital transformation, the future is full of possibilities—for us and for you.

About the Role

As a Customer Service Advisor, you’ll:

- Build meaningful relationships with our members and help them find the right products and services to support their goals—whether that’s saving for a special trip, buying a first home, or planning for the future.
- Communicate confidently across multiple channels, including in-branch, over the phone, and online, to support members with their accounts.
- Focus on doing what’s right for our members—without the pressure of sales targets.

Each YBS branch has its own unique character and strengths, making every location a special place to work. Here’s what the hiring manager says about our Birmingham.

The Birmingham branch of YBS is situated right in the centre of the city. It benefits from fantastic transport links via the Metro tram, train stations and busses as well as local access to the A38 leading to the major motorway network, meaning this is a fantastic opportunity for commuters and locals alike. The Birmingham branch of YBS is situated in New Street, close to New Street Train Station in the heart of this vibrant City. The Branch is a Dual location shared with Wolverhampton where the successful candidate will be required to work between both locations.

Wolverhampton is a smaller City, also with direct Train, Tram & bus links to & from Birmingham. The Wolverhampton Branch is in Queen Square in the heart of the City, a short walk from the train/tram and main bus station. Both branches are extremely popular with our members and within easy commuting distance of each other. As Manager I'm looking to attract someone who has a real passion to excel in providing an exceptional customer service with commitment and flexibility to further enhance our existing successful team and who really cares about their customers, colleagues as well as the organisation they represent. This is also a great opportunity for your own personal development and potential career progression. A perfect way to start your YBS journey.

About You

You don’t need a background in financial services or years of customer service experience. What matters most is your mindset and values. We’re looking for someone who:

- Is motivated to go the extra mile for colleagues and members, contributing to shared goals.
- Thrives in dynamic environments and embraces change with curiosity and positivity.
- Values diversity and understands the importance of different perspectives, experiences, and skills.
- Shows empathy and emotional intelligence, creating a welcoming and supportive atmosphere for everyone.
- Builds strong, respectful relationships with members and teammates.
- Has a growth mindset and is eager to learn through our training and development opportunities.
- Is confident using digital tools and open to learning new technologies.
- Is committed to personal development and staying future-ready.

About Us

At YBS we don’t have shareholders, we have members. We care about people and that includes you. So here, you’ll be respected for who you are, you’ll be able to bring your whole self to work, and you’ll have everything you need to build a long and rewarding career.

Flexibility. We offer a range of flexible working options without unsocial hours, which can help you find a healthy work-life balance. Whether it’s finishing early for an appointment or fitting your studies and hobbies in around your working hours, we can help make it work for you. We’re happy to talk flexible working and you can reach out to us anytime during the recruitment process to discuss this.

Development. We want you to feel challenged here. Whatever your ambitions, we’re committed to helping you develop your skills and move ahead in your career journey. From day one, we’ll set you up for success with a brilliant induction and full training plan, all designed to get you up to speed quickly.

Inclusivity. We’re passionate about creating an inclusive environment where everyone is welcome and able to be themselves. If you’ll go the extra mile to help our members, you’ll fit right in and feel you belong here.

About our Benefits
We offer lots of fantastic rewards that you can make the most of in and out of work, including:

- Holiday. You’ll get 28 days plus Bank Holidays, as well as the option to buy up to a further 5 days.
- Bonus. At YBS we work collaboratively and share in our success together, so when we reach our goals were all rewarded with an on target bonus of 7% of eligible pay (with the opportunity to earn up to a maximum 15%).
- Pension. We know how important it is to save towards the future, that’s why we’ll contribute up 11% into your YBS pension.
- Healthcare. Health and wellbeing are an important part of life at YBS, when you join us you’ll have access to a range of health benefits to suit your life including private medical insurance, dental and healthcare plans.
- My Benefits. When you join YBS you’ll have access to our self-service benefits portal, where you can access a range of retail, hospitality and health discounts
Ready to apply?
Great with people? Then we think it would be great to meet you. Apply now.,

title: Solar PV Electrician - Solar & Battery Installations (Bristol Hub)
description:
£45,000 – £55,000

- company van and fuel card
- full-time
- UK-wide with overnight stays Monday–Thursday when needed

About Spark

The Spark vision is to take the standards of the residential solar industry and redefine them. Founded by a team with 3 decades of experience, our goal is prioritising both products and service and placing the customer at the forefront of our ethos.

We are proud to be MCS-registered, HIES and Which? Approved, and known for setting high standards in workmanship, compliance, and customer care.

We don't offer off-the-shelf solar systems. Instead, we have curated a range of panels, batteries, and inverters for their blend of optimal performance and assured quality. We have chosen products that allow us to ensure that every system Spark installs is excellent as standard, seamlessly blending high-quality solar into a bespoke system that is tailored exclusively to our customers.

As demand for domestic solar continues to surge, we're expanding our renewable operations team and are looking for an experienced Solar PV Electrician to assist the installation of our residential solar projects across the UK. This role is attached to our new Bristol hub.

Key Responsibilities

- Installation and commissioning of solar PV inverters and battery storage systems
- Carrying out service, maintenance, and inspection works on existing systems
- Installation of AC supplies, containment, and cable runs
- Fault finding, testing, and troubleshooting of PV and battery systems
- Ensure all work is carried out in line with industry best practice and system specifications
- Provide technical support to internal teams and back-office staff
- Maintain full compliance with health & safety procedures and risk assessments
- Maintain accurate records of installations, maintenance, and repairs
- Travel across the UK where required, with overnight stays Monday–Thursday when necessary

Requirements

Essential Requirements

- Qualified Electrician (NVQ Level 3 or equivalent)
- 18th Edition (BS 7671)
- Test & Inspection Certificate (2391 or equivalent)
- Valid CSCS or ECS card
- Minimum 2 years' experience in solar PV and/or battery storage systems
- Strong understanding of electrical installations and testing procedures
- Ability to clearly explain technical issues to customers in a professional manner
- Ability to work at heights and outdoors in varying conditions
- Strong computer literacy
- Ability to use technology remotely
- Full UK driving licence
- Willingness to travel

Benefits

- £45,000 – £55,000 per year (dependent on experience)
- 22 days holiday per year + bank holidays (rising to 27 with long service)
- Uniform and PPE provided
- Company van with fuel card for business use
- Food allowance if staying away

Are you an offshore renewables professional, commercial mariner, or veteran with hands-on experience in the offshore wind sector? If you love the industry but are tired of unpredictable shift patterns, long travel times, and being away from home, this is your route to a rewarding, shore-based career.

At South West Maritime Academy, we are looking for a GWO Training Instructor to join our expert team. This role allows you to maintain your connection to the offshore wind sector, utilise your specialised safety knowledge, and enjoy the job security and regular hours of a land-based position.

The Role: What You’ll Be Doing
Working alongside our lead instructional team, you will be responsible for delivering high-impact, life-saving course content to delegates entering or advancing in the offshore renewables sector.

- Deliver Core GWO Modules: Help deliver our comprehensive GWO Basic Safety Training (BST) modules, including Sea Survival, Fire Awareness, First Aid, Manual Handling, Working at Heights and associated refresher courses.
- Bring Real-World Skills to Life: You will use your practical familiarity of safety protocols to give delegates a realistic understanding of what to expect in the field.
- Build Rapport & Share Anecdotes: We pride ourselves on our passionate instructors who build genuine relationships with students. Your personal experience is what brings our curriculum to life and keep delegates returning to us for their refresher updates.
- Maintain the Fleet & Kit: Take a hands-on role in managing our extensive kit stores, ensuring all specialist GWO safety gear, harnesses, PPE, and training rigs are meticulously maintained and "battle-ready" for practical exercises.
- One-Team Culture: We are a small, tight-knit crew. You’ll chip in with the rest of the team to keep our communal training spaces and facilities clean, tidy, and professional.

What We’re Looking For
We are looking for someone with genuine offshore experience who can command a classroom and outdoor training rig with confidence.

- Industry Background: Strong, demonstrable experience working within the wider renewable energy sector. You should have practical, real-world experience performing safety-critical or technical tasks relevant to renewables environments (such as working at height, manual handling, or safety operations). Backgrounds across offshore, onshore or general renewable energy sectors are highly welcome.
- Working at Height Experience & Bonus Tickets: Demonstrable commercial working at height experience is a key advantage. Holding a recognised rope access qualification, such as IRATA (Industrial Rope Access Trade Association) or a similar standard, is highly desirable.
- The "X" Factor: A confident communicator who can naturally build relationships with students and create an engaging, supportive learning atmosphere.
- Physical Fitness: The role involves leading active, hands-on drills, including working at heights and open-water exercises, requiring a good level of physical fitness.

Note: If you already hold GWO Basic Safety Training (BST) certifications and/or a recognised teaching ticket (like AET Level 3), that’s excellent. However, if you have the right general renewables industry experience, background, and attitude, we will fully support you with obtaining your GWO BST certifications and required training.

Why Join Us?

- Work-Life Balance: Transition to regular, predictable hours with a full-time, shore-based contract.
- Stay in Renewables: Remain a vital part of the green energy sector by training the next generation of technicians.
- Professional Growth: Expand your own portfolio. We invest heavily in our team, helping you gain advanced GWO, MCA, and RYA instructional tickets.

About South West Maritime Academy
We are a premier UK provider of specialist commercial maritime and renewable energy training, based at our expansive 10-acre site at Cromhall Quarry.

As the parent company to The Lake, our facility is a vibrant hub where professional safety programmes meet an active outdoor leisure destination for open water swimming, scuba diving, and paddleboarding.

Our global footprint also includes our sister company, Palma Sea School in Mallorca, giving our wider team an unparalleled network of expertise across both the commercial and leisure maritime sectors.

Our USP
Unlike standard, classroom-bound providers, we have the unique, dedicated infrastructure to deliver training in real-world scenarios. From live-fire simulators to our expansive open-water quarry environment, we offer delegates the most realistic, hands-on GWO training available in the South West.

title: Management Accountant
description:
Management Accountant
Lanes Group is a leading nationwide utility services provider with over 4,500 dedicated employees. Our diverse subsidiaries drive our success across various sectors, contributing to a remarkable turnover of over £500 million. We are committed to excellence and innovation, ensuring we provide industry leading services to our clients and stakeholders.

Department
Finance works closely with operational and support teams across the UK, providing financial expertise, governance, reporting, and commercial insight to help the business make informed decisions and achieve its strategic objectives.
The team is responsible for maintaining robust financial controls, managing budgets and forecasts, ensuring compliance with statutory and regulatory requirements, and delivering accurate financial information across the business. Through proactive support and analysis, Finance helps drive performance, accountability, and continuous improvement at every level of the organisation.

The role:
This role delivers accurate monthly management accounts with clear variance insights to support decision‑making. Responsibilities include leading budgeting and forecasting, monitoring KPIs, and driving cost‑control initiatives. Working closely with department heads, you’ll provide actionable financial analysis, maintain financial models and reporting tools, ensure compliance with internal controls, and support year‑end audit and statutory reporting. The role also manages balance sheet reconciliations and provides ad hoc analysis for key business initiatives.

Hours: Monday to Friday – 37.5 Hours per week
Employment Type: Permanent
Location: Leeds, LS12

Accountabilities & Responsibilities:

- Prepare monthly management accounts, including detailed variance analysis and commentary.
- Monitor and report on key performance indicators (KPIs) to support strategic decision-making.
- Lead the finance teams input into budgeting and forecasting processes, ensuring accuracy and alignment with business objectives.
- Drive cost control initiatives and identify opportunities for financial optimization.
- Collaborate with department heads to deliver actionable financial insights and guidance.
- Develop, maintain, and enhance financial models and reporting tools to improve efficiency and accuracy.
- Ensure compliance with internal controls and adherence to financial policies.
- Support year-end audit activities and statutory reporting requirements.
- Perform balance sheet reconciliations to maintain data integrity.
- Provide ad hoc financial analysis to inform and support key business initiatives.

Qualifications & Experience:

- ACA, ACCA, or CIMA qualified.
- Proven experience in a management accounting role.
- Previous audit experience preferable.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
- Proficient in Excel.
- Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.
- Ability to work independently and meet tight deadlines.
- Knowledge of Power BI or other data visualization tools and financial systems (e.g., Microsoft D365, NetSuite) preferred.

Living the Company Values:
By embedding our companies core values and purpose into each role, ensures that every employee, regardless of their role or level, understands how their individual development and contributions align with our purpose of ‘improving today for a better tomorrow’.

Each role and value has an alignment to set proficiency levels and expectations, this role holder is expected to:

- Leading: Acts as a role model, shaping the learning agenda and influencing change.
- Agile: Anticipates learning needs, adjusts quickly to changing operational contexts.
- Nurturing: Supports the development of others through coaching and structured development plans.
- Engaging: Inspires and motivates learners, builds trust and credibility
- Safe & Secure: Ensures all learning is aligned to safety and compliance standards.

Your Contribution to the company:

- Strive to be always positive and constructive
- Adhere to all company policies
- Straight talking about the facts of the situation – open discussions are the best way to find solutions
- Help others through communicating clearly
- Deliver on commitments
- Ensure that any ideas that may enhance the productivity or systems of the company are brought to the attention of Senior Management, or your colleagues
- Deliver our Company Values understanding that by working together in unity we are ‘Stronger Together’

Equality, Diversion & Inclusion
At Lanes Group, we are dedicated to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace where everyone feels valued and empowered. We believe that our differences make us stronger and are committed to providing equal opportunities for all employees. We welcome and encourage applications from individuals of all backgrounds, including those from underrepresented groups. Join us in our commitment to creating a more inclusive and diverse world.

title: Your Career. Your Impact. Our Supply Chain: Explore Opportunities at Coca-Cola Europacific Partners
description:
At Coca-Cola Europacific Partners (CCEP), we’re proud to produce, move, and deliver some of the world’s most iconic drinks — right here in Great Britain. From Coca-Cola to Monster, Fanta to Schweppes, our Manufacturing and Logistics teams are at the heart of our operations, ensuring our products reach millions of consumers every day.

We make 97% of our products locally in GB and sell over six billion beverages annually. Our operations span high-speed production lines, automated warehouses, and dynamic logistics networks — all powered by a team of over 3,600 employees across England, Scotland, and Wales.

Location: Various UK sites

Contract Type: Permanent and Fixed-Term Opportunities

Experience Levels: Career changers, frontline professionals, emerging leaders and experienced Supply Chain professionals

What you become part of:

CCEP has five major manufacturing sites in Great Britain, each playing a vital role in our supply chain:

- Wakefield, West Yorkshire – Europe’s largest soft drinks plant by volume, producing over 210 million cases annually across 12 lines.
- Sidcup, Kent – One of the busiest drinks manufacturing sites in Europe, producing around 50% of the GB SKU portfolio.
- Milton Keynes, Buckinghamshire – A key site supporting national distribution and production.
- Edmonton, North London – Produces over 160 million cases annually across seven lines.
- East Kilbride, Scotland – Serving Scotland and the North, with six production lines.

We also operate depots and offices in locations including Uxbridge, Morpeth, and Nottingham, supporting our national logistics and commercial functions.

Why Joins Us?

At CCEP, our supply chain is the engine that keeps some of the world’s most loved brands moving. From manufacturing to logistics, from planning to engineering, every role plays a vital part in delivering excellence.

We’re committed to increasing the number of women in our supply chain teams and creating an environment where everyone can thrive, grow, and make an impact.

You don’t need previous FMCG or Supply chain experience to build a successful career at Coca Cola Europacific Partners.

For many of our roles, full training is provided, including:

- On-the-job coaching from experienced colleagues

- Safety and technical training to help you succeed in a fast-paced environment
- Ongoing development opportunities to build your skills and confidence

Whether you’ve worked in retail, hospitality, construction, or another industry, your transferable skills: like teamwork, problem-solving, and attention to detail, are highly valued here. We’re proud to offer a supportive environment where people from all walks of life can thrive, grow, and build long-term careers in manufacturing and logistics.

Roles We’re Hiring for:

- Production Operators & Technicians
- Warehouse Coordinators & FLT Operators
- Logistics & Supply Chain Planners.
- Team Leaders & Managers
- Engineering & Maintenance

What we Offer:

At CCEP, we believe in rewarding our people. Our benefits include:

- Competitive salary and performance-based bonus
- Private Medical Insurance, Pension scheme with employer contributions
- 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays
- Employee wellbeing programmes and mental health support
- Access to exclusive discounts and perks through our employee platform

Apply Now:

Be part of a business that’s refreshing the world and making a difference — one bottle, one pallet, one career at a time.

description:
To deliver evidence-based holistic professional mental health care to people within the context of an integrated multi-disciplinary, multi-agency integrated community mental health team.

The post holder is identified as a skilled and creative practitioner with knowledge of working with and supporting people living within their own communities and will be an integral member of the Community Mental Health Team.

Acting within their professional boundaries, the post holder will provide support and intervention for the presenting person through holistic person-centered assessment, clinical consideration, diagnosis, treatment and evaluation of their care within a multi-agency team approach. They will demonstrate safe, clinical decision-making, expert care and support for people within their homes.

The post holder will work collaboratively with the wider multi-disciplinary general practice teams to meet the needs of people within their community.

- To take responsibility for a clinical caseload, providing comprehensive assessment, care and treatment to clients referred to the Community Mental Health Team in accordance with CTP and Mental Health legislation.
- Foster robust working relationships with all partners, in particular Local Authority, Primary Care and 3rd sector agencies.
- Contribute to the continuing improvement and development of community mental health services.

We are looking for highly motivated individual to join our well-established multi- disciplinary CMHT. The main purpose of this role is to deliver evidenced-based, holistic care to individuals suffering with mental health issues.

The post will be based in Maritime Resource Centre with strong links with Local Authority, the inpatient wards within CTM, our GP partners and third sector organisations.

The post holder will need to hold a first level qualification in mental health nursing, possess excellent clinical knowledge and experience of mental health, with reference to relevant legislation such as the Mental Health Measure 2010. Excellent communication, listening and organisational skills are essential along with MDT working, in a challenging and changeable environment.

The post holder will be expected to manage a caseload of patients with mental health issues, subject to CTP and will work under the leadership of a Band 7 Team Leader.

Cwm Taf Morgannwg (CTM) University Health Board, part of NHS Wales, serves a large population across a diverse and beautiful region, steeped in history and heritage. With nearly 13,500 staff, our health board is one of Wales’s largest employers.

Together, we are Team CTM; a workforce dedicated to offering excellent patient care and support to the 450,000 people across our three regions, Bridgend, Merthyr Tydfil, and Rhondda Cynon Taf. We operate three District General hospitals, several community hospitals, primary and community care facilities.

CTM’s location offers the best of South Wales, just 20 minutes from Cardiff’s vibrant city life, the natural beauty of the Brecon Beacons, and the serene coastline at Ogmore. Whether you enjoy lively urban amenities, peaceful countryside, or seaside escapes, our location makes an ideal setting for both work and personal life.

- We work together as one team

CTM employees enjoy benefits including; a leading pension, generous leave, flexible work, career growth, and access to ongoing learning and development.

title: Lecturer in Cyber Security

description:
About This Role

We offer a BSc in Cyber Security and Digital Forensics, an NCSC accredited MSc in Cyber Security, and a provisionally NCSC accredited Integrated degree apprenticeship taught at our partner Gloucester College in Cheltenham.

We have recently benefited from a substantial investment in research capacity by the university, have a community of active PhD students and collaborate closely with Industry and Government.

You will either have a PhD in Cyber Security, Computer Science or a closely related discipline, or else equivalent industry experience. Applications from experienced practitioners would always be welcomed.

Your expertise must be aligned with one or more of the CyBOK KAs, however we are particularly interested in enhancing our expertise within digital forensics.

The primary focus of this role will be teaching, and we will expect you to support teaching on our programmes, although you will be encouraged and supported in your research ambitions.

Where you will be working

UWE Bristol is a campus-based University, with vibrant campus communities that are central to student life.

In this role, you’ll be based at our modern Frenchay Campus where we’ve invested in state-of-the-art facilities designed to help both staff and students succeed.

You’ll spend most of your time on campus, typically 80 percent of your time, with the opportunity to work from home on the remaining days.

Why UWE Bristol?

We are one of the largest providers of Higher Education in the South West with 38,000 students and 4,000 staff from right across the globe. Based in vibrant Bristol , our ambitions are to make a positive difference to our planet, transforming futures through actions and solving real world challenges.

We offer a wide range of employee benefits including progressive pay rates, very generous annual leave and career average pension schemes as well as retail savings, onsite nursery and opportunities for training and personal development.

We also provide a tailored professional programme to support our academic colleagues in delivering the highest in professional teaching standards.

Add your individuality to ours

UWE Bristol recognises the power of a truly diverse university community .

We’re part of a vibrant, multicultural city and welcome talented people from all backgrounds. Diversity is our strength, enhancing creativity, decision‑making, and problem‑solving. Join our supportive community and thrive.

We particularly encourage applications from global majority and female candidates as we are currently under-represented in this area, however all appointments are made strictly on individual merit.

As a Disability Confident employer, we encourage applications from disabled or neurodivergent candidates.

Further information

If you would like to speak to us to find out more about this role, please contact Phil.Legg@uwe.ac.uk

This is a full-time post which is fixed term until 31 st July 2027

This post is available on a job share basis for applicants wishing to work part time

Salary offers are made in line with the University’s salary assessment guidelines, reflecting your relevant skills and experience in parity with colleagues.

Right to Work in the UK

If offered a role, you will need to provide valid documentation confirming your right to work in the UK before employment begins. Guidance on acceptable documents is available via the Home Office Right to Work Checklist .

We may be able to sponsor eligible candidates for this role under the Skilled Worker visa route; however, visa sponsorship eligibility is assessed only at offer stage, being invited to interview does not indicate an offer of sponsorship.

Please review our Skilled Worker Guidance and UK Government website to assess your eligibility. If you do not qualify you may wish to explore other visa options .

Please note that UWE Bristol does not cover any visa or health surcharge costs.

Next Steps

We’d love to hear from you - if this role excites you, please complete our application form as soon as possible and tell us how your skills and experience meet the criteria listed in the Person Specification, using clear and relevant examples wherever possible.

We’ll keep you informed of the outcome by email once shortlisting is complete.

title: Agentic Engineer
description:
A global media and content business is hiring an Software Engineer with strong AI knowledge to build the first dedicated agent platform inside a high-volume, deadline-driven editorial and licensing operation.

Editorial teams across four continents source, clear, produce and distribute content seven days a week to over 1,500 clients, sitting on an archive of roughly one million photographs and 40,000 video clips. A lot of the work keeping that moving is repetitive and judgement-light and currently scales linearly with headcount. This role exists to change that. You'll be the first dedicated hire on the agent platform, building a suite of AI agents that take on those repetitive layers so editorial and commercial teams can focus on the work that actually needs a human. This is a build role, not a research role, and success looks like agents running in production against real workflows, not prototypes.

Role: Agentic Engineer
Location: Hybrid, Birmingham. 2 to 3 days on site

What you'll be doing:

- Design, build and ship production LLM agents against real editorial, rights, archive and commercial workflows, from scoping through to deployment and monitoring
- Build the shared platform underneath the agents including orchestration, tool and API integrations, retrieval, prompt management, evaluation and observability
- Integrate agents with existing systems including the archive, submission portal, clips platform and internal editorial tooling
- Work directly with editorial, research and commercial teams to identify the workflows worth automating and define what 'good enough to trust' looks like for each
- Build evaluation and guardrails so agent output quality is measurable rather than anecdotal, with human review at the right points
- Own cost and latency, keeping model spend proportionate to the work being replaced
- Document and hand over so the platform is not a single-person dependency
- Keep an eye on the tooling landscape and make pragmatic build-versus-buy calls

What you'll need:

- 3+ years commercial software engineering experience with strong TypeScript skills (and ideally a background in PHP)
- Experience with either Claude Code, Cursor or Codex
- Built and shipped at least one LLM-powered feature or agent into production and operated it afterwards (real, used side projects count)
- Practical grasp of the agent toolkit: function and tool calling, RAG, vector databases, structured output, prompt engineering and context management
- Comfortable with at least one agent framework or SDK, with an understanding of why the abstractions exist rather than blind loyalty to a specific one
- Solid API and integration experience, since much of this role is plumbing agents into systems that were not designed for them
- Able to talk to non-technical colleagues about what an agent can and cannot reliably do, and confident enough to push back when a request is a bad fit

This role would suit an engineer who wants genuine greenfield ownership of an agent platform, a varied problem space spanning editorial, rights, archive and commercial, and short feedback loops with the people whose work the agents actually change.

title: Mechanical Engineers

Drawing on more than 55 years' experience in highly regulated sectors subject to strict security and safety requirements, we provide our customers with engineering and project management services, as well as digital services and solutions to optimize the performance of complex infrastructure projects throughout their life cycle. To ensure a viable, efficient, and reliable energy future for all.

Job Description

The Role:

Reporting to the Turbine Island Senior Mechanical Engineer, you will be responsible for various Turbine Island design development activities. The Mechanical Engineer shall work closely with multi-disciplined teams and the supply chain to help deliver the Turbine Island design.

Key Responsibilities:

- Acting as an Intelligent Customer, involved in checking supplier deliverables, including design against requirements.

- Development and checking with support of Senior Engineers of Process Flow Diagrams, Piping and Instrumentation Diagrams, Layout Drawings, Component Sizing Calculations, Component and Equipment Datasheets and Specifications, and other concept or detailed design related documents

- Interface with wider Turbine Island team and stakeholders

- Attend Design Reviews and HAZID/HAZOP studies with multidisciplined teams

- Ensure adherence to the company statutory H&S Policies and rules and compliance with the project and Quality Management System

Qualifications

Your Background:

- Previous experience, in the nuclear sector or other highly regulated industries such as thermal power generation or oil and gas and process sectors. Good experience and background in thermal power systems and equipment such as steam turbines, condensers, feedwater heaters, pumps, and piping systems.
- Preferably with good experience in similar roles with specific emphasis on FEED through to detailed design and EPC delivery.
- Development of procurement specifications and working with equipment suppliers.
- Strong technical background and broad experience in thermal power or similar projects.
- Excellent communication skills and ability to interact with internal and external stake holders.
- Ability to identify and manage critical interfaces on major projects.
- Good knowledge of UK Health and safety regulations, safety systems, HAZOP and engineering substantiation and technical standards.
- Appreciation and application of ASME, European and UK codes and standards.
- Systems Engineering experience or awareness desirable.
Personal Specification/Attributes:

- Results oriented, ability to work independently and proactively as part of a team, good organisation skills, ability to deal with confidential and sensitive nuclear information in a professional manner and in-line with export control obligations.
- Bachelor’s degree or Higher National Diploma in an engineering discipline.
- CEng in a relevant discipline or working towards Professional Registration.
- SC Clearance or capable of achieving it.

Additional Information

Security clearance:

Due to the nature of work to be undertaken applicants will be required to meet certain residency criteria in order to attain a minimum level of UK security clearance if not already security cleared to a minimum SC level.
